commits.message:
fix: correct the post-maven release-type path in the release pipeline

A post-maven rerun (Maven Central already published, run only downstream
artifacts and finalize) hit two bugs:

prepare.sh ran its version/tag/changelog validation before the
docker-only|post-maven early-exit, so a post-maven rerun failed checks
that only apply to the pom bump and tag it never performs. Move the
early-exit above the validation block.

finalize.sh was gated to full,maven-only, so a post-maven run skipped
finalize entirely -- no next-development-version bump, changelog rewrite
or doc updates. Add post-maven to the allowed release types.

fix: make versioned-site terraform run cross-account correctly

The versioned-site release step failed with a 403: terraform's S3 backend
(mockserver-terraform-state) lives in the build account, but versioned-site.sh
assumed the website-account role before terraform init, so the backend was
read with the wrong account's credentials. The release-website role also only
had content-sync + CloudFront-invalidation permissions, not enough to create
the S3 bucket, CloudFront distribution and Route53 records a new versioned
site needs.

- main.tf: both aws providers gain a dynamic assume_role keyed on a new
  website_role_arn variable. The S3 backend now uses the agent's own
  build-account credentials; the provider hops to the website account.
  Empty website_role_arn keeps the local AWS_PROFILE workflow working.
- variables.tf: add website_role_arn (default "").
- cross-account-role.tf: broaden the release-website role policy to manage
  the website S3 buckets, CloudFront, and the mock-server.com Route53 zone;
  read-only on the role itself (no self-escalation).
- versioned-site.sh: run terraform with the agent's credentials and pass the
  website role ARN to the provider via TF_VAR_website_role_arn; the post-apply
  S3 mirror still assumes the website role.

fix: grant the release agent access to the website terraform state

The versioned-site release step runs terraform against the terraform/website
stack, whose state lives in s3://mockserver-terraform-state/website/
terraform.tfstate. The release-queue Buildkite agent's IAM role had no access
to that bucket, so terraform init failed with a 403 refreshing state.

Add an aws_iam_policy granting the release agent s3:GetObject/PutObject/
DeleteObject on the website/ prefix (scoped so it cannot read other stacks'
state) plus s3:ListBucket on the bucket, and attach it to the
buildkite_release_stack module's managed_policy_arns.

fix: raise versioned-site step timeout to 60 minutes

The versioned-site release step timed out at its 15-minute limit. It runs
terraform apply (creating CloudFront distributions) and then mirrors the
full historical docs site (~460 MB, 35k+ S3 objects) into the new
versioned bucket — build #27 got ~44% through the mirror before the
timeout killed it.

Raise the timeout to 60 minutes, consistent with the other heavy steps
(maven-plugin and docker are also 60; maven-central is 180).

fix: confine assume_website_role credentials to a subshell

versioned-site.sh failed at git push ("could not read Username for
https://github.com"). assume_website_role exports website-account
credentials into the shell, so the subsequent git_commit_and_push reads
the GitHub token from a build-account secret via load_secret while those
website-account credentials are active -- the read fails, leaving the
push with no auth header.

Wrap assume_website_role and the aws s3 operations in a subshell in both
versioned-site.sh and helm.sh (helm.sh has the same ordering) so the
exported credentials stay local to the subshell and git_commit_and_push
runs with the agent's own build-account credentials.
release: versioned site 6-0.mock-server.com
release: publish mockserver-node 6.0.0
release: Helm chart 6.0.0

fix: correct ECR registry, javadoc output path and SwaggerHub API URL

Three release-pipeline component scripts failed in release build #29:

docker.sh hardcoded ECR_REPO=public.ecr.aws/mockserver/mockserver, but the
ECR Public registry alias is AWS-assigned, not the repository name. Resolve
it at run time via `aws ecr-public describe-repositories`; a local dry-run
without AWS credentials falls back to a placeholder.

javadoc.sh passed -DreportOutputDirectory to `mvn javadoc:aggregate`, which
the plugin ignores, then synced a path that never existed. Sync the
aggregate HTML from where maven-javadoc-plugin actually writes it
(mockserver/target/reports/apidocs) to versions/<version>/apidocs/.

swaggerhub.sh POSTed to /apis/{owner}/{api}/{version}, which only supports
GET and DELETE -- HTTP 405. The SwaggerHub Registry API save-definition
operation is POST /apis/{owner}/{api} with the version as a query parameter.

release: stamp client library and OpenAPI versions to 6.0.0

The npm, pypi, rubygems and swaggerhub publish components read the version
to publish from their package's own version file. finalize bumps those
files but runs after the publish group, so release build #29 published
stale versions (pypi published mockserver-client as 5.16.0; npm would have
published mockserver-node@5.15.0 over the already-released version).

Stamp the release version 6.0.0 into all of them so the publish group
publishes 6.0.0:
- mockserver-node / mockserver-client-node: package.json version, the
  bundled netty jar filename, the mockserver-node devDependency, the
  index.js runtime default, Gruntfile.js, README and examples
- mockserver-client-python/pyproject.toml
- mockserver-client-ruby version.rb
- the embedded OpenAPI model spec

finalize still re-applies these (a no-op) and updates the remaining
site/Helm/docs references.

fix: make git_commit_and_push and git_tag_and_push idempotent

Release builds are frequently re-run after a partial failure. Two shared
git helpers were not idempotent and broke re-runs:

git_commit_and_push: when a re-run finds the change already committed by
an earlier run, `git add` stages nothing and `git commit` exits non-zero
with "nothing to commit", failing the script under set -euo pipefail.
This is what failed release build #30's versioned-site step -- the
terraform.tfvars change was already committed by build #29.

git_tag_and_push: when a re-run finds the tag already created by an
earlier run, `git tag` exits non-zero with "tag already exists".

Skip the commit when nothing is staged, and skip the tag when it already
exists locally or on the remote -- both return success so a re-run is a
clean no-op.
release: publish mockserver-node 6.0.0
release: Helm chart 6.0.0

fix: make the publish components idempotent for re-runs

Release builds are re-run after partial failures, but the publish
components were not idempotent -- a component that already published its
artifact in an earlier run then failed the re-run. Build #31's github
step failed exactly this way (the mockserver-6.0.0 GitHub release already
existed from build #29), and pypi/rubygems/maven-plugin would fail the
same way on the next re-run after publishing 6.0.0 in build #31.

Make four components skip cleanly when their artifact already exists:
- github.sh: skip `gh release create` if `gh release view` finds the
  release
- maven-plugin.sh: exit early if the version is already on Maven Central
- pypi.sh / rubygems.sh: the pre-existing-version check now logs and
  exits 0 instead of erroring

build: make the swaggerhub release step non-blocking

Publishing the OpenAPI spec to SwaggerHub via its Registry API needs
account / API-plan access the pipeline cannot guarantee -- the write
endpoint returns 403/404 even with a valid key on an account without it.
SwaggerHub is an optional third-party catalogue mirror and must not block
the release.

Mark the swaggerhub step soft_fail: true so a failure no longer fails the
build, and document the manual web-UI upload fallback in the
release-management skill's Manual Follow-up section. The step stays in the
pipeline so it publishes automatically if SwaggerHub access is ever in
place.

fix: bundle SLF4J provider in no-dependencies jars and stop dependency leakage

The mockserver-netty-no-dependencies shaded jar, which the Docker image and
CLI run directly, shipped without an SLF4J logging provider, so logging
silently fell back to a no-op logger and the container produced no output.
The module shades mockserver-netty as a dependency; mockserver-netty declares
slf4j-jdk14 optional so the binding is not imposed on library consumers, and
optional dependencies are not transitive, so it never reached the shade
classpath.

Declare slf4j-jdk14 directly in mockserver-netty-no-dependencies so the shade
plugin bundles the provider. It is kept optional: shade bundles a module's own
optional dependencies anyway, and optional keeps slf4j-jdk14 off the classpath
of anything that consumes this artifact as a Maven dependency.

Separately, every *-no-dependencies module declared its shaded source module
as a normal compile dependency, so Maven consumers of these "no dependencies"
artifacts wrongly received the un-shaded module and its transitive
dependencies on the classpath. Mark each source dependency optional so the
published artifacts are truly dependency-free. The maven-netty-no-dependencies
invoker test now declares mockserver-testing explicitly, as it no longer
arrives transitively.

Add a behavioural regression test: NoDependenciesJarRunner captures the forked
jar's output and ExtendedNoDependenciesJarMockingIntegrationTest asserts the
jar boots and logs its startup banner with no SLF4J provider warnings.

Closes #2097

test: make RecordedExpectationFileSystemPersistenceTest deterministic

shouldPersistRecordedExpectationsOnForwardedRequest waited for asynchronous
file persistence (event-log ring buffer -> listener -> file write) with a
fixed three-second sleep, which failed intermittently on slow or loaded
machines when the write had not yet landed.

Replace the sleep with a poll that waits up to 30 seconds for the expected
content and returns as soon as the write completes. Verified stable over five
consecutive runs.

docs: add mandatory changelog review to the pre-commit workflow

Add a Changelog Review step to the commit workflow so every commit is checked
against changelog.md and user-facing changes are recorded under [Unreleased].
Renumber the adversarial review and commit steps and update the skip
conditions and quick-reference diagram to match.
release: Helm chart 6.0.0

fix: make npm publish idempotent and wait for registry propagation

Release build #32 published mockserver-node@6.0.0 successfully, but the
mockserver-client-node build that runs next failed with ETARGET: its
npm install needs mockserver-node@~6.0.0 and npm's registry is eventually
consistent, so the just-published version was not yet downloadable.

publish_one() now:
- skips cleanly (return 0) if the package version is already on npm, so a
  re-run does not try to republish mockserver-node@6.0.0 over itself; the
  npm package name is read from package.json since it differs from the
  directory name (mockserver-client-node publishes as mockserver-client)
- after `npm publish`, blocks until the new version is actually resolvable
  from the registry (polling, 300s ceiling) before returning, so the
  second package's `npm install` can resolve the first

curl calls use connect/max-time limits so a hung registry does not stall
the step.

test: guard executable jar logging with a boot-and-log integration test

The mockserver-netty jar-with-dependencies executable uber-jar — run by the
MockServer Maven plugin and shipped via Homebrew — is built by
maven-assembly-plugin, separately from the maven-shade-plugin
mockserver-netty-no-dependencies jar. Only the latter had a logging
regression test, so a future assembly-config change could silently strip the
SLF4J provider from the executable jar (the issue #2097 failure mode) with
nothing to catch it.

Add JarWithDependenciesLoggingIntegrationTest: it boots the assembly jar in a
forked JVM and asserts it logs its startup banner with no SLF4J provider
warnings — the same behavioural guard that ExtendedNoDependenciesJarMockingIntegrationTest
provides for the no-dependencies jar.

Closes #2097
release: publish mockserver-client-node 6.0.0

fix: declare commons-lang3 and commons-io directly in mockserver-examples

mockserver-examples uses org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.isNotBlank
and org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils directly but declared neither — it relied
on them arriving transitively through mockserver-netty-no-dependencies and
mockserver-client-java-no-dependencies. Those modules now mark their shaded
source module optional to stop dependency leakage, so the transitive commons
artifacts no longer reach the examples compile classpath and mvn clean
install fails to compile mockserver-examples.

Declare both directly; versions are inherited from the parent pom's
dependencyManagement.

fix: publish the maven-plugin to Maven Central, not just validate it

The parent pom configures central-publishing-maven-plugin with
autoPublish=false and waitUntil=validated, so maven-plugin.sh's mvn deploy
only uploaded and validated the deployment on the Sonatype Central Portal —
it never promoted it, so the plugin never actually reached Maven Central.

Override both on the command line: autoPublish=true promotes the deployment
once validation passes, and waitUntil=published blocks until the Portal
confirms PUBLISHED so a non-zero exit is a real publish failure.
release: Helm chart 6.0.0
release: set next development version 6.0.1-SNAPSHOT
release: update version references to 6.0.0

fix: prevent HTTP/2 requests through the HTTPS CONNECT proxy from hanging

A client tunnelling an HTTP/2 request through MockServer's HTTPS
forward-proxy (HTTP CONNECT) hung for ~30s and was then closed with a
GOAWAY, producing no log entry. The internal self-loopback relay
hard-wired an HTTP/1.1 codec while its TLS layer could negotiate h2 via
ALPN, so the HTTP/2-framed request was never decoded.

RelayConnectHandler now selects the loopback codec from the protocol
negotiated with the proxy client - an HTTP/2 codec when the client
negotiated h2, the HTTP/1.1 codec otherwise - so the loopback's TLS
layer and codec always agree and the relay stays a transparent
passthrough.

Also adds an http2Enabled configuration property (default true); when
false ALPN no longer advertises h2 and h2c is not detected, forcing
HTTP/2-capable clients to HTTP/1.1.

Fixes #2260

fix: publish the maven-plugin via the Central Portal API

The previous attempt added -DautoPublish=true -DwaitUntil=published to
mvn deploy, but Maven gives explicit POM <configuration> precedence over -D
user properties. The parent pom sets autoPublish=false / waitUntil=validated
as explicit configuration, so the flags were silently ignored: the maven-plugin
deployment stopped at VALIDATED and never reached Maven Central, while the
step still exited 0 and looked successful.

Drop the non-functional flags. central-publishing-maven-plugin prints the
deploymentId on upload, so capture the deploy output, extract that id, and
promote the deployment with POST /api/v1/publisher/deployment/{id}, then poll
the status endpoint until it leaves VALIDATED (failing on FAILED or timeout).

docs: move SLF4J / no-dependencies fixes to the Unreleased changelog section

The #2097 logging fix and the no-dependencies dependency-leak fix ship in
6.0.1, not 6.0.0. They were recorded under [Unreleased], but the 6.0.0 release
renamed that section to [6.0.0], carrying the entries with it. Move them back
under the new [Unreleased] section so they are attributed to 6.0.1.

fix: repair failing CI pipelines

Three pipelines were failing, all confirmed against live build logs:

- Buildkite: mockserver-integration-testing-no-dependencies shaded an
  empty jar. Its mockserver-integration-testing dependency was marked
  optional with no explicit scope, so the parent pom's managed test
  scope applied and the shade plugin skipped it, breaking the
  mockserver-netty-no-dependencies invoker test compilation. Declare
  scope compile explicitly so shade bundles the classes.

- CodeQL: the Java analysis ran `mvn clean compile`, but
  mockserver-examples depends on the *-no-dependencies shaded jars
  whose classes only exist after the shade plugin runs in the package
  phase. Run `mvn clean package` instead.

- Welcome bot: actions/first-interaction@v3 requires pr_message; the
  workflow only supplied issue_message and failed every run. Add it.

fix: derive OpenAPI spec version in test from the spec resource

OpenAPISpecHandlerTest.shouldReturnOpenAPISpecWithCorrectContentType
hardcoded `version: 5.16.0`. The release process stamps the version into
the embedded OpenAPI spec resource (and other non-Java files) but never
rewrites .java files, so the test went stale at the 6.0.0 release and
failed the mockserver-netty build.

Read the expected version from the spec resource itself so the assertion
tracks the released version automatically and never needs a manual
update.

fix: bundle mockserver-testing in integration-testing-no-dependencies jar

The gradle-netty-no-dependencies-dependencies integration test failed
with NoClassDefFoundError for org.mockserver.test.Assert and
org.mockserver.test.Retries. The shaded base classes in
mockserver-integration-testing (AbstractProxyIntegrationTest,
AbstractBasicMockingIntegrationTest) reference those mockserver-testing
classes, but they were missing from the shaded jar.

mockserver-testing is a compile dependency of
mockserver-integration-testing, but the parent pom's dependencyManagement
forces it to test scope when resolved transitively, so the shade plugin
excluded it. Declare mockserver-testing directly with an explicit compile
scope so it reaches the shade classpath, mirroring the fix already
applied to mockserver-integration-testing in this pom.

fix: pin uuid to a patched version to clear CVE-2026-41907

GitHub Dependabot reported CVE-2026-41907 (uuid < 11.1.1, missing buffer
bounds check in v3/v5/v6) against the mockserver-node and
mockserver-client-node packages. uuid is a transitive development-only
dependency (via nyc, request, istanbul-lib-processinfo) and the
dependents cap it at uuid@^3 / ^8, so a normal update cannot reach the
patched release.

Add an npm overrides entry forcing uuid to ^11.1.1 in both packages and
regenerate the lockfiles; uuid now resolves to 11.1.1 everywhere. The
mockserver-client-node lockfile additionally syncs its mockserver-node
devDependency snapshot from ~6.0.0 to 6.0.0 to match package.json.

The grunt build (jshint, ts) and npm ci both still pass.

feat: stream proxied LLM/MCP traffic and add a dashboard Traffic Inspector

Lets MockServer act as an observability proxy in front of AI coding
agents and LLM/MCP endpoints so developers can inspect the traffic.

Streaming relay (mockserver-core / mockserver-netty):
- relay streaming proxy responses (Server-Sent Events and chunked) to
  the client incrementally instead of fully buffering them, while
  capturing a bounded copy as readable text into the event log
- new StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator, StreamingResponseRelayHandler,
  StreamingBody and StreamIdleTimeoutHandler
- force full aggregation when a forward response override is present
- new configuration: streamingResponsesEnabled, maxStreamingCaptureBytes,
  streamIdleTimeoutSeconds

Dashboard Traffic Inspector (mockserver-ui):
- new Traffic view with a Dashboard/Traffic toggle, a master list of
  proxied calls and an adaptive per-kind detail pane (Messages,
  Conversation transcript, SSE Timeline, MCP, Raw JSON)
- Download HAR button

Documentation:
- new AI traffic inspection guide, updated dashboard and configuration
  pages, and internal architecture docs

docs: record trunk-based development in the git policy

State explicitly that the repository uses trunk-based development -
commits go directly to the default branch and feature/topic branches
are not used - so the agent instructions match the team's workflow.

fix: detect streaming responses only by text/event-stream content type

StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator classified any chunked response with
no Content-Length as a streaming response. WAR/servlet deployments strip
Content-Length and use chunked transfer-encoding for every response, so
all WAR responses were misclassified as streaming - clients received
head-only (bodyless) responses, failing 14 mockserver-war integration
tests on master (build #4335).

Narrow streaming detection to Content-Type: text/event-stream, which is
what real LLM streaming APIs and MCP streamable-HTTP use.

feat: add agent-oriented MCP tools for debugging and verification

Add seven MCP tools and supporting capabilities so coding agents can
diagnose failed requests and verify implementations against a contract:

- explain_unmatched_requests: ranked closest-expectation diffs with
  remediation hints for requests that matched no expectation, also
  exposed as PUT /mockserver/explainUnmatched and the
  mockserver://unmatched resource; debug_request_mismatch results are
  now ranked by closeness
- create_expectations_from_recorded_traffic: turn traffic recorded
  through the forwarding proxy into active mock expectations
- verify_traffic_against_openapi and run_contract_test: check that
  recorded traffic, and a running service, conform to an OpenAPI
  contract
- run_resiliency_test: send malformed and boundary-case requests and
  report which inputs a service fails to handle gracefully
- record_llm_fixtures and load_expectations_from_file: snapshot LLM/MCP
  traffic into committable, secret-redacted fixtures and replay them,
  reconstructing SSE streaming responses

The MCP initialize response now carries an instructions field so
connecting agents discover these capabilities up front. Consumer and
internal documentation and the changelog are updated.

docs: add AI-native SDLC principles guide

Add docs/operations/ai-native-sdlc-principles.md covering the principles for
working with AI across the software development lifecycle: the engineer's role,
spec-first control, the trust model, verification over generation, context,
standardisation, observability, security boundaries, continuous improvement, and
the full system model. Includes the AI failure modes and the lethal trifecta,
with guardrails (sandbox, policy enforcement, task-scoped tokens) and an AI
Firewall as the architectural mitigation.

Cross-link the new guide from the docs index, the AGENTS.md documentation table,
and ai-assisted-development.md.
docs: correct operations doc count in README quick reference

feat: add SES email forwarding for mock-server.com

Add a Terraform stack (terraform/ses-email-forwarding/) that provisions
AWS-native catch-all email forwarding: all mail to *@mock-server.com is
received by SES, stored in S3, and re-sent by a Lambda forwarder to a
configured destination address.

- SES domain identity, DKIM, and a catch-all receipt rule
- S3 bucket for raw inbound mail with lifecycle expiry
- Node.js Lambda that rewrites the From header (Reply-To preserves the
  original sender) and forwards via SES SendRawEmail
- Route 53 MX, verification, DKIM, and DMARC records
- Optional CloudWatch error alarm + SNS notification (enable_monitoring)
- Documentation in docs/infrastructure/aws-ses-email-forwarding.md
fix: README.md Previous Versions missing 5.15.0 + remove extra table indentation (#2262)

feat: add stable Automatic-Module-Name to every published JAR manifest

Downstream JPMS consumers can now `requires` MockServer modules with
names that no longer change across version bumps. Each module pom
defines a <module.name> property and the parent maven-jar-plugin emits
it as Automatic-Module-Name. The -no-dependencies shaded variants gain
a ManifestResourceTransformer so the entry survives shading; the WAR
modules are skipped because maven-jar-plugin doesn't run for war
packaging. Module names match the actual root package of each module
(e.g. mockserver-testing -> org.mockserver.test) so a future
module-info.java effort can align cleanly.

docs: prune obsolete plans and refresh gaps audit

Delete six superseded plan files (issue-resolution, java-17-migration,
monorepo-migration, pr-resolution, release-pipeline, release-pipeline-next-steps)
and three empty `.gitkeep` placeholder directories under docs/decisions and
docs/investigation. Annotate the remaining plans (build-optimisation,
security-remediation, testing-improvements) with their current implementation
status so readers can see what is done versus pending without diving into the
codebase.

Refresh `docs/gaps-and-recommendations.md` against the verified state of the
repo: Gap 2 (release pipeline), Gap 12 (deprecated packaging), Gap 13 (.gitignore),
and Gap 14 (dependency automation) are now Resolved; Gap 5 (version references)
and Gap 9 (helm hosting) downgraded to Partial with current data; Gap 11 is
addressed separately. Inline the TOTP rotation steps in `release-process.md`
in place of the broken link to the now-deleted release-pipeline-next-steps.md.

Rebuild the plans index in `docs/README.md` and add the new LLM/agent mocking
RFC (`plans/mockserver-llm-mocking.md`), fact-checked against the codebase:
22 MCP tools (not "~20"), generic scenario state machine already shipped
(`scenarioName`/`scenarioState`/`newScenarioState` + `ScenarioManager`), HAR
export wired into the dashboard AppBar — so RFC-2 reduces to Layer B only.

fix(tls): validate cert paths in Configuration fluent setters

The instance-level fluent setters on Configuration.java accepted custom
TLS certificate paths without checking that the file exists, so a typo
in privateKeyPath / x509CertificatePath / certificateAuthorityPrivateKey
/ certificateAuthorityCertificate would only surface much later during
the TLS handshake as an unhelpful Netty exception. The matching static
setters on ConfigurationProperties already call fileExists() on the
same paths; this brings the fluent setters to parity.

Add unit coverage for each of the four touched setters: a non-existent
path raises a RuntimeException whose message names the path, null and
empty are tolerated (matching the existing isNotBlank-guarded contract
of ConfigurationProperties.fileExists), and a valid path stores the
value.

Removes docs/spec/tls-certificate-validation/ — all functional
requirements are now implemented in the codebase.

feat(client): exponential WS reconnect and JS verifyZeroInteractions

The Python websocket client capped reconnect attempts at 3 but slept
a flat one second between them; switch to the same min(2^n, 8) seconds
back-off the Ruby client uses, matching NFR-06 of the client-libraries
spec across all three callback-capable clients.

The Node.js websocket client had no reconnect logic at all — a single
WebSocket close ended callbacks silently. Add a 3-attempt cap with
matching exponential back-off, triggered from both connection.close and
post-initial-connect connectFailed. The initial connect failure still
rejects the original promise as before, so existing error handling for
"can't connect to MockServer" keeps working.

Add the verifyZeroInteractions() shorthand to the Node.js client (and
mockServerClient.d.ts) — Python and Ruby already expose it and Java
treats it as the canonical no-traffic assertion. Implemented as a thin
wrapper over verify({}, 0, 0); existing verify() semantics unchanged.

Removes docs/spec/client-libraries/ — the spec's functional and
non-functional requirements are now satisfied across all three
non-Java clients.

refactor(test): dedupe docker-compose examples and integration tests

The 10 published docker-compose examples under
mockserver/mockserver-examples/docker_compose_examples/ and the 10 CI
test directories under container_integration_tests/ both kept their own
copy of every compose file, differing only by the client-image name
(`integration_testing_client` vs `integration_testing_client_curl`) —
and the examples' image name was not built anywhere in the repo,
making every published example silently broken.

Collapse both trees onto a single source of truth using docker compose's
overlay merge. Each example now holds only the user-facing MockServer
configuration (public `mockserver/mockserver:latest`, exposed host
ports, no test sidecar) so `docker compose up` works out of the box.
Each test directory holds an `integration_test.sh` and a tiny
`docker-compose.override.yml` that swaps in the locally-built
`:integration_testing` image, resets host port-publishing to avoid
agent-side port clashes, and adds the curl/nghttp `client:` sidecar
the tests exec into.

The harness (`container_integration_tests/docker-compose.sh`) resolves
the base+overlay pair from the test case name, exports an
`${OVERRIDE_DIR}` env var so overlays needing test-local writable
volumes (with_persisted_expectations) or test-generated fixtures
(with_mtls) can address paths inside the test directory rather than
the example dir, and guards against pre-2.22 docker compose versions
that lack the `!reset`/`!override` merge tags used by the overlays.

`docker_compose_with_mtls` — previously example-only — is now wired
through the harness with a new integration_test.sh that regenerates
certs on every run from the example's generate_certs.sh, asserts a
valid-cert request returns the seeded body, and asserts a missing-cert
request is rejected. A directory-local `.gitignore` keeps the
generated certs and copied config out of git.

README files in both trees explain the architecture and the
`${OVERRIDE_DIR}` mechanism so future contributors can extend either
side without recreating the drift.

Resolves Gap 11 in docs/gaps-and-recommendations.md.

docs: close several open gaps with new architecture / perf / config / release reference

Add a "Where to make changes" section to CONTRIBUTING.md mapping the
common contribution types (matchers, actions, Netty pipeline, TLS,
configuration properties, ring buffer / log retention, event system,
dashboard UI, clients, MCP/A2A, build, Docker, Helm, CI, release,
website) to the right module and reference doc. Link CONTRIBUTING.md
to docs/code/overview.md and docs/architecture.md as the entry points.

Add docs/code/configuration-reference.md explaining the property
loading mechanism — system property > env var > properties file >
default — the four equivalent forms (file, env, sysprop, programmatic
Configuration setter), the property categories, and the five-place

fix(test): deflake MockServerEventLog concurrent verification

Replace Thread.sleep-based synchronisation with a CountDownLatch so the
main thread waits deterministically for the background add() to complete
before calling verify(). verify() already calls drainDisruptor() so once
both add() invocations have returned, both entries are guaranteed to be
processed before the assertion runs.

feat(security): SSRF / ReDoS / XPath DoS / unbounded body / SecureRandom protections

Implements 8 of 12 items from docs/plans/security-remediation.md and
adds warning logs for the remaining four breaking-change items.

Resolved fully:
- SEC-1: SSRF — new InetAddressValidator (loopback, link-local, RFC 1918,
  RFC 4193 ULA, cloud-metadata) wired into the forward and forward-template
  handlers; opt-in via mockserver.forwardProxyBlockPrivateNetworks (default
  false for backwards compatibility — localhost / Docker / k8s keep working)
- SEC-2: ReDoS — RegexStringMatcher evaluates patterns through a shared
  daemon-thread executor with mockserver.regexMatchingTimeoutMillis
  (default 1000ms); timeouts return non-match and log WARN
- SEC-6: XPath DoS — XPathEvaluator uses the same shared executor with
  mockserver.xpathMatchingTimeoutMillis (default 1000ms) and returns a
  type-appropriate sentinel (FALSE / "" / NaN / null) on timeout
- SEC-9: SecureRandom — finished the migration the previous commit started;
  UUIDService and TemplateFunctions now use SecureRandom
- SEC-11: bounded bodies — mockserver.maxRequestBodySize (10 MiB) and
  mockserver.maxResponseBodySize (50 MiB) wired into PortUnificationHandler
  (HTTP/1.1 + HTTP/2 inbound) and HttpClientInitializer (upstream responses);
  BREAKING — previously unbounded
- PER-1: documented LMAX Disruptor power-of-2 sizing for maxExpectations and
  maxLogEntries in the consumer docs

Warning-only (defaults unchanged, opt-in flip via tlsAllowInsecureProtocols):
- SEC-3: WARN when forwardProxyTLSX509CertificatesTrustManagerType=ANY
- SEC-4: WARN when Velocity class loading is enabled
- SEC-8: WARN when javascriptDisallowedClasses is empty
- SEC-10: WARN when tlsProtocols includes TLSv1 / TLSv1.1; new
  mockserver.tlsAllowInsecureProtocols (default true) lets users opt into a
  hardened TLS profile without rewriting tlsProtocols

Plan and changelog updated; consumer docs document all six new properties.

fix(tls): unbreak dynamic CA generation by relaxing fluent-setter validation

Commit 179bc1899 ("fix(tls): validate cert paths in Configuration fluent
setters") added fileExists() to the four instance setters on
Configuration.java. That broke BCKeyAndCertificateFactory's dynamic CA and
SSL certificate generation flow: at BCKeyAndCertificateFactory.java:101,
140, 259, and 278 the factory calls these instance setters with the
*destination* path BEFORE the file is generated, so fileExists() now
throws and aborts dynamic certificate creation. All
ClientAuthenticationDynamicCAMockingIntegrationTest tests have been
failing since Buildkite build #312 (commit 8afcea94b, which first
inherited 179bc1899).

Remove fileExists() from the four affected instance setters and document
the deliberate asymmetry with their static ConfigurationProperties
counterparts (which still validate, because user-supplied configuration
should fail fast). User typos in custom certificate paths are still
surfaced by CertificateConfigurationValidator at TLS-init time, so the
"catch typos early" intent of 179bc1899 is preserved on the user-facing
code path.

Update the four ConfigurationTest setter tests to assert the new
contract (any value accepted; null/empty tolerated; round-trips
unchanged) and add a changelog entry under Fixed.

fix(matchers): stabilise regex / XPath timeout protection under parallel CI

Two issues observed in Buildkite mockserver-java build #330 caused a
flake in HttpRequestPropertiesMatcherTest.shouldMatchXPathBody:

1. The shared cached thread pool in MatchingTimeoutExecutor reuses
   worker threads across submissions. When a previous task timed out
   and was cancelled with interrupt, the long-running work (XPath /
   regex evaluation) ignored the interrupt and kept running; on
   completion the worker returned to the pool with its interrupt flag
   set. The next submission could then observe spurious failure or a
   prematurely cleared interrupt. Wrap each user task in a clean
   prologue that calls Thread.interrupted() to clear any residual
   interrupt flag before the real work runs.

2. The 1000ms default timeout for regex and XPath had insufficient
   headroom for CI parallel-class execution latency. Raise both
   defaults to 5000ms (still bounds pathological backtracking, which
   takes minutes-to-hours). Update Javadoc, consumer docs, and the
   changelog entry to match.

Consolidates remaining work from the prior security remediation plan
into a single document focused on insecure-by-default flips for the
next major release. Drops completed items and adds three new flips
(localBoundIP, attemptToProxyIfNoMatchingExpectation, HTTP parsing
limits) plus an explicit list of items considered and rejected.

fix(pr-monitor): drop unsupported --auto flag so merges actually fire

The script only invokes `gh pr merge` after observing buildkite_state ==
SUCCESS and zero failed Actions, so the merge can happen immediately.
The `--auto` flag asks GitHub to queue an auto-merge once required
checks pass, but this repository does not have repository-level
auto-merge enabled, so every call returned:

    GraphQL: Auto merge is not allowed for this repository
    (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)

Removing `--auto` makes the merge synchronous; branch protection rules
are still enforced server-side, and the existing `else` branch already
handles the "MERGE FAILED - Will retry" case. Log line updated from
"MERGE QUEUED/COMPLETED" to "MERGED" to reflect the synchronous flow.

build(ci): speed up snapshot deploy

The :nexus: deploy snapshot to Sonatype step on mockserver-java was
taking ~17 min — actually longer than the :maven: build step itself —
because it ran serially and from a cold container.

Add four flags to `.buildkite/scripts/steps/java-deploy-snapshot.sh`:

  -T 1C                       run module compile + package + upload in
                              parallel, matching what the test build
                              step already does and what
                              scripts/release/finalize.sh's snapshot
                              path already does. Central Portal's
                              snapshot endpoint handles concurrent
                              uploads from the same session.
  -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true   defensive — release profile is not active
  -Dmaven.source.skip=true    on the snapshot path so neither plugin
                              runs today, but the flag protects against
                              a future profile-activation regression.
  -Dgpg.skip=true             same rationale — snapshots are not
                              signature-checked by Central Portal.

The release flow is untouched: scripts/release/components/maven-{central,plugin}.sh
and scripts/release/finalize.sh invoke `mvn deploy -P release` which
activates the release profile that re-enables javadoc / sources / GPG /
central-publishing — none of these new flags suppress those.

Estimated yield ~5-7 min from -T 1C alone (Sonatype upload remains
network-bound but parallel module deploys overlap with the next module's
package phase).

feat(llm): foundations for first-class LLM/agent mocking

Scaffold the new `httpLlmResponse` action type so LLM expectations can
be registered, persisted, dispatched, and round-tripped through the
JSON expectation format and the dashboard pipeline. No provider codec
ships in this commit -- every provider returns 501 at dispatch until
M1 lands Anthropic and OpenAI Chat Completions encoders. This is the
foundation that the response builder, conversation matchers, MCP
tools, dashboard rendering and remaining 5 codecs will build on
across M1-M4 of the implementation plan.

Adds:
- Provider-neutral domain model: Completion, ToolUse, Usage,
  StreamingPhysics, EmbeddingResponse, HttpLlmResponse, Provider enum
  (7 providers covered at the type level).
- ProviderCodec interface + thread-safe registry under
  `org.mockserver.llm` (empty at M0; populated from M1).
- `Action.Type.LLM_RESPONSE` enum value, full DTO + Jackson
  serializer + JSON Schema entry, with the new action plumbed
  through Expectation copy/equals/hashCode, ExpectationDTO,
  ObjectMapperFactory, JsonSchemaExpectationValidator, and the
  HttpActionHandler dispatch switch (with expectationPostProcessor
  guaranteed on the exception path).
- Metrics.Name.LLM_RESPONSE_ACTIONS_COUNT registered alongside the
  other action counters so increments do not throw at runtime.
- HttpLlmResponseActionHandler returning a 501 body until codecs
  land in M1.
- `mockserver.maxLlmConversationBodySize` config property (bytes;
  default 1 MiB; clamped to [16 KiB, 64 MiB]); env-var form and
  consumer documentation entry.
- ForwardChainExpectation.respondWithLlm() so the Java client can
  build LLM expectations without dropping to raw JSON.

Tests: 68 new unit tests across 6 classes (model equals/hashCode,
registry concurrency, expectation round-trip, config clamping,
handler 501 behaviour) plus existing ForwardChainExpectation and
serialization regression suites verified green.

fix(buildkite): treat skipped downstream builds as terminal in trigger-pipeline.sh

The trigger-pipeline.sh poll loop only recognised passed/failed/canceled/not_run
as terminal states. When a downstream build was `skipped` by Buildkite (e.g.
mockserver-infra has skip_queued_branch_builds: true, so older queued runs are
supplanted by the newest), polling fell through to the wildcard arm and ran
for the full 2-hour MAX_WAIT, holding a trigger-queue agent slot.

Treat `skipped` as success with a :fast_forward: log line — skip_queued_branch_builds
is intentional, so the newer build for the same branch is the source of truth.

feat(llm): Anthropic + OpenAI codecs with streaming physics and embeddings

Implements milestone M1 of the LLM/agent mocking feature. With this commit
an LLM expectation registered via `llmMock(...).withProvider(ANTHROPIC | OPENAI)`
returns a real, byte-correct provider response instead of a 501 placeholder.
The conversation matcher and remaining 5 codecs follow in M2 and M4.

Codecs:
- `AnthropicCodec` (Messages API, version 2024-10-22) -- non-streaming JSON
  with text and tool_use content blocks, mapped stop_reason, usage; streaming
  SSE sequence (`message_start` -> `content_block_start`/`*_delta`/`*_stop`
  per text/tool block -> `message_delta` -> `message_stop`) with the named
  Anthropic event types.
- `OpenAiChatCompletionsCodec` (Chat Completions, 2025-01) -- non-streaming
  `chat.completion` with `choices[].message`, finish_reason mapping
  (`end_turn` -> `stop`, `tool_use` -> `tool_calls`, `max_tokens` -> `length`);
  streaming `chat.completion.chunk` sequence terminating with `data: [DONE]`;
  embeddings endpoint with deterministic vectors keyed by SHA-256 over
  `seed:dimensions:input` (so different dimensions values yield independent
  vectors, not prefix-compatible) and L2 normalisation.

Action dispatch:
- `HttpLlmResponseActionHandler` now looks up the registered codec and
  encodes for non-streaming, embeddings, and streaming paths. Returns 400
  with `{"error":"unsupported LLM provider: X","supported":[...]}` when no
  codec is registered for the requested provider, and 502 with the provider
  name on internal codec failure.
- `HttpActionHandler.LLM_RESPONSE` branches on streaming: streaming responses
  build an ephemeral `HttpSseResponse` (content-type: text/event-stream,
  cache-control: no-cache) and delegate to the existing SSE handler, with
  `expectationPostProcessor.run()` guaranteed in `finally`; WAR deployments
  without a Netty `ctx` return 501 (parity with the SSE case).
- `ProviderCodecRegistry` static initialiser eagerly registers the Anthropic
  and OpenAI codecs at class-load time.

Streaming physics:
- `StreamingPhysicsExpander` applies `timeToFirstToken`, `tokensPerSecond`,
  `jitter` (uniform +/- fraction), and `seed` to a raw `List<SseEvent>`,
  producing a new list with per-event delays. Codecs always pipe their raw
  event lists through this expander.

Builder API (Java client):
- `LlmMockBuilder.llmMock(path).withProvider(...).withModel(...)
  .respondingWith(completion()|embedding()).applyTo(client)`.
- `Llm` static-import facade re-exporting `completion()`, `toolUse()`,
  `inputTokens()`, `outputTokens()`, `streamingPhysics()`,
  `timeToFirstToken()`, `tokensPerSecond()`, `jitter()`, `embedding()`.
- `Completion.streaming()` no-arg shortcut and varargs
  `withStreamingPhysics(Object... parts)` that merges `Delay` + per-field
  `StreamingPhysics` fragments left-to-right, so `withStreamingPhysics(
  timeToFirstToken(300, MILLISECONDS), tokensPerSecond(50), jitter(0.2))`
  composes as in the spec example.
- `LlmConversationBuilder` ships as a pre-release stub; only `conversation()`
  is callable. The full multi-turn implementation lands in M2.

Shared utility:
- `JsonEscape.escape()` covers the seven RFC 8259 short escapes plus
  `\uXXXX` for control characters below U+0020. Both streaming codecs use
  it instead of duplicated private helpers.

Tests: 173 new + updated unit tests across 10 classes covering codec
output shape (golden-style structural assertions, not random ids), streaming
sequence ordering, physics formula determinism with fixed seed, embedding
independence across dimensions, handler dispatch (200 for registered
providers, 400 for unregistered, streaming routes through `handleStreaming`),
failure-mode validation, and the client builder wiring. All M0 tests
remain green; the M0 handler tests are updated to match the new 400 contract
for unsupported providers.

Adds CustomJsonUnitMatcherProvider SPI plus a mockserver.customJsonUnitMatchersClass

feat(llm): conversation-aware matchers with per-session isolation

Implements milestone M2 of the LLM/agent mocking feature. A registered
LLM conversation now branches its response based on the inbound message
history (turn index, latest-message contents/role, presence of a tool
result correlated by tool call id) and can isolate state per session via
`isolateBy(header(...) | queryParameter(...) | cookie(...))`. The full
agent-loop flow (turn 1 -> tool_use, turn 2 after tool_result -> final
answer) works end-to-end across a real client/server boundary.

Decode path:
- AnthropicCodec.decode() and OpenAiChatCompletionsCodec.decode()
  produce a `ParsedConversation` from the inbound request body. Tool
  call ids are preserved on `ToolUse.id` so the matcher can correlate
  tool results back to the specific call that produced them.
- Both decoders fail-closed: malformed JSON, wrong-shape bodies, or
  bodies exceeding `mockserver.maxLlmConversationBodySize` yield an
  empty `ParsedConversation`, which the matcher treats as no-match
  without throwing.

Matching:
- `LlmConversationMatcher` evaluates the five predicates with AND
  semantics: `whenTurnIndex`, `whenLatestMessageContains` (substring or
  regex), `whenLatestMessageRole`, `whenContainsToolResultFor` (now
  correctly correlated by tool call id, not name only).
- Predicates serialise as a `ConversationPredicates` value object on
  `HttpLlmResponse`, with full DTO + JSON-schema coverage, so they
  survive the client/server PUT/expectation boundary. The
  `LlmConversationMatcher` is reconstructed lazily on the server side
  from the deserialised predicates.

Isolation:
- `ScenarioManager` gains composite-key storage `(scenarioName,
  isolation)` while preserving every existing single-arg method as a
  delegate with `isolation=null`. `compute()`-based atomicity is kept;
  `clear(name)` uses `keySet().removeIf` so concurrent inserts cannot
  survive a clear.
- `IsolationSource` (header/query/cookie) describes where to read the
  per-session key from the inbound request. The source is encoded as a
  reserved `__iso=` suffix on the auto-generated scenario name
  (`__llm_conv_<uuid>`), keeping the change off the JSON schema and DTO
  surface. `RequestMatchers.extractIsolationKey` decodes the source and
  reads the value at match time; missing keys fall back to the shared
  scenario (verified by the new end-to-end test).
- `getAllStatesStructured()` returns `Map<ScenarioKey,String>` for
  programmatic callers; the legacy `getAllStates()` Map<String,String>
  is preserved with javadoc warning that composite key string format is
  display-only.

Client builder:
- `LlmConversationBuilder.conversation().withPath(...)
  .withProvider(...).isolateBy(...).turn().whenTurnIndex(0)
  .respondingWith(completion()...).andThen().turn()
  .whenContainsToolResultFor("search").respondingWith(...).applyTo(client)`.
- `TurnBuilder` carries per-turn predicates and the completion; each
  turn becomes one Expectation with auto-generated scenario state
  progression (`Started -> turn_1 -> ... -> __done`).
- `Llm` static-import facade re-exports `conversation()`, `header()`,
  `queryParameter()`, `cookie()` so a single static import covers the
  full builder.

Tests: 27 (matcher) + 20 (scenario manager composite key) + 7 (round
trip) + 13/11 (decoders) + 14 (client builder) + 4 (end-to-end
including isolation fallback and predicate-on-wire) -- 183 unit and
integration tests, all green. Regression suites for ScenarioManager,
JsonSchemaExpectationValidator, ForwardChainExpectation,
ExpectationSerializer, and ClientAndServerMockingIntegrationTest's
`shouldErrorForInvalidExpectation` confirmed unchanged.

feat(llm): MCP control plane, dashboard rendering, and consumer/internal docs

Implements milestone M3 of the LLM/agent mocking feature. The LLM
feature is now discoverable from natural-language agents (two new MCP
tools), from the dashboard UI (provider/model badge + scripted-turn
panel), and from the consumer documentation site.

MCP control plane:
- `mock_llm_completion` registers a single-turn LLM expectation
  (provider, path, model, text, toolCalls, stopReason, usage,
  streaming). Tool count goes from 22 to 23.
- `create_llm_conversation` builds a multi-turn scenario-chained
  conversation with optional per-session `isolateBy` (header /
  queryParameter / cookie). Returns the auto-generated scenario name
  and per-turn states. Tool count goes from 23 to 24.
- Both tools advertise only providers with a registered codec
  (ANTHROPIC + OPENAI at this milestone) in their JSON Schema enum,
  and the runtime rejection path returns a structured
  `{error, message, supported[]}` for providers that haven't shipped
  a codec yet. Pre-validation at the tool boundary avoids the
  runtime 400 surprise that would otherwise hit users of in-progress

feat(llm): OpenAI Responses, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Ollama codecs

Implements milestone M4 of the LLM/agent mocking feature. The remaining
five providers now have working codecs registered with the
ProviderCodecRegistry, so the Provider enum's seven values are all
functional. The MCP tool enum (M3) picks them up automatically because
it queries `supportedProviderNames()` rather than hard-coding the list.

New codecs:
- `OpenAiResponsesCodec` (`OPENAI_RESPONSES`, apiVersion `2025-03`) --
  uses the Responses API output[] array shape with `message` and
  `function_call` items; streaming uses named SSE events
  (`response.created` -> `response.output_item.added` /
  `response.output_text.delta` / `response.output_item.done` ->
  `response.completed`). Token usage uses `input_tokens` /
  `output_tokens`, not the Chat Completions `prompt_tokens` /
  `completion_tokens`. Decode handles the Responses API's flexible
  `input` parameter (string or messages-array).
- `GeminiCodec` (`GEMINI`, apiVersion `v1beta-2025`) -- uses
  `candidates[].content.parts` with `text` and `functionCall` parts;
  `finishReason` mapped from common LLM stop reasons; tool call IDs
  synthesized from `name_index` since Gemini doesn't return IDs.
  Streaming chunks parse + re-serialise tool arguments so a non-JSON
  or syntactically broken `arguments` string cannot corrupt the wire
  output.
- `BedrockCodec` (`BEDROCK`, apiVersion `bedrock-2023-05-31`) --
  delegates to `AnthropicCodec` since AWS Bedrock's
  Anthropic-on-Bedrock invokeModel/InvokeModelWithResponseStream wire
  format is identical to native Anthropic. Bedrock's binary
  `{"chunk":{"bytes":...}}` SSE wrapping is documented as out of
  scope -- targeting the plain Anthropic body is sufficient for the
  testing scenarios this feature supports.
- `AzureOpenAiCodec` (`AZURE_OPENAI`, apiVersion `2024-10-21`) --
  delegates to `OpenAiChatCompletionsCodec` since Azure is
  wire-compatible (only URL paths and auth headers differ).
- `OllamaCodec` (`OLLAMA`, apiVersion `ollama-2025`) -- uses Ollama's
  `/api/chat` shape: top-level `message` object, `prompt_eval_count`
  / `eval_count` for token counts, `created_at` as ISO-8601. Tool
  calls in the streaming path are emitted on the final `done:true`
  chunk (matching Ollama's native behaviour), with arguments
  parsed and re-serialised so non-object args cannot break the
  chunk. NDJSON wire format is approximated via SseEvent without
  named events (documented limitation).

Registration:
- `ProviderCodecRegistry`'s static init now registers all 7 codecs.
  `supportedProviderNames()` returns the full set, which transitively
  expands the M3 MCP tool enum so MCP clients can target any provider.

fix(release): protect historical-milestone refs in finalize.sh find-and-replace

The general find-and-replace pass at the end of finalize.sh blindly substitutes
$OLD_VERSION -> $RELEASE_VERSION across all HTML/MD/YAML/JSON/TXT files. It
can't distinguish a current-version reference (e.g. `mockserver_version: 6.0.0`,
`<version>6.0.0</version>`) from a historical milestone reference (e.g.
`Fixed in 6.0.x`, `Before 6.0.0`, `removed in 6.0.0`, `switched to Sonatype
Central Portal in 6.0.0`). Bumping the version on a historical-milestone line
turns the statement into a lie.

Multiple historical mangles slipped through in the 6.0.0 release commit
(a513654d2) and would have slipped through the 6.1.0 release (had the
unrelated OLD_VERSION auto-derive bug not made the entire pass a no-op):
  - SECURITY.md  "Fixed in 6.0.x"
  - docs/code/overview.md  "Before 6.0.0... in 6.0.0"
  - docs/testing.md  "removed in 6.0.0"

Solution: switch the find-and-replace to a sed address-negation pattern
(`/HISTORICAL_RE/!s/X/Y/g`) that skips the substitution on lines matching
common historical-milestone markers — Before, Until, Since, Fixed in,
removed in, introduced in, deprecated in, added in, updated in, released
in, changed in, As of, Requires, Minimum version, and "<verb> ... in"
forms (switched, moved, migrated, renamed, published).

Trade-off acknowledged in the comment: a line that mixes a historical
marker AND a current-version reference is protected as a whole — a
tolerable false negative (operator can hand-fix in the finalize commit)
versus the worse alternative of letting documentation lies ship.

Verified portability (GNU + BSD sed both accept `-E`, `[[:space:]]+`,
`(A|B|C)` alternation, `[^.]+`, and `/.../!` address negation). Tested
against 14 fixture lines covering historical refs (6 protected) and
current-version refs (8 bumped), all correct.

fix(release): upload all historical helm charts on each release

The helm release step uploaded only the new mockserver-${RELEASE_VERSION}.tgz, relying entirely on the versioned-site cross-bucket mirror to carry historical charts across when a new bucket is created. When that mirror is skipped or fails (as it did for 6.0.0 -> 6.1.0), index.yaml ends up referencing chart files that aren't in the bucket, and `helm pull` / `helm install` return an HTML 404 page for older versions.

Sync every helm/charts/*.tgz on each release so the bucket is self-healing — the repo's helm/charts/ holds the canonical historical set, so any gap left by the cross-bucket mirror is closed here.

Closes #2282

release: split version-references update out of finalize so the website ships current

Root cause of the v6.1.0 wrong-version-on-www.mock-server.com incident:
finalize.sh was the LAST step of the release pipeline AND the only place
that committed "release: update version references to X.Y.Z" (changelog,
_config.yml, package.json files, etc.). The website deploy ran in the
parallel publish group BEFORE finalize, cloned the repo on a fresh agent,
and built Jekyll against the previous version's _config.yml.

Fix: extract the version-references update into its own stage that runs
between Versioned Site and the parallel publish group.

* scripts/release/update-version-references.sh (new) — byte-for-byte
  copy of the extracted block from finalize.sh. Runs the changelog
  promotion, _config.yml bump, package.json / pyproject.toml /
  version.rb edits, and the general sed pass; commits + pushes
  "release: update version references to X.Y.Z". The commit message
  format is unchanged so any downstream annotation/log scrapers keep
  working.
* scripts/release/finalize.sh — now does only the SNAPSHOT pom bump +
  mvn deploy + commit. File header docstring explains the split.
* scripts/release/release.sh (local orchestrator) — fires
  update-version-references inside the component loop immediately after
  maven-central succeeds, so subsequent components (website, helm,
  docker, npm, etc.) see the new refs. New flag
  --skip-update-version-references for explicit opt-out. Post-loop
  guard exits 2 if maven-central was not executed and the operator
  didn't pass the skip flag — prevents silently shipping stale docs in
  partial-run scenarios. Inline comment explains why local ordering of
  maven-plugin (which runs first locally) diverges from CI (where
  maven-plugin is in the parallel publish group) without producing a
  stale-version artifact.
* .buildkite/release-pipeline.yml — new ":bookmark_tabs: Update Version
  References" step between Versioned Site and the parallel publish
  group. Comment on Versioned Site explains why it can safely precede
  the version-refs commit.
* .buildkite/scripts/release-runner.sh — adds update-version-references
  to the top-level stage dispatch.
* docs/operations/release-process.md — file-ownership table now
  attributes most version-bearing files to update-version-references.sh;
  OpenAPI yaml stays attributed to prepare.sh (consistent with the
  inline comment in both old and new code paths).
* docs/operations/release-principles.md — orchestrator description
  updated to include the new stage.

Validated: bash -n on all four shell files, python yaml.safe_load on

second-round PASS.

feat(deps)!: remove Nashorn, migrate JavaScript engine to direct Polyglot API

GraalJS 25.x dropped the JSR-223 javax.script bridge. The previous
createEngine() path (Nashorn-then-GraalJS via ScriptEngineManager)
returned null at runtime, silently breaking every JS template.

Rewrite JavaScriptTemplateEngine to call the GraalVM Polyglot API
directly (Context.newBuilder("js") + Source.create + Value), behind
an Initialization-on-Demand Holder (PolyglotRunner) so the standard
distribution — which does not bundle GraalVM — loads cleanly and
degrades gracefully when GraalVM is absent. Tests run 26-of-26 in
JavaScriptTemplateEngineTest with 0 failures, 0 skipped.

Detail:
- Remove org.openjdk.nashorn:nashorn-core:15.7 from mockserver/pom.xml
  and mockserver-core/pom.xml
- Delete ScriptBindings.java (JSR-223 Bindings impl, no callers)
- Replace Nashorn probe in ExpectationSerializer with GraalVM probe
- Update 4 unit + 1 integration test file: nashornAvailable()
  -> graalJsAvailable() / isPolyglotAvailable(), drop the
  (engineByName==null) ? nullValue() : assert paired branches that
  were silently passing because Nashorn was on the classpath
- Update two denied-class assertion strings to match GraalJS's
  TypeError wording vs Nashorn's ClassNotFoundException
- Drop --add-exports=java.base/sun.security.{x509,util}=ALL-UNNAMED
  from mockserver/pom.xml — repo-wide audit found zero references
- Bump docker/graaljs/Dockerfile GRAALJS_VERSION 24.1.1 -> 25.0.3;
  remove js-scriptengine.jar (dropped in 25.x); migrate icu4j to
  org.graalvm.shadowed coordinates; add jniutils.jar (new transitive
  of truffle-runtime in 25.x)
- Rewrite consumer response_templates.html JavaScript Engine section:
  GraalVM polyglot is the sole engine, NOT bundled in the default
  distribution; use the -graaljs Docker variant or add polyglot+js
  JARs to libs/, or declare them as Maven deps when embedding
- HostAccess.ALL retained — identical security posture to the
  previous polyglot.js.allowHostAccess=true; allowHostClassLookup
  remains the class-denial boundary

Known behavioural shift carried as follow-up:
- BUILT_IN_FUNCTIONS suppliers are now evaluated once per template
  execution rather than lazily per JS variable access (the previous
  ScriptBindings.get() called supplier.get() on each access). For
  uuid/rand_int/etc., reading the variable twice within one template
  now returns the same value. Templates that need per-access
  freshness should call the supplier explicitly via a host helper

BREAKING: Removing org.openjdk.nashorn:nashorn-core; downstream

feat(llm): drift detection — replay cassettes against the live provider

Add detect_llm_drift: replay a recorded LLM cassette against the live provider
(via the runtime-LLM client SPI) and report STRUCTURAL drift — new/removed
fields and type changes in the responses — not semantic differences.

  documents into path->type maps (objects by name, arrays by representative first
  element) and reports added / removed / type-changed paths. Reusable.
- DriftDetector: for each recorded exchange, decode the recorded request via the
  ProviderCodec, build a fresh live request via the runtime LlmClient, send it
  through an injected LlmTransport, and diff the live response shape against the
  recorded one. Fails closed per exchange (missing client/codec, network error,
  non-2xx, non-JSON -> COULD_NOT_CHECK), never throws. DriftReport carries the
  per-exchange outcome and rollup counts.

  none), builds a transient NettyHttpClient transport (bounded wind-down), runs
  the detector, and warns when the cassette provider and resolved backend
  provider differ. Off unless configured; intended for an opt-in/scheduled CI
  lane, never per-commit. No dashboard control (operational/CI tool).

feat(mcp): add run_mcp_contract_test MCP server conformance tester

Adds a deterministic conformance tester for a target MCP (Model Context
Protocol) server reachable over Streamable HTTP, exposed as the
run_mcp_contract_test MCP tool (roadmap item #8).

McpContractTest is a pure orchestrator with an injected JsonRpcExchange
transport, so the check sequence is unit-testable without a network. It
runs the required JSON-RPC handshake and core methods against the
endpoint and validates the SHAPE of each response (JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope
and required result fields), never the semantics of any tool:

- initialize (protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo.name; captures session)
- notifications/initialized (accepted, no error)
- ping (returns a result)
- tools/list (array of tools, each with a name and an object inputSchema)
- unknown method (rejected with JSON-RPC error code -32601)
- tools/call (optional, shape only; skipped unless a toolName is given)

inputSchema 'type' and tools/call 'isError' are treated as optional per
the MCP/JSON-Schema specs, so conformant external servers that omit them
are not failed. The check sequence is self-consistent with MockServer's
own McpStreamableHttpHandler, so it passes against /mockserver/mcp.

The McpToolRegistry handler validates targetUrl, drives the exchange
over the existing HttpURLConnection helper (10s per request), extracts
the session header case-insensitively, and parses JSON or SSE responses.

Docs updated: changelog, docs/code/llm-mocking.md, roadmap status,

fix(cors): make the dashboard work cross-origin (reflect Origin, MCP preflight)

CORSHeaders emitted an empty Access-Control-Allow-Origin when corsAllowOrigin
was blank (the default), and empty Allow-Methods/Allow-Headers when those were
blank — so the dashboard served from another origin (e.g. the dev server on a
different port) was blocked by CORS. Now, when blank:
 - Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflects the request Origin ("*" when none),
 - Access-Control-Allow-Methods / Allow-Headers fall back to sensible defaults
   and reflect the preflight's requested headers.
An explicit corsAllowOrigin is still honoured as an allow-list, the credentials
branch reflects the specific origin, and "*" is never paired with
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

The MCP Streamable-HTTP endpoint (/mockserver/mcp) bypassed CORS entirely; it
now answers the CORS preflight (OPTIONS carrying an Origin) and echoes CORS
headers on every response, exposing Mcp-Session-Id so a cross-origin dashboard
can read the session id returned by initialize. A bare OPTIONS still returns 405.

feat(core): add HttpChaosProfile for HTTP fault injection on mocked responses

Introduce a declarative, top-level expectation 'chaos' block that injects

mocked responses, mirroring the existing LlmChaosProfile conventions.

- HttpChaosProfile model (errorStatus, retryAfter, errorProbability, latency,
  seed) with range/NaN validation; reuses Delay for latency.
- ChaosProbability.shouldInject(prob, seed): shared determinism helper
  (deterministic at 0.0/1.0, reproducible via seed, NaN never injects).
- Expectation.chaos top-level field (clone/equals/hashCode) + client builder
  ForwardChainExpectation.withChaos().
- Serialization via HttpChaosProfileDTO (latency wrapped as DelayDTO, per the
  existing DTO convention) + JSON schema + embedded OpenAPI model.
- Wired into HttpActionHandler at the mocked-response choke point for RESPONSE,
  RESPONSE_TEMPLATE and RESPONSE_CLASS_CALLBACK (error short-circuit, then
  latency); FORWARD/proxy and RESPONSE_OBJECT_CALLBACK paths unchanged.
- Inert when no chaos block is present (no behaviour change for existing
  expectations).

HttpActionHandlerChaosTest (error + latency behaviour). 159 targeted tests green.

feat(core): add count-based stateful faults to HttpChaosProfile

Add a (succeedFirst, failRequestCount) request-count window to
HttpChaosProfile so chaos can be applied statefully by match index,
without any clock dependency:
- succeedFirst (>=0): first N matching requests bypass chaos.
- failRequestCount (>=1, optional): the next M matches are eligible;
  after succeedFirst+M matches the expectation recovers. Omit for
  unlimited faults after the succeed window.
These express 'fail first N then recover' (retry/backoff testing),
'succeed N then fail', and 'fail only the Nth request'.

The window (countWindowEligible) gates BOTH error injection and latency,
and is ANDed with the existing errorProbability/seed, so an expectation
with no count fields behaves exactly as before. The per-request index is
Expectation.getMatchCount() (incremented atomically in consumeMatch),
captured synchronously at dispatch BEFORE the scheduler lambda to avoid a
concurrent-match race. Long arithmetic guards the window upper bound.

Serialization via HttpChaosProfileDTO + JSON schema (minimums) + embedded
OpenAPI. Tests cover fail-first-then-recover, succeed-then-fail, Nth-only,
window-gated latency, and backward compatibility, on mocked and forwarded

fix(metrics): add CORS headers to /mockserver/metrics so the dashboard can fetch cross-origin

build(benchmark): add JMH hot-path benchmark module (not in default build)

Adds mockserver-benchmark, a JMH micro-benchmark module targeting the request-
matching hot path (RequestMatchers.firstMatchingExpectation). It is the
measurement gate for the Part-A allocation optimizations: those wins are
allocation reductions that k6's end-to-end signal cannot prove, so each must
show a before/after gc.alloc.rate.norm delta from `-prof gc` here.

MatchingBenchmark scans a no-match request across expectationCount
(1/10/100/1000), matcherType (EXACT/REGEX/JSON_BODY) and logLevel (INFO/WARN) —
the worst case that forces a full N-matcher scan — with detailedMatchFailures
off (the performance-tuned default). The logLevel axis exposes work that is not
gated by log level today (e.g. the per-field "because" string building).

Deliberately NOT listed in the parent pom <modules>, so `mvn install` and CI
never build it (JMH's annotation processor and the benchmark classpath stay out
of production artifacts). Build and run on demand via ./run.sh (see README).
Java 17, JMH 1.37.

perf(matching): skip "because" string-building when INFO logging is off

failFast() builds the human-readable "did not match because…" message — the
per-field appends and, more expensively, generateHintsForField() — for every
field of every matcher on every request, gated only by !controlPlaneMatcher.
That message is only ever consumed by the INFO log in matches(), so a
performance-tuned deployment (log level reduced below INFO) was allocating and
discarding it. Gate the building on the same isEnabledForInstance(INFO) check.

Unchanged when INFO is on (the message is still built and logged). No diagnostic
is affected: the match evaluation, the MatchDifference population (which powers
detailedMatchFailures / debugMismatch / explainUnmatched / verification), the
fail-fast difference counter and the boolean result all stay unconditional — only
the discarded human-readable string assembly is skipped. The gate mirrors the
existing INFO check in matches() (global log level, not logLevelOverrides), so it
is a behavioural no-op.

(matching the other tests) and stop the watcher before the final assertions

test(core): assert inside retry loop to fix ExpectationFileWatcherTest flake

The prior stabilisation (989a00f36) still failed under CI load with

expectationFileWatcher.stop() and ran a separate, non-polled
assertThat(size==4) + containsInAnyOrder. stop() calls cancel(true), which
interrupts a background addExpectationsFromInitializer reload mid-flight (it
clears then re-adds per file), so the immediately-following bare read could
observe a transient 3-of-4 state.

feat(chaos): add time-based outage windows driven by the controllable clock

Add a self-healing time-based outage window to HttpChaosProfile via two new
fields: outageAfterMillis (chaos becomes active this long after the
expectation's first match) and outageDurationMillis (chaos stays active for
this long then recovers; omit for an unbounded outage). This models a
dependency that is healthy, degrades for a bounded window, then comes back —
and gives the controllable clock (TimeService) its first chaos consumer.

The window is anchored at the expectation's first match: Expectation records a
set-once chaosFirstMatchEpochMillis (via TimeService) on the first
consumeMatch(); it is transient runtime state (not serialized, cloned, or part
of equals/hashCode), mirroring matchCount. HttpChaosProfile.timeWindowEligible
computes eligibility from that anchor and the current clock instant (start
inclusive, end exclusive), returning true when no window is configured
(backward compatible) and failing open when the anchor is unknown. The handler
evaluates the gate once per request at dispatch and collapses the profile to
null outside the window, uniformly disabling drop/error/latency; it composes
with the count window and probability draws (all must pass). Because the window
is measured with the controllable clock, freezing/advancing it via
PUT /mockserver/clock makes outages deterministic in tests with no real waiting.

Wires the fields through the DTO, JSON schema, embedded OpenAPI, the MCP
create_expectation schema, and the Node/Python/Ruby clients, with model,

clock that is reset after each test) plus consumer docs and a changelog entry.

perf(core): cache sorted matcher list in CircularPriorityQueue

toSortedList() previously rebuilt a fresh ArrayList via
stream().collect(Collectors.toList()) on every call, costing one
stream-pipeline construction + N ConcurrentHashMap.get() lookups +
ArrayList allocation per request during the matcher scan.

This adds a volatile List<V> sortedCache that is:
- returned directly on subsequent calls with no mutations (cache hit)
- rebuilt once and cached on a cache miss
- nulled immediately on every mutation: add(), remove(),
  addPriorityKey(), removePriorityKey(), setMaxSize()

The returned list is wrapped in Collections.unmodifiableList to enforce
the contract that callers must not mutate it (both call sites in
RequestMatchers use enhanced-for only, but the unmodifiable wrapper
makes the invariant enforceable at runtime).

fix(core): use Unpooled.wrappedBuffer for zero-copy response body encoding

PooledByteBufAllocator.DEFAULT.buffer() was causing two problems: it
allocated direct buffers (causing UnsupportedOperationException when
tests call buf.array()), and recycled pooled buffers can contain stale
data beyond the written bytes.

Unpooled.wrappedBuffer(bytes) is strictly better: it is zero-copy (no
heap allocation, no data copy), heap-backed so buf.array() works, and
the buffer capacity exactly equals the byte array length so there is no
stale data padding. Unpooled.EMPTY_BUFFER is retained for the empty case.

fix(core): break ConfigurationProperties/MockServerLogger class-init deadlock

ConfigurationProperties and MockServerLogger referenced each other from
their static initializers: ConfigurationProperties.<clinit> eagerly built a
MockServerLogger, while MockServerLogger.<clinit> ran configureLogger() which
read ConfigurationProperties. Two threads first-touching the two classes
concurrently each took one class-init lock and waited for the other - a
permanent deadlock that surfaced as a 30-minute Surefire fork timeout and
forced the parallel unit-test configuration to be reverted (enabled in
7b2fa05aa, reverted in 4fbf52ae0).

Make initialization acyclic from both directions:

- MockServerLogger.<clinit> now installs only the default java.util.logging
  format via installDefaultJavaLoggingFormat(), which never reads
  ConfigurationProperties. The configured log level is applied separately by
  configureLogger() (the format/version output is unchanged, so no logs are
  lost or reformatted). Its clinit-safe fallback uses printStackTrace rather
  than logEvent() to avoid re-reading ConfigurationProperties.
- ConfigurationProperties applies the configured level by calling
  MockServerLogger.configureLogger() from a static block after PROPERTIES is
  loaded (one-way dependency), and its logger is now lazily initialized via a
  holder so its <clinit> no longer constructs a MockServerLogger.

Add ClassInitializationDeadlockTest, which first-touches both classes from two
threads in an isolated child-first class loader. It fails (30s deadlock) on the
old code and passes on the fixed code, guarding against regression before
re-enabling parallel test execution.

test(core): run mockserver-core unit tests in parallel (two-phase Surefire)

Enable Surefire parallel=classes (threadCount=4) for mockserver-core, in two
phases: a parallel phase for the bulk of the suite and a sequential phase
(parallel=none) for the classes that mutate JVM-global state which cannot be
thread-isolated. On this machine the unit suite runs in a few minutes where the
pre-fix clinit deadlock could hang it for the full 30-minute fork timeout.

Root-cause the static-state interference that previously forced parallel to be
reverted, rather than relying solely on an exclusion list:

- UUIDService.fixedUUID, EpochService.fixedTime and TimeService.fixedTime were

  Add explicit global variants (fixedUUIDGlobally / fixedTimeGlobally) for the
  cases that genuinely need cross-thread fixing (timestamps produced on the
  event-log disruptor thread). TimeService keeps the controllable-clock API
  (freeze/advance/reset) untouched, and the fixing rules pin EpochService only
  so they do not interfere with isFrozen() clock-control assertions.

- Add JUnit rules FixedTime, GlobalFixedTime and FixedUUID (ExternalResource)
  that pin in before() and always reset in after(), so a fixed value can never
  leak onto a reused Surefire worker thread. Migrate the test classes (and the

  ParallelStaticStateGuardTest, which fails the build if the parallel-excluded

feat(core): validate LlmChaosProfile numeric fields (match HttpChaosProfile)

LlmChaosProfile previously accepted any numeric values silently, unlike
HttpChaosProfile which already validates its fields in the withX setters.
Retrofit the same validation onto LlmChaosProfile so a malformed profile
fails fast with a clear IllegalArgumentException:

  errorProbability / truncateAtFraction  in [0.0, 1.0] (NaN rejected)
  errorStatus / quotaErrorStatus          in [100, 599]
  quotaLimit / quotaWindowMillis          >= 1

Validation fires when a profile is built via the Java client or parsed
from the chaos MCP parameter (parseChaosProfile already guards each field
by JSON type before calling the setter, so absent fields are unaffected).
Add LlmChaosProfileTest covering accept/reject for every validated field.

feat(core): add HTTP body-corruption chaos faults (truncate + malformed body)

Add two body-corruption faults to HttpChaosProfile for testing client-side
body-parsing resilience:

  truncateBodyAtFraction  keep only a leading fraction (0.0-1.0) of the body
  malformedBody           append a broken-JSON fragment so the body fails to parse

Both are deterministic (no probability draw), applied to the real mocked or
forwarded response via a new applyBodyChaos() helper in HttpActionHandler's two
response choke points, gated by the existing count window and time-based outage
window. Connection-drop and error injection still take priority — an injected
error body is never corrupted — and streaming bodies are skipped. The corrupted
response preserves Content-Type and drops any stale Content-Length so the encoder
re-frames it correctly. Metered as fault_type=truncate / fault_type=malformed.

Exposed in expectation JSON (schema + embedded OpenAPI model), the create_expectation
chaos MCP parameter, and the Java/Node/Python/Ruby clients. The dashboard chaos
composer is a curated subset and is left unchanged (it already omits drop/outage
fields). Covered by mocked + forwarded handler tests, model validation/round-trip
tests, an MCP round-trip test, and Python client round-trip tests.

feat(core): add slow (dribbled) response chaos fault to HttpChaosProfile

Add a slow-response fault: slowResponseChunkSize + slowResponseChunkDelay
trickle the response body to the client in small chunks with a delay between
each (chunked transfer-encoding), for testing read timeouts and slow-network
handling. This is distinct from latency, which delays the whole response by a
fixed amount before sending it.

Both fields are required — a chunk size with no delay just chunks without
slowing. The shared applyResponseChaos helper (renamed from applyBodyChaos; it
now covers body corruption AND slow response) sets a fresh ConnectionOptions
(copying the other fields so the shared original is not mutated) carrying the
chunk settings on the real mocked or forwarded response, which NettyResponseWriter
then dribbles. Deterministic; gated by the count and outage windows; skipped for
streaming; drop/error injection still take priority. Metered fault_type=slow.

Exposed in expectation JSON (schema + embedded OpenAPI, delay $ref), the
create_expectation chaos MCP parameter (with >= 1 validation on size and delay
value), and the Java/Node/Python/Ruby clients. Covered by mocked + forwarded
handler tests, validation/round-trip model tests, an MCP round-trip test, and
Python client round-trip tests.

feat(core): add stateful HTTP request quota (rate limit) to HttpChaosProfile

Add a deterministic fixed-window request quota to the HTTP chaos block — the
counterpart of the existing probabilistic 429 and of the LLM quota. Set quotaName,
quotaLimit and quotaWindowMillis (optional quotaErrorStatus, default 429) and
requests beyond the limit within the window are rejected with that status and the
retryAfter header. Expectations sharing a quotaName share one counter (model an
upstream account limit); the count resets when the window elapses and on server
reset. The quota gate takes priority over the probabilistic error and the body/slow
faults (after connection-drop); metered as fault_type=quota.

Backed by a new process-wide, thread-safe HttpQuotaRegistry (a deliberate parallel
of LlmQuotaRegistry, kept as a separate registry so HTTP and LLM quotas with the
same name do not collide), reset alongside the LLM registry in HttpState.reset().

Exposed in expectation JSON (schema + embedded OpenAPI), the create_expectation
chaos MCP parameter (with >= 1 validation), and the Java/Node/Python/Ruby clients.
Covered by a registry unit test, mocked-response behaviour tests (limit, custom
status, priority over the probabilistic error), validation/round-trip model tests,
an MCP round-trip test, and Python client round-trip tests.
