feat(core): add gradual degradation ramp to HttpChaosProfile

Add a degradationRampMillis field that models a dependency deteriorating over
time: when set, the probabilistic fault rates errorProbability and
dropConnectionProbability ramp linearly from 0 at the expectation's first match
up to their configured values once the ramp window has elapsed, then stay full.
Useful for alerting / SLO error-budget-burn tests.

Implemented with two model methods — degradationFactor(firstMatch, now) (the
ramp factor in [0,1], clock-driven) and copy() (full-field duplicate) — and a
shared HttpActionHandler.effectiveChaos(expectation) helper that replaces the
two duplicated inline outage-window checks and applies the ramp by scaling a
copy's probabilities. The ramp uses the controllable clock so it is
deterministic under freeze/advance; only the probabilistic rates ramp (latency,
body corruption, slow response and quota are unaffected).

Exposed in expectation JSON (schema + embedded OpenAPI), the create_expectation

feat(core): add service-scoped HTTP chaos via /mockserver/serviceChaos

to all matched forward expectations to that host, instead of authoring a chaos
block on every route — the 'break service X' control for running MockServer as a
chaos proxy (plan item G-A4, least-invasive design).

- New process-wide ServiceChaosRegistry (host -> profile), host normalised

- New control-plane endpoint PUT/GET /mockserver/serviceChaos (behind

  {clear:true} clears all; specifying both clear and host is a 400. The chaos
  block is parsed through HttpChaosProfileDTO.buildObject() so range validation
  runs and invalid values return 400. Register/remove/clear are audit-logged.
- Resolution happens only on the matched-forward path: HttpActionHandler falls
  back to the host-keyed profile when a matched forward expectation has no chaos
  of its own; an expectation's own chaos always wins (even when gated off by its

Exposed via the REST control-plane endpoint (the HttpChaosProfile model is
already in all four clients; per-client convenience wrappers and an MCP tool are

unregistered-host) and endpoint tests (register+get, remove, clear, conflict,
invalid-profile, missing-host).

Add convenience wrappers over the PUT/GET /mockserver/serviceChaos control-plane
endpoint so service-scoped chaos can be driven from each client and from AI

  Java   MockServerClient.setServiceChaos(host, HttpChaosProfile) / removeServiceChaos(host)

ServiceChaosRegistryTest mutates the process-wide ServiceChaosRegistry singleton
(shared with HttpState.reset and the matched-forward chaos path), so it must run

test(core): harden test parallel-safety (PortFactory, EchoServer queue, @TempDir)

Follow-on robustness for the parallel mockserver-core test run, fixing the
remaining static/shared-state and filesystem hazards:

- PortFactory: remove the sleep(250) that ran after closing the probe sockets -
  it only widened the window between releasing a port and the caller binding it.
  Each socket is now opened with setReuseAddress(true), bound, recorded, stored
  in the array immediately (so the finally block closes it even if bind throws),
  and all are closed in a finally. Callers still handle BindException (the only
  fully race-free option is binding the real socket); behaviour and the public
  findFreePort()/findFreePorts(int) signatures are unchanged.

- EchoServer: the shared NextResponse queue was a LinkedList mutated from test
  threads while the Netty handler consumed it - make it a ConcurrentLinkedQueue
  and switch EchoServerHandler from a non-atomic isEmpty()+remove() (which could
  throw NoSuchElementException) to an atomic poll()+null-check. Structural queue
  operations are now thread-safe; note that a single EchoServer instance shared
  across concurrent test classes can still interleave logically - isolating that
  needs per-class instances, a separate change.

- Tests: ExpectationFileWatcherTest and VelocityTemplateEngineTest wrote files
  to the working directory (mockserverInitialization*.json, testInputFile.txt),
  polluting CWD and risking collisions under parallel runs. Move both into a
  @Rule TemporaryFolder (the Velocity import is referenced by absolute path so it
  stays CWD-independent).

feat(core): add TTL / auto-revert (dead-man's switch) to service-scoped chaos

Add an optional ttlMillis to a service-scoped chaos registration so the chaos
auto-reverts after that many milliseconds — a dead-man's switch so a fault
self-heals even if the matching clear is never sent (e.g. an external chaos
orchestrator crashes mid-experiment), and the one-shot time-box form: a single
call breaks a host for a bounded window.

ServiceChaosRegistry now stores entries with an optional expiry, using an
injected clock (the singleton uses TimeService::currentTimeMillis — real time by
default, deterministic under PUT /mockserver/clock, consistent with the outage
and degradation windows). Expiry is overflow-safe (saturating add) and applied
lazily on lookup, so the matched-forward path auto-heals transparently. GET
/mockserver/serviceChaos now reports a ttlRemainingMillis countdown per
TTL-bearing host. Backward compatible: put(host, profile) keeps no expiry.

Exposed via PUT /mockserver/serviceChaos (ttlMillis, >=1 else 400), the
manage_service_chaos MCP tool, and the Java/Node/Python/Ruby clients
(setServiceChaos(host, chaos, ttlMillis) / ttl_millis). Covered by registry unit
tests (expiry, no-expiry-when-0, ttlRemaining, saturating-overflow), an
end-to-end forward-path auto-revert test via clock freeze/advance, endpoint
tests (ttl + GET countdown + <1 rejection), an MCP test, and client tests.

feat(metrics): add active service-scoped chaos gauge (Prometheus + OTLP)

Expose mock_server_active_service_chaos — a Prometheus gauge reporting the
number of hosts with a currently-active service-scoped chaos profile — so an
operator can alert on "chaos is still live" and watch it drop to 0 as profiles
are cleared or their TTLs lapse. The natural companion to the TTL/auto-revert
dead-man's switch: the switch bounds each fault, the gauge confirms the fleet
is clean.

Implemented as a GaugeWithCallback that reads ServiceChaosRegistry.activeCount()
at scrape time rather than tracking the value imperatively, so TTL auto-revert
(which removes a profile lazily, with no put/remove call) is reflected without
any extra plumbing. activeCount() counts non-expired entries without allocating
a snapshot map and iterates the ConcurrentHashMap weakly-consistently (an
approximation acceptable for a gauge). Registered only when metricsEnabled, and
mirrored over OTLP by OtelMetricsExporter so OTLP-only consumers can observe it.

Covered by MetricsTest (gauge present; reflects live registry across
put/remove/reset; accessor safe when disabled), ServiceChaosRegistryTest
(activeCount excludes TTL-expired entries via a fake clock), and
OtelMetricsExporterTest (gauge exported). Docs: chaos_testing.html metrics
table + PromQL, docs/code/metrics.md, changelog.

feat(ui): add a Chaos tab for managing service-scoped chaos

The dashboard could show that service-scoped chaos was active (the metrics

fix(core): emit CORS headers on service-scoped chaos responses

The dashboard's Chaos tab calls GET/PUT /mockserver/serviceChaos. When the
dashboard is served from a different origin (e.g. the UI dev server on :3000
hitting MockServer on :1080) the GET failed with a CORS error: the control-plane
API only emits CORS headers when enableCORSForAPI is set, and a simple GET
triggers no preflight to auto-enable it, so the response carried no
Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

Add CORS headers to the serviceChaos GET and PUT responses unconditionally, via
a CORSHeaders field on HttpState and a withDashboardCORS helper — mirroring the
always-on CORS already applied by the metrics (MetricsHandler) and MCP endpoints
for exactly this dashboard-served-cross-origin case. CORSHeaders.addCORSHeaders
is idempotent (setHeaderIfNotAlreadyExists), so it composes safely with the
conditional CORS ResponseWriter may also apply; control-plane authentication is
unaffected (it gates the request before the response is built); and the PUT's
OPTIONS preflight is still handled by the existing global mechanism.

Tested in HttpStateTest with the default configuration (enableCORSForAPI off):
the GET and PUT responses carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflecting the
request Origin.

fix(core): record mock drift — forward-match stubs instead of reverse-filter matching

Mock drift detection never recorded anything end-to-end. HttpActionHandler.analyseDrift
(the only caller of HttpState.allMatchingExpectation) used
RequestMatchers.retrieveActiveExpectations(request), which treats its argument as a
FILTER: it builds a matcher FROM the concrete incoming request and reverse-matches it
against each expectation's bare definition. Because the concrete forwarded request
carries headers (content-type, host, accept, …) that bare {method,path} stubs lack,
those headers became required match criteria and nothing matched — so the baseline
stub was never found and no DriftRecord was ever produced.

Fix: add RequestMatchers.retrieveExpectationsMatchingRequest(RequestDefinition) doing
FORWARD matching ("does each active expectation's matcher match this concrete
request?", via httpRequestMatcher.matches(request) — the same direction used when
serving), returning ALL matches so drift can find a lower-priority baseline alongside
a higher-priority forward. allMatchingExpectation now calls it. The behaviour change is
scoped to drift (that method has no other caller). It is read-only — unlike
retrieveActiveExpectations it does not submit matcher removals.

Why tests missed it: the F3 DriftAnalyzer tests call analyse() directly with hand-built
objects, never exercising the forward → analyseDrift → allMatchingExpectation wiring.
Added RequestMatchersForwardMatchingTest (5 tests) covering the bug class: a
header-bearing concrete request must still match a bare stub via forward matching, and
the old reverse-filter method returns empty for the same input (pins the distinction).
Verified end-to-end against a running server: the demo now records 14 drift records.

feat(core): incremental OpenAPI sync — make PUT /mockserver/openapi idempotent

Re-importing an OpenAPI spec now updates expectations in place and prunes
operations no longer in the spec, instead of creating fresh duplicates each
time. Generated expectations get a stable id `openapi:<specKey>:<operationId>`
(specKey = sanitized spec title, or a hash of the spec when untitled; a numeric
suffix disambiguates multiple expectations per operation). On import,
HttpState.add(OpenAPIExpectation) computes the spec's namespace prefixes, prunes
existing expectations in those namespaces that are absent from the new set, then
upserts the rest. Pure diff logic lives in OpenApiSyncPlanner (unit-tested).

This changes /openapi from additive to incremental — the common single-import
flow is unaffected; re-imports of the same spec are now clean instead of
duplicating. Non-OpenAPI and differently-titled expectations are untouched.

feat(grpc): built-in gRPC Server Reflection (v1 + v1alpha)

Add GrpcServerReflectionHandler, mirroring the built-in health-check handler:
it answers grpc.reflection.v1(alpha).ServerReflection/ServerReflectionInfo
without a client-side proto, serving list_services, file_containing_symbol and
file_by_filename from the loaded GrpcProtoDescriptorStore (manual protobuf via
CodedInput/OutputStream — no new dependencies). Wired into the netty gRPC path
alongside the health handler; unknown symbols/files return NOT_FOUND, unsupported
request types UNIMPLEMENTED.

Limitation (documented): the gRPC path is buffered-unary, so this serves a single
ServerReflectionRequest per HTTP/2 request (covers `grpcurl list` and single
symbol/file lookups); fully-interactive bidi-streaming reflection is not supported
by the current pipeline.

feat(async): AsyncAPI-driven Kafka/MQTT broker mocking (mockserver-async, MVP)

disabled) with a self-signed cert and ALPN "h3". MVP request handler echoes the
:method/:path to prove the stack; full mock-pipeline bridging is a documented
follow-up. Fully isolated from the existing TCP/HTTP(1.1/2)/gRPC pipeline — zero
impact when disabled.

Test starts the server and exchanges a request via netty's HTTP/3 client; it
assume-skips when the BoringSSL/QUIC native is unavailable so it never fails a
build on unsupported platforms (it passes on macOS aarch64 here). See
docs/code/http3.md for enablement, native-platform requirements and MVP bounds.

feat(core): request-level OpenTelemetry spans via RequestSpans (F8)

(static volatile Tracer installed by GenAiSpanExporter, isEnabled() short-circuit,
fully fail-soft). Spans carry http.request.method/route, http.response.status_code,

feat(netty): route HTTP/3 through the full request pipeline (U4)

Lift HTTP/3 from an echo-only MVP to pipeline-integrated. A QUIC stream's
headers + data frames are assembled into an HttpRequest and routed through the
same HttpState/HttpActionHandler path as HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (expectation
matching, recording, proxy, callbacks), then the HttpResponse is written back as
HTTP/3 frames. Wire Http3Server into the MockServer lifecycle (start when
http3Port>0, stop on shutdown) with fail-soft startup — an unavailable native
QUIC provider or bind failure logs a warning and leaves the main server running,
never crashing it. Reuse MockServer's configured TLS certificate (self-signed
only as a fallback). Release the body CompositeByteBuf via handlerRemoved, shut
the event-loop group on start failure, share a single Metrics instance per
server, and warn on unsupported streaming bodies. HTTP/3 stays off by default
and is still labelled experimental because the underlying QUIC codec is an
upstream Netty incubator artifact.

feat(async): production-grade AsyncAPI broker mocking (U3)

Lift mockserver-async from MVP to production-grade:

- REST control-plane: PUT/GET /mockserver/asyncapi to load an AsyncAPI spec and
  start mocking, and report status + recorded messages; cleared on reset. Routed
  via a core-side SPI (AsyncApiControlPlane + AsyncApiControlPlaneRegistry) with
  the implementation in mockserver-async self-registered by reflection at startup
  (501 when the module is absent), so mockserver-core keeps no dependency on
  mockserver-async.
- Consumer/subscriber mocking: Kafka + MQTT subscribers record received messages
  (key, headers, timestamp) into a bounded FIFO store (evict-oldest, cap 1000) so
  memory stays bounded. KafkaConsumer is confined to a single poll thread with
  subscribe/unsubscribe queued as pending ops and wakeup()-based clean shutdown.
- Schema validation of generated and consumed messages against channel JSON
  Schemas, reusing core's JsonSchemaValidator.
- Configurable Kafka record keys + headers and MQTT QoS (0/1/2) + binary payloads.
- Build wiring: mockserver-async bundled (optional dep) into mockserver-netty and
  the no-dependencies shade so the control-plane is reachable at runtime.

Schema-aware example generation honours enum/default/const/min/max/format. Load
failures return 400 and roll back partial broker setup. Deferred (documented):
dashboard UI, live-broker tests, SASL/TLS, correlation IDs, client-java helpers.

feat: production-grade service mesh / sidecar mode (F14)

Lift F14 from a static route-builder + scaffold to a working sidecar:

- xDS RDS gRPC server: a real Envoy-compatible Route Discovery Service over
  HTTP/2 on xdsPort (when xdsEnabled), translating active expectations into an
  envoy.config.route.v3.RouteConfiguration. Wire format is hand-coded
  (ProtoWriter/ProtoReader + XdsProtoMessages) to avoid the heavyweight
  io.envoyproxy.controlplane:api / grpc-java dependencies; field numbers match
  the Envoy v3 protos and are pinned by a golden-bytes test. ProtoReader is
  hardened against malformed client input (bounds-checked skips). Supported
  subset is full-state RDS responses; delta xDS, LDS/CDS/EDS/ADS and
  watch-on-change are documented as not implemented.

- Transparent proxy: SoOriginalDstHelper reads the original destination of
  iptables-REDIRECTed connections from /proc/net/nf_conntrack (JNI-free, capped
  scan), platform-gated to Linux with a graceful Host-header fallback and no
  fabricated destinations. TransparentProxyHandler sets the channel's remote
  socket so the existing forward path targets the original destination; added to
  the pipeline only when transparentProxyEnabled.

- Lifecycle: the xDS server starts/stops with MockServer, fail-soft (a bind
  failure logs and leaves the main server running), with an idempotent stop.

- Helm: optional iptables init container (NET_ADMIN) that excludes MockServer's
  own egress by UID before REDIRECT to avoid a redirect loop, NET_ADMIN on the
  app container for transparent proxy, and the xDS port exposed — all gated on
  the sidecar values.

SO_ORIGINAL_DST is Linux-only and unit-tested cross-platform (integration tested
on Linux only).

response — status (equal), headers (subset), body (JSON-structural else string) —
returning a per-interaction pass/fail summary: 202 when all pass, 406 otherwise,
400 on malformed input. Non-static actions (forward/callback/template) are
flagged unverifiable. Consumer + internal docs updated.

feat(grpc): gRPC-Web support for browser clients via localized translation (G9)

Let gRPC-Web clients call the existing gRPC mocking. A localized translation
layer detects application/grpc-web[+proto] and application/grpc-web-text
(base64), feeds the length-prefixed message through the existing gRPC match path
(GrpcFrameCodec / GrpcToHttpRequestHandler), and re-frames the response as
gRPC-Web: message frames followed by a 0x80 trailer frame carrying
grpc-status/grpc-message (GrpcStatusMapper), base64-encoded for -text. gRPC
handlers are also added to the HTTP/1.1 pipeline so gRPC-Web works over HTTP/1.1,
and isGrpcContentType now excludes application/grpc-* to avoid misrouting.
Connect protocol is documented as not-yet-supported. No new dependencies;
existing gRPC integration tests unchanged.

fix(core): list DNS and binary expectations in active-expectation retrieval

DNS and binary expectations were created successfully but never appeared
in active-expectation listings (the dashboard Mocks page and
PUT /mockserver/retrieve?type=ACTIVE_EXPECTATIONS). gRPC mocks, which use
HTTP-shaped request matchers, were unaffected, which made the bug look
DNS-specific.

Both retrieveActiveExpectations and retrieveRequestMatchers reverse-match
each expectation against the supplied filter. The dashboard and the REST
retrieve endpoint pass an empty HttpRequest (not null) when listing all
expectations, so the HTTP-style else branch was taken. An HTTP/OpenAPI
matcher only matches HttpRequest/OpenAPIDefinition definitions and returns
false for DnsRequestDefinition/BinaryRequestDefinition, so those
expectations were silently dropped.

An HTTP-shaped filter has no vocabulary to describe non-HTTP protocol
expectations, so it must not exclude them. A new notFilterableByRequest
helper lets DNS/binary expectations bypass an HTTP/OpenAPI filter and
always be listed, while a same-protocol filter still narrows normally.

test(ui): use userEvent delay:null in composerKinds to fix CI timeout

The "preserves a user-customised path when leaving gRPC" test typed input with
userEvent's default per-keystroke delay, taking ~5s and timing out on the slower
CI agent (Test timed out in 5000ms). Switch all userEvent.setup() calls in
composerKinds.test.tsx to setup({ delay: null }), removing the artificial typing
delay — the slow test now runs in ~0.9s. Test-only change.

feat(core): expose build-time git commit hash on /mockserver/status

The status endpoint and the Prometheus mock_server_build_info metric now
report the abbreviated git commit hash the artifact was built from,
alongside the existing version and group/artifact id.

The hash is captured at build time by the git-commit-id-maven-plugin
(initialize phase) into the ${git.commit.id.abbrev} property, which the
templating-maven-plugin substitutes into the generated Version class. It
is populated for SNAPSHOT and RELEASE builds produced from a git checkout
and degrades to an empty value when no git metadata is available (e.g. a
source tarball), in which case the field is omitted from the status JSON
and the metric label reports "unknown".

Inside a linked git worktree the resolved hash is that of the shared
repository HEAD rather than the worktree's own HEAD; single-working-tree
clones (CI and the release pipeline, which is what ships) resolve correctly.

test(ui): raise vitest global testTimeout to 20s to fix CI-load timeouts

The composerKinds "preserves a user-customised path when leaving gRPC" test still
timed out (5140ms) on the loaded CI agent even after switching to userEvent
delay:null — the cost is render + multiple kind-switches + React re-renders under
CI CPU contention, not just typing. Raise the global vitest testTimeout/hookTimeout
to 20s so CI-load latency does not cause spurious "Test timed out in 5000ms"
failures across the UI suite.

feat(openapi): resolve callback runtime expressions at fire-time (G15)

OpenAPI callback runtime expressions ({$request.body#/...}, {$request.query.x},
{$request.header.x}, {$request.path.x}, {$request.method}, {$url}) were stripped
to empty at spec-conversion time. Now OpenAPIConverter preserves them verbatim in
the generated after-action request, and HttpActionHandler.dispatchAfterAction
resolves them against the triggering request (OpenApiRuntimeExpressionResolver)
just before firing — a strict no-op (same instance, no clone) when no expressions
are present, so existing webhook after-actions are unaffected. Response
expressions ($response.*) remain out of scope (response not available at
fire-time). Docs updated.

feat(graphql): GraphQL subscriptions over WebSocket (graphql-transport-ws) (G8)

Fuse the existing GraphQL AST matcher with bidirectional WebSocket support to mock
GraphQL subscriptions. A new GraphQLSubscriptionHandler implements the
graphql-transport-ws protocol (also accepts legacy graphql-ws):
connection_init->connection_ack, ping->pong, subscribe (AST-matched query) ->
ordered next... then complete, error on no match, client complete cancels the
stream. Adds a graphqlSubscriptionFilter (GraphQLBody) to HttpWebSocketResponse;
the existing messages sequence (with per-message delays) supplies the pushed
payloads. No new dependencies. Docs + schema updated.

feat(llm): emit AWS event-stream framing for Bedrock streaming (G14 part)

Bedrock InvokeModelWithResponseStream uses the vnd.amazon.eventstream binary
format; MockServer previously did not, so raw (non-SDK) Bedrock streaming
clients could not parse responses. Add BedrockEventStreamEncoder
(prelude + headers + payload + prelude/message CRC32s, each chunk JSON
base64-wrapped in {"bytes":...}) and a third StreamingFormat AWS_EVENT_STREAM;
BedrockCodec declares it and the format-aware write layer emits concatenated
event-stream messages with content-type application/vnd.amazon.eventstream,
preserving inter-chunk streaming-physics timing. SSE/NDJSON providers are
unchanged. SigV4 runtime-client signing remains a documented follow-up.
No new dependencies (java.util.zip.CRC32 + Base64).

fix(graphql): preserve subscription fields + enforce connection_init (review)

Address review-final BLOCK on G8. createMatcher dropped explicitly-configured
GraphQLBody.fields when selectionSetMatchType was null (it read fields from the
freshly-reassigned body). Extract normaliseSubscriptionBody() that captures the
original fields BEFORE defaulting to AST_SUBSET, with a regression test. Also
enforce graphql-transport-ws ordering (ignore subscribe before connection_init,
using the previously-unread connectionInitialised flag) and null-guard
handshaker.close().

feat(proxy): pluggable original-destination resolver chain + PROXY-protocol v1 (G5)

Generalise transparent-proxy original-destination resolution into an ordered,
pluggable chain (CompositeOriginalDestinationResolver, first non-null wins), with
conntrack extracted as a named strategy (no behaviour change to the existing
Linux sidecar path). Add a byte-level ProxyProtocolOriginalDestinationHandler that
parses PROXY protocol v1 (hand-rolled, no new dependency, fail-safe pass-through
for non-PROXY bytes) and sets the original destination — enabling transparent
interception behind AWS Gateway Load Balancer / HAProxy. Native strategies
(SO_ORIGINAL_DST getsockopt, TPROXY, eBPF) and PROXY v2 are documented as
deferred. Off by default (transparentProxyEnabled).

feat(core): pluggable ExpectationStoreFactory seam for clustered state (G10 phase 1)

Introduce ExpectationStoreFactory — a small SPI/registry (mirroring the
AsyncApiControlPlane/DriftStore/WasmStore pattern) through which HttpState
obtains its RequestMatchers, instead of constructing it inline. The default
factory is the standard in-memory RequestMatchers constructor, so behaviour is
identical when no override is registered (verified: HttpStateTest 121 +
RequestMatchersTest green, 0 regressions).

This establishes the construction substitution point for clustered shared state:
an optional backend (phase 2 — embedded Infinispan data grid) can register a
factory returning a clustering-aware RequestMatchers so a MockServer fleet shares
expectations. Phase 2 additionally needs the CircularPriorityQueue storage made
overridable (documented as deferred). No new dependency; no behaviour change.

fix(ui): correct Mocks-page Java/JSON code generation for all action types

An adversarial review of the composer code generation found the generated
Java client snippets did not compile against the real MockServerClient API
for several types, and one JSON payload diverged from the server model:

- DNS expectations emitted a bare request() instead of a dnsRequest()
  matcher, losing dnsName/dnsType/dnsClass entirely.
- SSE, WebSocket, binary, DNS and gRPC-stream responses used a
  .respond(...) overload that does not exist; the client exposes
  respondWithSse / respondWithWebSocket / respondWithBinary /
  respondWithDns / respondWithGrpcStream.
- forward-with-fallback used .forward(...) instead of the
  .forwardWithFallback(...) method.
- chaos chained .withChaos(...) after the terminal action (which returns
  Expectation[]); it must precede the action on the ForwardChainExpectation.
- the GraphQL body JSON used the key "graphql" instead of the
  server-canonical "query", so the query text was dropped on the server.

Also closes Java/JSON parity gaps (SSE retry, gRPC headers, DNS answer
records) and rewrites Java import emission as a computed set so the
snippets compile standalone (body-matcher factories, Scheme, TemplateType,
callback, dnsRecord, WebSocket matcher imports, Base64, Delay).

Adds standardCodegenJavaCorrectness.test.ts pinning the corrected Java and
updates the GraphQL body test to assert the "query" key.

fix(ui): correct LLM-conversation/expectation code generation

Adversarial review of the LLM-mock code generation (the LLM Conversation
kind on the Mocks page) found Java that would not compile, JSON the server
would reject, and a lossy round-trip:

- single-expectation Java referenced the Provider enum without importing

- conversation Java referenced ParsedMessage.Role without importing

- conversation Java emitted whole-number Double chaos args (errorProbability

- the round-trip parser read streaming from the httpLlmResponse top level,
  but it lives inside completion (Completion.streaming) where the generator
  and server put it; loading an existing conversation lost the flag.

refactor: remove inert bespoke replay feature (F13)

The replay feature was a non-functional placeholder: ReplayOrchestrator's
request sender threw UnsupportedOperationException, so PUT/GET
/mockserver/replay could never actually replay traffic. Replay is already
expressible through a primary action plus after-actions, and the
record -> reusable-mocks workflow already ships, so the bespoke orchestrator
added surface area with no working behaviour.

Removed:
- org.mockserver.mock.replay package (ReplayOrchestrator, RecordedRequest,
  ReplayReport, ReplayResult, ReplayResultCallback) + tests
- PUT/GET /mockserver/replay control-plane routes and handler methods in
  HttpState, and the replay reset() hook
- UI ReplayDialog component, lib/replay.ts, and the Replay button/icon/state
  in TrafficInspector (search field keeps its right alignment)
- "Replay Under Chaos" section in docs/code/request-processing.md

Non-breaking: the routes returned errors and the UI action was inert. The
separate record-retrieval feature (retrieveRecordedRequests) is unaffected.

feat: add beforeActions to expectations (multi-action increment 1)

Introduces `beforeActions` on an expectation: side-effect actions that run
*before* the primary response, complementing the existing fire-and-forget
`afterActions`. This is the first increment toward native multi-action
expectations (tee / shadow / fan-out / gate orchestration) and is fully
backward compatible — an expectation without `beforeActions` behaves exactly
as before.

A before-action reuses the existing AfterAction type plus three new optional
controls (meaningful only for before-actions; ignored by after-actions):
- blocking (default true): the response waits for the action to complete
- timeout: max wait for a blocking action (falls back to maxSocketTimeout)
- failurePolicy: FAIL_FAST (abort + 502) or BEST_EFFORT (log + continue, default)

Only httpRequest (webhook) before-actions are awaited; callback before-actions
and non-blocking before-actions are dispatched fire-and-forget (a WARN is
logged if blocking=true is set on a callback). The before-run + primary
dispatch are wrapped in scheduler.submit so any blocking wait runs off the
event loop (async) or inline (synchronous), mirroring forward-action
threading. On a fail-fast abort the expectation is still post-processed so
matcher state (responseInProgress, times exhaustion) is cleaned up.

Touches the model (AfterAction, FailurePolicy, Expectation), serialization
(AfterActionDTO, ExpectationDTO), JSON schema (afterAction.json,
expectation.json), the Java client (ForwardChainExpectation), and dispatch
(HttpActionHandler), with dispatch + serialization round-trip tests.

feat: mirror beforeActions in node, python and ruby clients

Adds the `beforeActions` expectation field and the three new AfterAction
controls (blocking, timeout, failurePolicy) to the non-Java clients so they
can produce and parse the new JSON, matching the Java server and client.

- node (mockServer.d.ts): beforeActions on the expectation type; blocking /
  timeout / failurePolicy on the AfterAction interface
- python (models.py): before_actions on Expectation + the new controls on
  AfterAction, with to_dict/from_dict (camelCase keys, single-object-to-list
  coercion); round-trip + omit-when-unset tests
- ruby (models.rb): same on Expectation + AfterAction via to_h/from_hash;
  single-object beforeActions/afterActions now normalise to an array on parse

All additive and optional — clients that never set beforeActions are
unaffected.

  beforeActions field, and the three before-only controls.

Docs only — no behaviour change. Full jekyll build not run (jekyll gem not

feat(ui): add before & after actions to the expectation composer

Exposes the server's beforeActions/afterActions on the Mocks-page composer,
following the existing chaos-panel pattern. Webhook (httpRequest) side-effects

- standardCodegen.ts: StandardSideEffectAction type + sideEffects on

  beforeActions/afterActions arrays (minimal emission — blocking only when

  HttpRequest model has no top-level host field); sideEffectsFromExpectation
  reads them back (Host header tolerant of object/array/legacy forms); Java +

- ComposerView.tsx: collapsible "Before & after actions" section with an

- tests: standardCodegen unit tests (emission, round-trip, Java/curl previews)
  and ComposerView panel tests.

docs: fix webhook host in before/after action examples

The webhook examples used a non-existent top-level "host" field on
httpRequest. The webhook destination is derived from the Host header, so the
JSON examples now use "headers": { "Host": [...] } and the Java example uses
.withHeader("Host", ...), matching the HttpRequest model and the UI composer.

style(ui): format nested builders in generated Java across indented lines

Deeply-nested builder calls in the Mocks-page Java code generation were
emitted as a single long line that overflowed the preview, e.g. the DNS
answer record:

    .withAnswerRecord(dnsRecord().withName("..").withType(..).withTtl(..).withValue(".."))

They are now broken across indented lines to match the surrounding builder
style:

    .withAnswerRecord(
        dnsRecord()
            .withName("..")
            .withType(..)
            .withTtl(..)
            .withValue("..")
    )

Applied to the DNS answer record and WebSocket message matcher (standard
codegen) and to withNormalization / respondingWith / withChaos (LLM
conversation codegen). Output is unchanged semantically — only whitespace.
Tests assert the multi-line structure and a 120-char line-length ceiling.

feat(proxy): parse PROXY protocol v2 (binary) original-destination headers

ProxyProtocolOriginalDestinationHandler previously parsed only PROXY protocol
v1 (text) despite its docstring claiming v1/v2. Add v2 (binary) support so
MockServer recovers the original destination behind load balancers that speak
v2 (e.g. AWS GWLB with send-proxy-v2, HAProxy send-proxy-v2).

The handler now dispatches on the first inbound byte: 0x0D -> candidate v2
(the 12-byte binary signature begins with 0x0D, which cannot start a v1
header, HTTP request, or TLS record); 'P' -> v1 (unchanged). For v2 it
confirms the signature, reads the 16-byte prefix (version+command,
family+transport, big-endian uint16 address length), bounds the address
length, waits for the full block, and extracts the destination for the PROXY
command on AF_INET and AF_INET6. LOCAL (health-check), AF_UNIX/AF_UNSPEC, and
version != 2 are consumed or passed through with no destination, deferring to
downstream resolution. All v1 behaviour is preserved; attribute-setting is
refactored into a shared applyOriginalDst. No new dependency — the binary
format is hand-parsed (no netty-codec-haproxy).

Adds 8 v2 tests (INET, INET6, LOCAL, UNIX, fragmented, signature-mismatch,
version-mismatch, oversized length) and updates the service-mesh consumer doc
and netty-pipeline internal doc to state v1+v2 are supported.

fix(ui): preserve response headers and unlimited-times on Mocks edit-in-place

Editing an existing static response and re-saving it silently dropped every
response header except Content-Type, because the static panel could not
represent arbitrary headers. Add a "Response headers" field (StaticState +
StandardStaticState), prefill it from the expectation (excluding content-type,
which keeps its own field), and emit the headers in both the JSON payload
(merged as a {name:[values]} map) and the Java snippet (.withHeader). The
dedicated content-type field wins if the user also types one in the textarea
(case-insensitive dedupe), so it is never emitted twice.

Also: the transition-times prefill now shows 0 for an explicitly unlimited
expectation rather than its (irrelevant) remainingTimes count, and the
WebSocket frame-matcher prefill uses denottable() so it tolerates both the
plain-string wire form and a NottableString object form.

Assumption: httpResponse.headers is a {name:[values]} map (KeysToMultiValues),
confirmed against the server serializer.

fix(ui): read scenario fields from the expectation top level in scripted-turns

gatherScriptedTurns read scenarioName / scenarioState / newScenarioState from
inside httpLlmResponse, but they are top-level Expectation fields (ExpectationDTO)
— the same location sessionGrouping already reads. Against real server payloads
the nested read returned undefined, so scripted-turn gathering produced nothing.
Also read `streaming` from inside `completion` (Completion.streaming) rather than
the httpLlmResponse top level. Test fixture corrected to the real payload shape.

fix(ui): correct LLM token usage and cost across providers

The OpenAI Responses API reports token usage as input_tokens / output_tokens
(like Anthropic), not the Chat Completions prompt_tokens / completion_tokens,
but every reader treated openai_responses usage as the Chat shape — so token
counts and cost rendered as zero/blank. Add an OpenAiResponsesUsage type and
read input_tokens / output_tokens for that provider in getTokenSummary, the
usage detail, and the conversation view.

Also: token extraction now reports "no usage data" when both counts are absent
rather than a misleading 0 tokens / $0.00; and Bedrock Claude cost now resolves
because the anthropic pricing branch strips the Bedrock model-id prefix
(anthropic.<model> / us.anthropic.<model>), which parseTraffic classifies as
kind 'anthropic'.

fix(ui): cover all providers in trajectory (Compare Runs) extraction

Trajectory extraction only handled Anthropic and OpenAI Chat: it read `choices`
for openai_responses (which exposes `output`), and ignored Gemini and Ollama
entirely, so Compare Runs could report structurally different runs as identical.
Extract tool calls / tokens / stop reason for openai_responses (output[]
function_call, input_tokens/output_tokens), Gemini (candidates parts
functionCall, finishReason), and Ollama (responseMessage.tool_calls), mirroring
expectationFromCapture.

fix(ui): route REST and WebSocket through a base-path-aware URL and keep reconnecting

REST calls built their URL via buildBaseUrl (protocol://host:port) with no base
path, while the WebSocket injected the dashboard's context path — so behind a
reverse proxy / servlet context the live stream worked but every action button
(clear, import/export, chaos, metrics, MCP, drift, debug-mismatch) 404'd.
ConnectionParams now carries a derived basePath (overridable via ?basePath=),
buildBaseUrl appends it, and the WebSocket plus the previously hand-rolled
builders in ComposerView / LibraryView / useDebugMismatch / clearServer all go
through it — one source of truth for the server origin.

Also: the WebSocket no longer gives up permanently after 10 attempts; it keeps
retrying at a capped 15s backoff so a server that restarts reconnects on its own
(onopen resets the counter and clears the error).

fix(ui): ignore Cmd/Ctrl+K and Cmd/Ctrl+L while typing or composing

Cmd/Ctrl+L maps to a full server reset and fired globally, so a stray keypress
while typing in any field (or during IME composition) could wipe the server.
The mod-key shortcuts now no-op when the event targets an input/textarea/select/
contenteditable or an IME is composing; Escape (toggle filter) is likewise
guarded so it does not fire from within a field.

fix(ui): select inspected traffic by stable key, not array index

The Traffic inspector keyed its detail pane on a positional index into the
filtered list, but the store fully replaces the traffic arrays on every
WebSocket refresh and the list is re-derived on each search keystroke — so the
stored index pointed at a different (or missing) request after any update, and
the user routinely inspected the wrong row. Select by the stable item key
instead (store field selectedTrafficKey), and clear it on clearUI.

fix(ui): make gRPC error-status chaos actually inject; clarify probability units

Registering a gRPC fault with only an error status code was a silent no-op:
the server injects a gRPC fault only when errorProbability > 0, but the form
left it unset. buildGrpcChaosProfile now defaults errorProbability to 1
(always inject) when a status code is chosen and no probability is given,
matching the HTTP chaos semantics. The error/drop probability inputs are now
labelled "(0–1)" so the fractional unit is explicit (the summary chips render
them as a percentage). buildGrpcChaosProfile / EMPTY_GRPC_CHAOS_FORM are
exported for unit testing.

fix(ui): label latency panel as cumulative and guard mismatch score divide-by-zero

The Metrics latency panel charts a histogram quantile that is cumulative since
server start, but was labelled "Request latency (since start)" / "p95 ms" which
reads like a windowed time-series; relabel it "cumulative since server start" /
"p95 ms (cumulative)" so a near-flat converging line is not misread as live
latency. Also guard scoreColor against a zero field count (a fieldless matcher
no longer renders as a red 0%/NaN).

fix(core): support per-service gRPC health override removal (dashboard Reset)

The dashboard's gRPC health Reset button sends PUT /mockserver/grpc/health with
{ service, remove: true }, but the handler had no remove branch and required a
'status' field — so Reset always returned 400 and the override persisted. Add
GrpcHealthRegistry.removeStatus(service) (empty service resets the default to
SERVING) and a remove branch in handleGrpcHealthPut, mapping the GET response's
"_default" sentinel back to the empty-string service key so the default row is
also resettable.

fix(ui): parse streamed Gemini and OpenAI Responses traffic

Unlike Anthropic and OpenAI Chat, the Gemini and Responses parsers ignored
text/event-stream bodies — a streamed reply parsed to empty candidates/output
and zero usage, so the conversation view showed "No conversation content" and
no tokens/cost. Add SSE reassembly for both: Gemini concatenates the partial
candidate parts plus the final usageMetadata/finishReason; Responses rebuilds
the output (text from output_text.delta events, function calls from
output_item.done items) and reads usage/model from the response.* events.

fix(ui): make Clear gRPC empty the whole section and fix the active count

"Clear gRPC" cleared only fault injection, but the "N active" badge counted
health overrides too, so it could stay non-zero after clearing — and the count
also included the always-present "_default" SERVING health entry, which is not
an override. The badge now counts only real health overrides (a named service,
or a non-SERVING default) plus fault-injection services, and Clear gRPC now also
resets the health overrides so the section fully empties (parity with HTTP/TCP).
Also note in the form that gRPC latency applies on the fault path, so it should
accompany an injected fault rather than be used alone.

style(ui): use a consistent typographic ellipsis in loading labels

Standardise the loading strings on "Loading…" (the AgentRunGraph convention)
instead of the ASCII "Loading..." used in the Cassettes and Library export tabs.

feat(proxy): add DNS-intent original-destination resolver

Adds a transparent-proxy original-destination strategy that recovers the
intended hostname for connections that arrived by IP because MockServer's own
DNS server pointed the name at that IP (DNS-steering).

- DnsIntentRegistry (mockserver-core, org.mockserver.mock.dns): a bounded,
  thread-safe singleton (mirrors DriftStore) recording the answeredIP ->
  hostname mappings MockServer's DNS server hands out; FIFO eviction at 10k,
  cleared by HttpState.reset().
- DnsRequestHandler records each A/AAAA answer it sends (exception-safe — a
  recording failure never breaks the DNS response; CNAME/NXDOMAIN not recorded).
- DnsIntentOriginalDestinationResolver (mockserver-netty) looks up the
  connection's local IP in the registry and returns an unresolved
  InetSocketAddress carrying the recovered hostname, so matching/forwarding work
  by name. Added to CompositeOriginalDestinationResolver.defaultChain() AFTER
  conntrack, so a real REDIRECT original-dst always wins and this only fills the
  gap. Returning a named address is deliberate — downstream forwarding resolves
  it and the existing loop-prevention header guards a DNS-to-self loop.
- Only active when transparent proxy is enabled and the DNS server has populated
  the registry, so the default path is unaffected.

feat(llm): AWS SigV4 signing for the Bedrock runtime client

The runtime Bedrock client (BedrockLlmClient) built the request but did not
sign it, so direct Bedrock calls failed closed unless the caller supplied a
pre-signed Authorization header out of band. Implement AWS Signature V4 signing
and apply it.

- AwsSigV4Signer (mockserver-core, JDK crypto only — SHA-256 + HmacSHA256, no
  new dependency): deterministic header-based SigV4 (canonical request,
  credential-scoped string-to-sign, kSecret->kDate->kRegion->kService->kSigning
  HMAC chain, Authorization + X-Amz-Date + X-Amz-Content-Sha256 +
  X-Amz-Security-Token). UTC-pinned date formatters; lowercase hex for
  hashes/signature, uppercase %-encoding for the canonical URI.
- BedrockLlmClient.buildCompletionRequest now signs when AWS credentials are
  present: creds parsed from LlmBackend.apiKey() as "akid:secret[:token]"
  (safe — AWS keys/tokens never contain ':'), region parsed from the
  bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com baseUrl (us-east-1 fallback), service
  "bedrock". The model-id path segment (with ':') is percent-encoded
  consistently in both the wire URI and the canonical request. Signing takes
  precedence over the headers escape hatch when creds are present; with no/blank
  /non-cred apiKey, behaviour is unchanged (backward compatible). The signing
  timestamp is an overridable seam for tests.
- Tests verify against GENUINE AWS-published vectors: the signing-key derivation
  constant (20120215/us-east-1/iam) and the full get-vanilla signature
  (5fa00fa3...bf31) — an external end-to-end check, not self-consistency — plus
  determinism, session-token, URI-encoding, and the Bedrock integration
  (signing applied with creds, skipped without; region in credential scope).
- Docs: llm-security-audit.md SigV4 section marked resolved; BedrockLlmClient
  Javadoc updated.

- PublishOptions (new, org.mockserver.async.publish): immutable carrier
  (key / qos / retain), qos validated to {0,1,2} at construction, shared

- AsyncApiParser parses v2 operation bindings.mqtt.{qos,retain} and the
  message bindings.kafka.key (literal/const/example extraction; a bare schema

  channel-level mqtt; v3 operation-level mqtt bindings (separate operations
  section) are intentionally not navigated — documented. All binding parsing is

feat(async): support multi-message channels (oneOf / multiple messages)

  channel/spec methods are unchanged.

feat(helm): support configurable pod-level securityContext

Closes #2320

The chart only allowed setting the container-level runAsUser; there was no way
to set a pod-level securityContext, so fields like fsGroup could not be
configured. fsGroup is pod-level only and is required for the pod to read/write
a mounted PersistentVolume on clusters with restrictive defaults — without it,
persisting expectations to a PVC silently fails.

Adds a top-level podSecurityContext value (default {}) rendered verbatim into
the Deployment's spec.template.spec.securityContext, so any pod-level field is
supported (fsGroup, fsGroupChangePolicy, runAsGroup, seccompProfile, …):

    helm install ... --set app.persistence.enabled=true \
                     --set podSecurityContext.fsGroup=2000

Backward compatible: the default {} emits no pod-level securityContext, so
existing deployments render identically; the container-level securityContext
(runAsUser / readOnlyRootFilesystem / allowPrivilegeEscalation) is unchanged.
Chart version is intentionally not bumped (it tracks the app version). Rendered
via the chart's existing {{- with }} + toYaml convention. Documented in the
chart README, docs/infrastructure/helm.md, and the consumer Helm page (with the
PVC-permissions guidance).

feat(proxy): add JNA SO_ORIGINAL_DST original-destination resolver

Add an O(1) getsockopt(SO_ORIGINAL_DST) resolver as the first strategy in the
transparent-proxy resolver chain, ahead of the O(n) conntrack /proc scan. It
reads the pre-REDIRECT destination directly from the socket via a minimal JNA
binding to libc getsockopt, decoding sockaddr_in / sockaddr_in6.

The resolver is additive and safe on all platforms: isSupported() requires
Linux + Netty epoll available + JNA loadable, and resolve() returns null for
non-EpollSocketChannel (e.g. the current NIO transport) so it transparently
falls through to the existing conntrack resolver. It only wins the chain once
the server bootstrap runs on the epoll transport (a later increment).

The sockaddr byte-layout decode (sa_family in host order; port and address in
network order; IPv4 16-byte / IPv6 28-byte structs) is a pure, package-private
function with 20 unit tests using independently-derived byte vectors. The
getsockopt syscall path is Linux/epoll-only and validated in CI.

Adds net.java.dev.jna:jna (5.17.0) and io.netty:netty-transport-classes-epoll
(managed netty version, classes-only for compile-time EpollSocketChannel
access); both recorded in docs/operations/security.md.

feat(transport): run on Netty epoll transport when available on Linux

Select the epoll transport for the server bootstrap and outbound client when
the native library is present on Linux, falling back to NIO everywhere else.
Epoll improves throughput/latency and is required for transparent-proxy
SO_ORIGINAL_DST resolution (which needs EpollSocketChannel children). A new
useNativeTransport configuration property (default true) forces NIO when set
false.

NettyTransport (mockserver-core, usable by both the server and the core HTTP
client) creates the EventLoopGroup from the config flag with a graceful NIO
fallback, and derives the channel class from the actual group/loop INSTANCE
(serverSocketChannelClassFor / socketChannelClassFor / datagramChannelClassFor)
so the group and channel can never desync — including the relay path, which
hands a single EpollEventLoop rather than a group. Wired into LifeCycle (boss
and worker groups), MockServer (server + DNS datagram channels), NettyHttpClient
(both bootstraps) and RelayConnectHandler. HTTP/3 QUIC, the MCP internal client
and test/echo servers intentionally stay on NIO and remain self-consistent.

The native netty-transport-native-epoll artifacts (linux-x86_64 + linux-aarch_64)
are bundled as runtime dependencies so epoll activates in the distribution and
the existing integration suite exercises it on Linux CI. Recorded in security.md.

Coverage: NettyTransport decision matrix + group-derived selection are unit
tested (incl. the single-EventLoop and epoll->NIO fallback paths); a Linux-gated
EpollTransportIntegrationTest asserts the server boots on EpollServerSocketChannel
and serves over both epoll and the NIO opt-out, plus a DNS-on-epoll boot check.
The SO_ORIGINAL_DST iptables end-to-end test is a documented CI-only placeholder.

Fix #2322: reset preserved Content-Encoding/Transfer-Encoding headers per request

PreserveHeadersNettyRemoves stored the preserved Content-Encoding /
Transfer-Encoding headers on a channel attribute but only set it when at
least one of those headers was present, never clearing it. On a reused
(pooled) keep-alive connection, a request without Content-Encoding inherited
the previous request's value, so it was recorded as compressed.

The attribute is now always reset per request (an empty list when neither
header is present), so stale encoding headers cannot leak to later requests
sharing the same connection.

feat(grpc): add gRPC bidi-streaming pipeline scaffolding (G7 phase 0)

Add a default-off `grpcBidiStreamingEnabled` flag and an alternate HTTP/2
pipeline branch that terminates the connection with Http2FrameCodec +
Http2MultiplexHandler (per-stream child channels) instead of the connection-
level HttpToHttp2ConnectionHandler adapter. This is the scaffolding for true
client-streaming / bidirectional gRPC in later phases.

When the flag is off (default) the existing h2 negotiation in
PortUnificationHandler.switchToHttp2()/switchToH2c() is preserved verbatim
inside an else-branch, so all HTTP/2 traffic (REST mocking, MCP, dashboard
WebSocket, proxy relay, gRPC unary, gRPC-web) is byte-for-byte unchanged. The
new branch is only taken when the flag is on AND gRPC service descriptors are
loaded.

In phase 0 the per-stream GrpcMultiplexChildInitializer only RE-AGGREGATES
each stream (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec + HttpObjectAggregator) and runs
the same downstream chain the connection adapter feeds, so even when enabled the
behaviour matches today for unary/server-streaming. The child initializer
propagates the parent channel's LOCAL_HOST_HEADERS attribute (HTTP/2 child
channels do not inherit parent attributes) so local-vs-proxy request detection
is correct. HTTP/2-level frame decompression is intentionally not applied on
this path (gRPC uses grpc-encoding, not HTTP/2 content-encoding) — documented.

Tests: EmbeddedChannel re-aggregation + header-preservation + oversized-body
rejection; a flag-off pipeline test asserting the connection adapter (not the
multiplex handlers) is installed by default; config default-false test. Later
phases (server-streaming over multiplex, client-streaming, full bidi) replace
the re-aggregation handlers with frame-level streaming handlers.

test(grpc): verify server-streaming over the gRPC multiplex pipeline (G7 phase 1)

Server-streaming gRPC already works over the phase-0 multiplex pipeline with no
production change: Netty's bidirectional Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec strips
the (HTTP/2-illegal) chunked Transfer-Encoding via its header blacklist, turns
each response HttpContent into its own DATA frame, and converts the
LastHttpContent trailers into a trailing HEADERS frame with grpc-status and
END_STREAM.

Add GrpcServerStreamingMultiplexTest (5 EmbeddedChannel tests) proving it:
the full frame sequence (initial HEADERS without transfer-encoding, N DATA
frames, trailing status HEADERS), single-message and error-status cases,
byte-for-byte gRPC framing parity against GrpcFrameCodec.encode, and custom
metadata preservation. Document the behaviour in docs/code/netty-pipeline.md.

Phase 2 (client-streaming) and phase 3 (full bidi) will replace the inbound
re-aggregation with frame-level streaming handlers.

test(grpc): verify client-streaming over the gRPC multiplex pipeline (G7 phase 2)

Client-streaming (collect-then-respond) already works over the phase-0 multiplex
re-aggregation path with no production change: multiple inbound HTTP/2 DATA
frames are re-aggregated into one FullHttpRequest body (byte concatenation of
the gRPC frames), which GrpcToHttpRequestHandler decodes into a JSON array body
with the x-grpc-client-streaming header — identical to the connection adapter.
Single-message requests still decode as a non-array object with no client-
streaming header, preserving the unary/client-streaming distinction.

Add GrpcClientStreamingMultiplexTest (5 tests, using the real greeting.dsc
CollectGreetings client-streaming method) proving multi-frame concatenation and
the JSON-array/header decode.

Also harden the phase-0 inbound re-aggregation tests: they previously fed
HttpObject inputs which Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec ignores (it only
accepts Http2HeadersFrame/Http2DataFrame inbound), so the codec was a no-op
pass-through and only HttpObjectAggregator was exercised. They now feed real
DefaultHttp2HeadersFrame + DefaultHttp2DataFrame so the codec's inbound decode
genuinely runs (and the tests can fail if it regresses). Drop the incorrect
@Sharable on the stateful test capture handlers and merge a duplicated one.

fix(release): harden cosign Helm-chart signing (non-fatal, key out of argv, sha-pinned)

Three fixes to the signing step added in the previous batch:
- Strictly non-fatal: loading the key (load_secret) was outside the failure guard, so under
  'set -euo pipefail' an IAM/network/JSON failure on get-secret-value would abort the release AFTER
  the chart was already pushed (describe-secret succeeding does not imply get-secret-value will).
  The whole attempt now runs in cosign_sign_chart(), which handles every failure explicitly and
  returns non-zero instead of aborting.
- Key out of the process table: the private-key PEM was passed via 'docker run -e', visible in
  'ps' for the container's lifetime. It is now written to a 0600 file under .tmp/ (mounted at /build)

Fix #2326: preserve original compressed request bytes alongside decompressed body

Replaces the decompressRequestBodies opt-out property with an automatic dual
representation. MockServer still decompresses request bodies for matching and
recording (unchanged default), but now also keeps the original on-the-wire
(compressed) bytes captured before decompression.

- New HttpRequest#getBodyAsOriginalRawBytes() returns the exact bytes the client
  sent (compressed when compressed, otherwise the decompressed bytes);
  getBodyAsRawBytes() is unchanged (decompressed).
- A BinaryBody expectation now matches against either the decompressed body or the
  original compressed bytes, so a mixture of compressed and uncompressed requests
  matches automatically with no configuration.
- The original bytes are captured in PreserveHeadersNettyRemoves (before the
  HttpContentDecompressor), carried on the request as originalBody, copied by
  clone()/shallowClone(), and serialised (base64) so they survive
  retrieveRecordedRequests and persistence. Excluded from equals/hashCode as a
  wire-representation detail. HTTP/1.1 only; HTTP/2 requests are unaffected.

Removes the decompressRequestBodies configuration property, its docs panel and
tests. Keeps the duplicate-Content-Encoding dedup guard (and its unit test) from
the earlier work, which is still correct.

feat(grpc): reactive bidirectional gRPC streaming handler (G7 phase 3a)

Add the per-stream reactive machinery for true interleaved bidi gRPC, behind
the existing default-off grpcBidiStreamingEnabled flag (multiplex path only):

- IncrementalGrpcFrameDecoder (mockserver-core): accumulates gRPC messages
  across HTTP/2 DATA frames, retaining trailing partial bytes (GrpcFrameCodec
  is whole-buffer and drops partials), with a per-message MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE
  check and an overall buffer cap (overflow-safe).
- GrpcBidiStreamHandler (mockserver-netty, per-stream, not @Sharable): opens
  the response on HEADERS, decodes each inbound DATA frame incrementally and
  writes response DATA frames IMMEDIATELY (interleaved, not buffered until
  END_STREAM), and emits a single guarded trailing grpc-status HEADERS frame
  on completion/error. Backpressure via autoRead-off + per-frame ctx.read();
  buffer-cap breach maps to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
- GrpcBidiRouterHandler (per-stream, not @Sharable): on the first HEADERS,
  routes true bidi methods (isClientStreaming && isServerStreaming) to the
  bidi handler and everything else to the existing Phase 0 re-aggregating
  chain (extracted to GrpcMultiplexChildInitializer.installReAggregatingChain),
  so unary/server-streaming/client-streaming stay byte-for-byte unchanged.

Phase 3a uses a canned echo responder; phase 3b replaces it with the
GRPC_BIDI_RESPONSE action (model/DTO/schema/dispatch + rule-driven responses)
and the matched-action routing guard; phase 3c adds clients/docs/WAR guard.

Tests (EmbeddedChannel, no grpc-java): IncrementalGrpcFrameDecoderTest (12 —
split-header/payload, multi-message, cap, MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE, invalid flag);
GrpcBidiInterleavingMultiplexTest proves msg1's response is emitted BEFORE
msg2 is fed (fails if buffered), split-frame accumulation, and unary-method
routing parity. review-final PASS (1 MINOR overflow-guard hardened).

feat(grpc): add GRPC_BIDI_RESPONSE expectation action (G7 phase 3b)

Make reactive bidi gRPC usable via expectations. New GrpcBidiResponse action
(model + DTO + JSON schema + Expectation/ExpectationDTO wiring + Action.Type)
carries initial headers, eager server-push messages, and a list of reactive
rules (GrpcBidiRule: a NottableString matchJson + response messages), plus the
final grpc-status. Reuses the existing GrpcStreamMessage model.

The multiplex router now decides routing with a NEW side-effect-free
HttpState.peekFirstMatchingExpectation: a true-bidi method whose matched
expectation is a GrpcBidiResponse is routed to GrpcBidiStreamHandler;
everything else falls back to the re-aggregating chain. Using a read-only peek
(not the consuming firstMatchingExpectation) is essential — otherwise a
times(1) non-bidi expectation on the same path would be consumed by the routing
probe and then missed, and the fallback path would double-count.

GrpcBidiStreamHandler is now driven by the matched GrpcBidiResponse: eager
messages on HEADERS, per-inbound-message first-match rule -> response DATA
frames (interleaved), trailing grpc-status from statusName. Rule matching is
exact-or-regex (DOTALL) honouring NottableString negation — mirrors
BidirectionalWebSocketFrameHandler (no substring matching). HttpActionHandler
gets a GRPC_BIDI_RESPONSE case returning 501 for WAR and non-multiplex paths.

Known limitations (documented, deferred): a matched GrpcBidiResponse is not yet
Times-consumed and bidi requests are not yet logged/verified (needs
responseInProgress lifecycle over the long-lived stream); per-message delay is
accepted but not yet applied. Both tracked in the plan.

Tests (no grpc-java): GrpcBidiResponseDTO serialization round-trip (8);
RequestMatchersPeek side-effect-free proof incl. times(1) not consumed (6);
GrpcBidiInterleavingMultiplexTest grown to 15 (two-rule interleave, no-false-
positive contains, NottableString negation, custom trailing status, multi-
response rule, times(1) not consumed by router). 229 tests pass; review-final
CRITICAL (probe side-effects) + MAJOR (contains) fixed; checkstyle clean.

feat(grpc): client builders + docs for GRPC_BIDI_RESPONSE (G7 phase 3c)

Expose the bidi gRPC action through all four client libraries and the consumer
docs, completing G7 Phase 3.

- Java: ForwardChainExpectation.respondWithGrpcBidi(GrpcBidiResponse).
- Python: GrpcBidiResponse + GrpcBidiRule dataclasses + respond_with_grpc_bidi

- StreamingBody optionally captures a System.nanoTime() per chunk (enabled on the
  recording/relay path only); interChunkDelaysMillis() derives relative delays.
  Timestamp capture stops once byte-capture truncates (and on stream error), so
  long-lived streams cannot grow the timestamp list unbounded.
- The relay path serialises inter-chunk delays into an internal
  x-mockserver-chunk-delays-ms header on the recorded log entry, attached on all
  three streaming completion paths via a shared attachStreamingHeaders helper.
- SseAwareExpectationConverter applies the captured delays during replay and
  STRIPS the internal header in both the SSE-conversion and truncated-fallback
  paths so it can never reach a client; SseBodyParser falls back to the fixed
  delay when timing is absent (backward-compatible; no JSON/DTO schema change).

Chunk→event mapping is exact for one-event-per-chunk LLM streams and best-effort
otherwise (documented). Tests (controlled clock, no wall-clock sleeps): per-chunk
capture/replay round-trip, truncation stops growth, error path, header stripping,
fallback. review-final PASS (prior BLOCK on unbounded growth + header leak fixed).

runtime state (responseInProgress/Times) node-local via matcherCacheById +

reconcileEvictions() drops node-local matchers (and their request definitions)
for ids the backend evicted. This is the seam phase 2c rebuilds from on
cluster invalidation.

feat(state): route persistence through a BlobStore face (G10 phase 2d)

(same paths, same FileChannel/FileLock/ByteBuffer write pattern); in-memory
is opt-in. The event log / Disruptor ring buffer stays node-local.

persistence layer's catch(Throwable) logs them) instead of silently
swallowing — closing a silent-data-loss path on disk-full/permission errors —
and falls back to an SLF4J logger when constructed without a MockServerLogger
(the StateBackendFactory path). Persistence write ordering is preserved via a
write lock that re-reads current state inside the lock so async expectation-
change callbacks can't overwrite newer state.

and HttpState wires it to RequestMatchers.reconcileFromBackend() so a mutation
on one node rebuilds the node-local matcher view on the others. reconcile is

propagate, not just sort-field changes; matching stays node-local (no per-request
grid hit), with the sorted view eventually-consistent under concurrent mutation

feat(state): clustered exactly-once Times via shared CAS (G10 follow-up)

once()) is now served exactly N times across the whole fleet, not N-per-node.
ExpectationEntry carries a remainingTimes counter; on a match the node
CAS-decrements it in the backend BEFORE serving (bounded retry), falls through
without serving when the allotment is already exhausted (another node won), and
schedules removal of the exhausted matcher (propagated by invalidation).
Unlimited Times, no backend, and non-clustered backends take the original
node-local consumeMatch() fast path unchanged — single-node behaviour is
byte-for-byte identical.

mis-reported success when the lambda was re-executed on retry; replaced with

feat(proxy): eBPF original-destination resolver strategy (G5)

from a pinned BPF hash map keyed by socket cookie, populated by an external BPF
program the operator deploys. Implemented via the existing JNA binding (no new
dependency) — bpf(BPF_OBJ_GET) then BPF_MAP_LOOKUP_ELEM/DELETE_ELEM, with the
bpf() syscall number selected per architecture (x86_64=321, aarch64=280) and

(does not load/attach the BPF program), keeping the privilege surface small
(CAP_BPF). Gated behind default-off transparentProxyEbpf (+ transparentProxyEbpfMapPath);
registered in the resolver chain at [TPROXY, eBPF, SO_ORIGINAL_DST, conntrack,
dns]. When disabled it returns null immediately (zero overhead) and on non-Linux

feat(http3): CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) handler scaffolding, default-off (G16 follow-up)

Add an Http3ConnectUdpHandler behind a new default-off http3ConnectUdpEnabled
flag. Full CONNECT-UDP datagram relay is NOT feasible with the bundled
netty-incubator-codec-http3 0.0.30.Final: its pseudo-header enum has no
:protocol and there's no SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL, so a compliant MASQUE
client is rejected at the wire before any handler runs (the QUIC transport DOES
support datagrams, so only the H3 layer blocks it). When the flag is enabled the
handler cleanly returns 501 to CONNECT requests and passes all normal requests
through untouched; when disabled (default) the handler is not inserted at all and
the H3 pipeline is byte-for-byte unchanged. Documents the precise codec blocker +
a full-relay implementation plan in the design note. 57 Http3 tests, 0 regressions.

feat(http3): real CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) forward proxy on mainline netty H3 codec

The netty HTTP/3 codec graduated from incubator to mainline Netty 4.2, so migrate
the dependency from io.netty.incubator:netty-incubator-codec-http3:0.0.30.Final to
io.netty:netty-codec-http3:${netty.version} (4.2.15.Final) — packages
io.netty.incubator.codec.{http3,quic} → io.netty.handler.codec.{http3,quic}. The
GA codec implements RFC 9220 extended CONNECT (the :protocol pseudo-header) and
QUIC datagrams, which the incubator did not. Native QUIC artifacts (all 5 platform
classifiers) are bundled transitively as before, so H3 still starts in the
distribution. No regression: 65 H3 + a HTTP/2/gRPC/proxy regression sample all pass.

Replace the 501 stub with a functional CONNECT-UDP relay (Http3ConnectUdpHandler):
recognise :protocol=connect-udp, parse the target authority (IPv4/IPv6/hostname),
open a UDP DatagramChannel, answer 200, and relay DATA frames <-> UDP datagrams
both ways with correct ByteBuf lifecycle, tearing down on stream close/error.
Advertise SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL only when enabled. Still gated behind
the default-off http3ConnectUdpEnabled flag; plain CONNECT passes through and
default H3 behaviour is unchanged.

fix(ci): skip clustered image build when host lacks JDK (unbreak container tests)

The container integration tests step runs on a bare Buildkite host (Docker
only, no JDK, SKIP_JAVA_BUILD=true) and downloads the prebuilt JAR artifact.
build_clustered_docker() unconditionally ran ./mvnw to resolve the Infinispan
runtime classpath, which died ("JAVA_HOME is not defined") under set -euo
pipefail and failed the whole step on every build.

Guard the clustered image build: skip gracefully (return 0) when no JDK is on
the host or the locally-built fat jar is absent. The clustered smoke test
already non-blocking-skips when the image is missing, so the variant is fully
built and tested in local dev (JDK + reactor present) and cleanly skipped in
the artifact-only CI container-tests step. Building the clustered image inside
the Maven step for CI coverage is a follow-up.

feat(http3): advertise Alt-Svc so clients auto-discover + upgrade to HTTP/3

When HTTP/3 is enabled (http3Port > 0), MockServer now advertises it on its TCP
responses via Alt-Svc — the standard discovery mechanism that lets HTTP/3-capable
clients automatically upgrade to H3/QUIC and fall back to HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 if
QUIC is unavailable (the fallback is client-driven; the server enables it by
advertising H3 while continuing to serve TCP). A stateless @Sharable
AltSvcHeaderHandler adds 'alt-svc: h3=":<http3Port>"; ma=<maxAge>' to outbound
HttpResponses on the HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, h2c, and gRPC-multiplex TCP paths (mirrors
TraceContextHandler); it never clobbers a user-set Alt-Svc and never touches
non-HttpResponse writes. Gated on http3Port>0 AND the new http3AdvertiseAltSvc
(default true) — when HTTP/3 is disabled (default) no handler is added and the TCP
server is byte-for-byte unchanged. New props http3AltSvcMaxAge (default 86400) +
http3AdvertiseAltSvc. Tests prove presence-when-enabled, absence-when-disabled,
and no-clobber; 0 regression across port-unification/HTTP-2/gRPC-bidi/H3 suites.

test(integration): explicit per-transport decode-smoke (decomposition safety net)

and match against an expectation keyed on the decompressed plaintext body.
If decompression were broken, the server would see raw gzip bytes and the
expectation would not match.

Add supportsRequestBodyDecompression() hook (defaults true) so WAR/servlet
transports -- which lack request-body decompression -- skip the gzip test
via Assume.assumeTrue rather than failing.  Remove unused `header` import.

ci(cache): add dependency caching for Maven/node/pip/bundler builds

Two-layer cache strategy for scale-to-zero Buildkite agents:

run-in-docker.sh now mounts /var/cache/buildkite/{maven,npm,pip,bundle}
into every Docker container. These persist across builds on the same EC2

  - S3 bucket: mockserver-ci-dependency-cache (dependency-cache.tf)
  - IAM policy: buildkite-dependency-cache (dependency-cache.tf)
  - IAM policy attachment on default + release stacks (main.tf)

To apply:
  cd terraform/buildkite-agents
  ./run.sh plan    # review the plan
  ./run.sh apply   # create bucket + policy + attach to agent roles

Until terraform apply runs, the S3 cache layer will gracefully no-op
(cache-restore/save soft_fail on AWS errors). The host volume layer

Close the two real HTTP/3 feature-parity gaps (everything else — matching,

- W3C trace-context: Http3MockServerHandler now parses traceparent/tracestate (or

fix(ci): make host-cache mounts fail-safe on non-root agents (unbreak all pipelines)

The dependency-cache change added `mkdir -p /var/cache/buildkite/...` directly
in run-in-docker.sh under `set -euo pipefail`. The Buildkite agent runs as a
non-root user without write access to /var/cache, so the mkdir failed and
aborted the wrapper before launching any container — breaking EVERY step that
runs via run-in-docker.sh (lint, build, test, validate) across all pipelines.

Only add a host-cache volume mount when its directory can actually be created
(`if mkdir -p ... 2>/dev/null`), silently skipping host caching otherwise. The
S3 cache layer (already soft_fail) is unaffected. Verified: with an unwritable
cache base the wrapper now survives (exit 0, no mounts) under set -euo pipefail.

feat(http3): MCP over HTTP/3 with control-plane auth + CORS parity

Extract the MCP protocol logic from McpStreamableHttpHandler into a transport-
neutral McpRequestProcessor (String body → McpResult), so both the TCP handler
(unchanged behaviour, delegates) and the H3 pipeline can serve MCP. Http3MockServerHandler
dispatches /mockserver/mcp requests to the processor and writes the result as H3
frames, sharing the same McpSessionManager so sessions work across transports.

Crucially, the H3 MCP path enforces the SAME control-plane authentication as TCP
(JWT/mTLS via httpState.getControlPlaneAuthenticationHandler, using the client cert
already captured on the request) before any tool execution — POST/GET/DELETE are
gated (401 with the identical JSON-RPC error), OPTIONS-with-origin is exempt for
CORS preflight — closing what would otherwise be an unauthenticated backdoor to the
MCP tools over QUIC. CORS headers match the TCP path. When no auth handler is
configured (default), behaviour is unchanged.

Adds 19 MCP-over-H3 integration tests (native QUIC) incl. auth reject/accept + CORS;
53 existing TCP MCP tests unchanged. 377 tests, 0 regressions.

feat(http3): gRPC unary over HTTP/3

Support gRPC unary calls over HTTP/3. Http3MockServerHandler detects application/grpc
requests and routes them through GrpcHttp3Adapter, which reuses the existing
GrpcFrameCodec + GrpcJsonMessageConverter to decode the length-prefixed gRPC message
to JSON (tagging x-grpc-service/method from the path, identical to the TCP path), so
expectations match the same way over H3 as HTTP/2. Http3GrpcResponseWriter re-encodes
the matched response to a gRPC frame and conveys grpc-status/grpc-message in a TRAILING
HTTP/3 HEADERS frame (trailers-only for bodyless errors) — the framing gRPC clients
require. Non-gRPC H3 requests and the existing HTTP/2 gRPC path are unaffected.

Server-/bidi-streaming gRPC over H3 is deferred (G16-FOLLOW-UP-5): the existing
streaming handlers are coupled to HTTP/2 frame types. Adds 19 adapter unit tests +
4 native-QUIC integration tests (unary round-trip, UNIMPLEMENTED, no-descriptors
passthrough, non-gRPC unaffected); 196 tests, 0 regressions.

revert(ci): remove broken host-volume + S3-runtime caching wiring (keep S3 infra config)

The host-volume cache layer (mounting /var/cache/buildkite/* into Docker

feat(http3): gRPC server-streaming + bidi-streaming over HTTP/3

Completes gRPC-over-HTTP/3 to full parity with HTTP/2 (G16-FOLLOW-UP-5):
unary already worked; this adds server-streaming and true bidi-streaming.

Server-streaming: HttpActionHandler routes the GRPC_STREAM_RESPONSE action to a
new transport-neutral GrpcStreamResponseWriter seam (implemented by
Http3GrpcResponseWriter) when the request arrived over HTTP/3 -- initial HEADERS,
one DATA frame per message (per-message delays scheduled on the QUIC stream event
loop), then trailing HEADERS with grpc-status. HTTP/2 is unchanged.

Bidi-streaming: Http3MockServerHandler routes a stream to the new
Http3GrpcBidiStreamHandler at HEADERS time when grpcBidiStreamingEnabled is on,
the :path resolves to a client+server-streaming method, and a GrpcBidiResponse
expectation matches (same two-phase peek-then-consume + responseInProgress
lifecycle as the HTTP/2 GrpcBidiRouterHandler). Inbound DATA frames are decoded
incrementally over the full-duplex QUIC stream; rule matches emit response DATA
frames; trailing HEADERS are written once the client half-closes and all
responses drain. channelInactive clears responseInProgress.

Shared, transport-neutral logic extracted to mockserver-core helpers
(GrpcStreamMessageEncoder, GrpcBidiRuleMatcher) and reused by both the HTTP/2 and
HTTP/3 handlers so framing and rule matching stay byte-identical; the HTTP/2
handlers were refactored to delegate (behaviour-preserving).

Covered by native-QUIC integration tests (Http3GrpcStreamingIntegrationTest):
server-streaming with delays, bidi with rule-driven responses + verification, and
the disabled-gate negative case. HTTP/2 server-streaming/bidi/integration tests
unchanged and green; checkstyle clean.

fix(log): O(1) size in CircularConcurrentLinkedDeque to stop CPU climbing as the log fills (#2329)

The bounded ring backing the request/event log checked capacity on every insert
with ConcurrentLinkedDeque.size(), which is O(n) (it walks the whole list). Once
the log reached maxLogEntries (default 100,000) each request paid an O(n)
traversal per log entry, so CPU rose as the log filled and stayed high — and
because clearing expectations does not clear the log, it never recovered. This
matches the reported symptom in #2329 (steadily increasing CPU under sustained
load, expectations cleared each cycle, periodic /retrieve).

Track size in an AtomicInteger updated by every mutator (add/offer/addAll-via-add/
clear/remove/removeItem/internal evict), so size() and the eviction check are O(1).
Behaviour is unchanged: same bounded-FIFO semantics, same evict-oldest order, same
onEvictCallback invocation. clear() now drains via a counted poll loop (equivalent
to the prior super.clear()/poll-loop, and keeps the counter consistent). isEmpty()
also uses the counter.

Measured per-insert cost at the default capacity (100k): ~210µs -> ~15ns
(~14,000x); the old cost scaled linearly with maxLogEntries (2.6µs@1k, 19.7µs@10k,
99.7µs@50k, 209.8µs@100k), the new cost is flat (~15-100ns).

Tests: size-consistency across evict/removeItem/clear, evict-callback order,
maxSize=0, and a 30s-timeout regression guard (150k inserts at 50k capacity, runs
in ~21ms — would take minutes under the O(n) path). changelog + memory-management
docs updated (incl. the clear-expectations-does-not-clear-the-log guidance).
