Adds testFramework(Platform) to build.gradle.kts; existing tests still pass (66 total).

feat(core): generate expectation code from recordings in JavaScript and Python

Extend the retrieve endpoint's format beyond JAVA/JSON so recorded or active
expectations can be returned as ready-to-paste JavaScript and Python client code
(format=JAVASCRIPT / PYTHON), alongside the existing JAVA builder output. Because
the Node and Python clients accept an expectation as a JSON object / dict, the
generators reuse the existing JSON serialization and wrap each expectation in the
correct client call + import preamble (mockServerClient(...).mockAnyResponse(...)
for JS; MockServerClient(...).upsert(Expectation.from_dict(json.loads(...))) for
Python) — verified against the real client APIs. The dashboard Library view gains
JavaScript/Python export options and a copy-as-code button.

REQUESTS/REQUEST_RESPONSES reject the code formats (parity with JAVA). Embedded
JSON is byte-identical to format=json so it round-trips, incl. hostile values
(quotes/backslashes/newlines/unicode). review-cheap PASS + fixes. mvn: serializer
+ HttpState (recorded + active + rejection paths) + guard tests; UI lint + 1376
vitest + build all green. Further client languages follow.

fix(dashboard): serve SVG assets with a non-null Content-Type

Opening the dashboard requested favicon.svg, which crashed Netty's
response encoder with "NullPointerException: value". The svg extension
was missing from DashboardHandler's MIME map, so MIME_MAP.get("svg")
returned null and the response carried a Content-Type header with a
null value, which Netty's header encoder rejects.

- add svg -> image/svg+xml to the dashboard MIME map, and fall back to
  application/octet-stream for any unmapped extension so a null
  Content-Type can never be produced again
- skip any null-valued header or trailer in
  MockServerHttpResponseToFullHttpResponse so a null header value can
  never fail response encoding (defense in depth)
- add regression tests and an SVG test fixture

Fixes #2358

fix(openapi): allOf with single scalar $ref no longer emits a single-element array

A property whose schema is `allOf: [ $ref to a scalar ]` (e.g. a string) was
generating a single-element JSON array instead of the scalar value — for example
`{ "baz": ["hello"] }` instead of `{ "baz": "hello" }`. This broke clients
generated against the spec, which fail to deserialize a String from an Array
value.

Root cause: the spec is parsed with resolveFully + resolveCombinators, which
flattens `allOf: [ $ref ]` and aggregates the member's example into a
single-element collection (a HashSet) attached to the now-scalar schema.
OpenAPIConverter.resolveSchemaExample then emitted that collection verbatim.

Fix:
- ExampleBuilder.normalizeFlattenedExample unwraps a single-element collection
  example back to its scalar value when the schema's resolved type is a scalar
  (string/integer/number/boolean); wired into example reads in both
  ExampleBuilder.fromProperty and OpenAPIConverter.resolveSchemaExample.
- The ComposedSchema allOf branch now returns the scalar example directly when
  every allOf member is a non-object example, instead of wrapping it in an empty
  object; object members and own properties still merge as before.

Adds ComposedSchemaExampleBuilderTest (unit + end-to-end via OpenAPIConverter)
and the openapi_allof_scalar_ref.yaml fixture to guard the regression.

Fixes #2357

feat(core): expectation code generation for all client languages + verification

Complete the retrieve-as-code feature so recorded/active expectations can be
returned as ready-to-paste client code in every official MockServer client
language: adds Go, C#, Ruby, Rust and PHP server-side serializers alongside the
existing Java/JavaScript/Python (format=GO|CSHARP|RUBY|RUST|PHP). Each reuses the
existing expectation JSON and wraps it in the real client call, with
language-correct string-literal escaping verified against hostile values (Go
backtick raw-string with interpreted-string fallback; Rust dynamic r#""# hash
bumping; C# verbatim @""; Ruby heredoc; PHP nowdoc).

PHP client gains Expectation::fromArray(array) (round-trip-faithful via raw-data
replay; docker-verified with php:8.3-cli) so generated PHP code compiles.

Dashboard Library view now offers all eight languages for mock setup (expectations
/ recorded), and verification code from recorded requests in seven languages
(reusing the existing client-side verificationCodegen — PHP has no verify
generator). REQUESTS/REQUEST_RESPONSES still reject mock-code formats (parity).
Existing formats byte-identical; Format resolved by name so the mid-enum additions
are safe. review-final PASS. mvn core (serializer 20 + HttpState 166 + guard) +
PHP phpunit + UI lint/1380 vitest/build all green.

test(ui): fix typecheck error in LibraryView verification-code test

The clipboard mock was declared vi.fn(async () => undefined) with no parameter,
so its call-args tuple typed as [] and the assertion writeText.mock.calls[0]![0]
failed tsc --noEmit (TS2493: tuple of length 0 has no index 0). npm run build
(tsc -b, project refs) skips test files so it passed locally, but CI's separate
typecheck step (tsc --noEmit) covers tests and caught it. Type the mock with an
explicit call signature vi.fn<(text: string) => Promise<undefined>>(...) so the
arg is typed without an unused parameter (keeps eslint happy too). lint +
typecheck + the 28 LibraryView vitest tests all pass.

fix(log): gate the request matcher behind the cheap log filter on retrieve (#2359)

CPU climbed over time under sustained load with periodic /retrieve and
per-cycle clear. The #2329 fix made log insertion O(1); this fixes the
remaining cost on the read paths.

retrieveLogEntries (every /retrieve) and retrieveLogEntriesInReverseForUI
ran the expensive request matcher — which clones the request and runs full
field-by-field matching — on every entry BEFORE the cheap type/not-deleted
predicate, so the matcher was evaluated against deleted tombstones and
wrong-type entries that were then discarded. As the log fills toward
maxLogEntries (clearing expectations does not clear the log, and clear at
INFO only marks entries deleted rather than removing them), each /retrieve
cost grew with total log size and stayed high.

The filters are now ordered cheap-predicate-first (matching the existing
expectation-id retrieve path), so the matcher only runs for entries that
can actually be returned. clear() also skips entries already marked deleted,
so a clear issued every cycle no longer re-matches the whole accumulated log
of tombstones. No behaviour change — same retrieved results, same clear
semantics.

Regression tests assert the matcher is evaluated only for entries that pass
the cheap predicate (not for deleted tombstones or wrong-type entries) and
that repeated clear does not re-scan tombstones; all three fail on the
pre-fix ordering.

Closes #2359

test(openapi): cover top-level allOf single scalar $ref end-to-end

Strengthens the #2357 regression net with the top-level variant: a response
schema that is directly `allOf: [ $ref to a string ]` (vs the existing
nested-property case). Asserts the generated body is the JSON string "hello",
not the array ["hello"], exercising the parser flatten + resolveSchemaExample
path that normalizeFlattenedExample fixes.

Also makes expectation selection precise by matching on
OpenAPIDefinition.getOperationId() instead of toString().contains(...), which
was loose because the expectation's toString embeds the whole spec (and thus
mentions every operationId).

fix(openapi): handle status-code range keys (2XX/4XX/5XX) in import and response validation

OpenAPI 3.x permits patterned response keys (1XX-5XX). Two defects:

- buildHttpResponse called Integer.parseInt on the response-map key, throwing
  NumberFormatException on a range key like "2XX". Uncaught inside the
  buildExpectations map(), this aborted the ENTIRE PUT /mockserver/openapi
  import. Now parsed via parseResponseStatusCode: 3-digit -> that code, range
  -> firstDigit*100 (2XX->200), "default" -> unset, anything else -> WARN +
  unset. Never throws.
- OpenAPIResponseValidator only matched the exact status then "default", so a
  spec defining only "2XX" reported a false "200 not defined" error. It now
  tries the range bucket between exact and default; exact still wins over range,
  range over default.

Adds converter + validator tests and an openapi_status_code_range.yaml fixture.

fix(openapi): make expectations->OpenAPI export schema-valid and faithful

The expectations->OpenAPI export (retrieve?format=openapi) could emit
schema-invalid and semantically wrong documents and had no tests. Fixes:

- Path parameters are emitted only when the path key contains the matching
  {name} placeholder, so the document no longer violates the OAS 3.0.3 rule
  that every in:path parameter be templated in the path.
- Negated matchers (NottableString.isNot()) and schema matchers
  (NottableSchemaString) are no longer silently exported as their positive
  literal form: a negated path/method skips the operation (logged), and negated
  header/query params are omitted. Previously path != "/admin" exported as a
  positive /admin operation.
- Two expectations sharing path+method now merge their responses into one
  operation instead of one silently overwriting the other.
- Path keys are normalised to a leading "/".
- Body media types prefer the actual Content-Type header; bodies map by type
  (binary -> schema {type:string,format:binary} instead of base64 text/plain;
  matcher-only bodies are described, not emitted as literal examples).
- Serialisation failure returns a minimal valid OpenAPI stub, not "{}".

Adds ExpectationExportSerializerTest (13 tests) which parses the generated
documents with swagger-parser and asserts zero validation messages.

fix(openapi): accept and emit contextPathPrefix on OpenAPIDefinition matcher

contextPathPrefix on an OpenAPIDefinition request matcher was set by the
converter, honoured at runtime, and emitted by the DTO serializer, but its
JSON schema rejected it and the model serializer dropped it. Fixes:

- openAPIDefinition.json (additionalProperties:false) now allows
  contextPathPrefix, so a matcher carrying it no longer fails validation.
- OpenAPIDefinitionSerializer (model) now writes contextPathPrefix, matching
  OpenAPIDefinitionDTOSerializer, so toString()/log output is faithful.
- mock-server-openapi-embedded-model.yaml keeps the published contract in sync:
  contextPathPrefix on OpenAPIDefinition, and operationsAndResponses on
  OpenAPIExpectation now documents both the string and {statusCode,exampleName}
  object forms plus contextPathPrefix.
- Removed a duplicate "openAPIDefinition" entry in JsonSchemaRequestDefinitionValidator.

Adds validator, model-serializer, and object-form deserializer tests.

fix(openapi): prevent cross-spec data loss in incremental sync via collision-resistant spec key

Importing an OpenAPI spec prunes prior expectations sharing its namespace. The
namespace key was derived from info.title alone, so two DIFFERENT specs sharing
a title collided into one namespace and importing one DELETED the other's
expectations (confirmed cross-spec data loss).

The spec key is now <sanitizedTitle>_<hash> where the hash is a SHA-256
(truncated) of the spec SOURCE identity (URL/file reference, or inline payload
content) — not the title. Distinct sources therefore never collide. SHA-256
replaces the former 32-bit String.hashCode(), which was too collision-prone for
a token guarding deletion.

Identity semantics (documented on OpenApiSyncPlanner.deriveSpecKey):
- URL/file spec: re-importing the same reference re-targets the same namespace,
  so incremental sync still prunes removed operations; different URLs never
  collide.
- inline payload: keyed by content, so a byte-identical re-import is idempotent
  but an EDITED inline payload gets a new namespace (its old operations are
  orphaned, not pruned). This deliberately favours collision-resistance over
  prune-on-inline-edit; reference a spec by URL/file for clean incremental sync.

Manual (non-openapi) expectations are never touched by the prune. Adds
OpenApiCrossSpecSyncTest (end-to-end via HttpState) covering: no cross-spec
deletion with shared titles, manual-expectation survival, and same-source
re-import still prunes; plus planner and converter unit tests.

fix(openapi): stop silent wrong/empty example selection, $ref leakage, and operationId collisions

Four correctness defects in OpenAPI->expectations conversion:

- Selecting a response by a pinned statusCode (or a named example) that the
  operation does not define silently returned a bare empty 200 (or a different
  named example). Now a WARN names the requested vs available keys and a
  deliberate fallback to the first defined response/example is used. Also fixes
  the bitwise | to logical || on the response filter.
- resolveSchemaExample returned null for the WHOLE object when any single
  property (or allOf own-property) example was null, discarding all resolved
  siblings. It now skips the null property and keeps the rest.
- Example $ref resolution: structure-depth truncation is now logged (was
  silent), both depth guards use >=, unresolvable $ref nodes are dropped instead
  of leaking literal {"$ref":...} into the response body, and resolveRef now
  navigates a JSON-pointer suffix beyond the example name.
- addMissingOperationIds now enforces global operationId uniqueness across paths
  and webhooks: author-supplied ids are reserved first, synthesized ids and
  duplicates are disambiguated deterministically and logged, so a hand-written
  "GET /pets" id or a webhook/path id clash no longer conflates two operations.

Adds OpenAPIConverterCorrectnessTest, OpenAPIParserOperationIdTest, and fixtures.

fix(openapi): honour default/enum for format-less numbers, emit XML bodies, precision fixes

Example-generation correctness fixes:

- integer/number schemas WITHOUT a format now honour `default` (and `enum`)
  instead of discarding the resolved value and emitting 0 / a random sample.
- application/xml (and text/xml, +xml) response bodies are now serialised as XML
  via XmlExampleSerializer instead of JSON; the serializer's encoding is made
  explicit and its swallowed exception is routed through MockServerLogger.
  Previously the XML serializer was dead code and XML responses were emitted as
  JSON.
- SAMPLE_DOUBLE_PROPERTY_VALUE is a real double 1.1 (was 1.1f -> 1.1000000238).
- DateSchema example formatting pinned to UTC so it can't shift near a day
  boundary.
- a no-format integer `example` beyond int range is preserved (Integer -> Long
  -> BigInteger) instead of being swallowed and lost.

Adds ExampleBuilderTest (33 deterministic cases) locking in the default example
shape for every primitive/format, composition, additionalProperties, OAS-3.1
type arrays, and circular-$ref termination, plus an XML response fixture.
docs(changelog): record OpenAPI handling hardening (audit follow-up to #2357)

fix(openapi): keep expectations->OpenAPI export schema-valid for more inputs

Re-review found three more cases where the export emitted schema-invalid
OpenAPI (reproduced via swagger-parser):

- a path key with a {name} placeholder that had no matching path parameter is
  invalid; synthetic in:path parameters are now generated so the set of {name}
  placeholders always equals the set of emitted path parameters.
- a non-conforming HTTP method (e.g. CONNECT, or an arbitrary recorded verb) is
  not a valid OpenAPI operation key; such operations are now skipped (logged),
  not emitted.
- two distinct path+method operations whose expectations share an explicit id
  produced a repeated operationId; ids are now de-duplicated document-wide
  (the same-path+method response-merge case is unchanged).

Adds regression tests that parse the generated document through swagger-parser
and assert zero validation messages.

fix(openapi): handle webhooks-only specs and tighten validator path/status matching

Re-review found a MAJOR null-safety bug plus validator minors:

- A valid OAS 3.1 webhooks-only spec (no `paths:`) made openAPI.getPaths()
  null, NPE-ing in buildExpectations (the NPE escaped the control-plane
  PUT /mockserver/openapi handler, which only catches IllegalArgumentException)
  and in the request/response/traffic validators. getPaths() is now null-guarded
  in all four, so webhook operations remain reachable and a paths-less spec is
  imported/validated instead of crashing.
- The response validator's range-bucket lookup is now case-insensitive, matching
  the converter which already accepts a lowercase `2xx` key.
- Request and traffic validators now prefer the most specific matching path
  (fewest {} placeholders), so a concrete `/users/me` wins over a templated
  `/users/{id}` regardless of declaration order.
- OpenApiTrafficValidator guards each request/response pair so one failure no
  longer aborts the whole batch (parity with OpenApiContractTest).
- Corrects stale "8-char" wording in specKeyFromHash javadoc (returns 16).

Adds webhooks-only, concrete-before-templated, and lowercase-range fixtures + tests.

fix(openapi): emit well-formed namespaced XML example bodies (regression fix)

Wiring XmlExampleSerializer into the XML response path exposed that it never
declared XML namespaces: a namespaced schema produced an empty body (default
namespace -> StAX "Prefix cannot be null", caught) or malformed XML (prefixed
namespace -> unbound prefix). The serializer now drives the StAX namespace API:
default namespaces via setDefaultNamespace + writeDefaultNamespace (xmlns="..."),
prefixed via setPrefix + writeNamespace (xmlns:prefix="..."), each declared once
on the introducing element; namespaced attributes bind their prefix first.

Also: ArrayExample.asString() now comma-separates correctly (was "[ab,c]"), and
the OAS 3.1 type-array integer path preserves an int-overflowing author example
(Integer -> Long -> BigInteger), matching the typed branch.

Adds XmlExampleSerializerTest (XML matrix parsed with a namespace-aware
DocumentBuilder + integrated namespaced-response regression cases) and
ArrayExampleTest.

docs(openapi): allow object form for OpenAPIDefinition specUrlOrPayload in embedded model

The published embedded model declared OpenAPIDefinition.specUrlOrPayload as
string only, but the runtime schema (openAPIDefinition.json) and the serializer
both support an inline JSON-object payload (as OpenAPIExpectation already
documents). Aligns the published contract with runtime behaviour.
docs(changelog): record OpenAPI re-review second-round fixes

fix(openapi): null-guard getPaths in OpenAPISerialiser for webhooks-only specs

Completes the webhooks-only hardening: OpenAPISerialiser.retrieveOperation and
retrieveOperations also dereferenced openAPI.getPaths() without a guard, so a
valid OAS 3.1 webhooks-only spec (no paths:) NPE'd on the operation-retrieval /
request-matching path even after the converter and validators were fixed. Both
now treat null paths as empty and still process webhooks.

Adds webhooks-only retrieveOperations/retrieveOperation tests.

fix(openapi): correct XML namespace scoping (descendants no longer inherit wrong namespace)

The previous XML fix de-duplicated xmlns declarations using a flat
"ever-declared" set, which is wrong: XML namespace scope is the nearest in-scope
binding, and a descendant can shadow an ancestor. Suppressing the
re-declaration made a deeper element silently inherit the wrong namespace, e.g.
a <tns:Customer> in namespace B nested in a <tns:Order> in namespace A resolved
to A, and a default-namespace A->B->A nesting resolved the grandchild to B. The
output parsed but was semantically corrupt.

The serializer now ALWAYS declares the namespace on each element that carries
xml.namespace (StAX scopes bindings correctly; a redundant identical xmlns on a
child is harmless). Also: XML-1.0-illegal characters in example/default/enum
values are stripped before writing (so a control char no longer yields an
unparseable body), a malformed xml.name is sanitised to a valid XML name and
logged, and the prolog declares XML 1.0 instead of 1.1.

Adds prefix-rebind and default-namespace-shadow regression tests (which fail on
the old code), plus illegal-character and malformed-name tests.

fix(openapi): preserve supplementary-plane chars in XML values; reject ':' in XML names

Follow-up to the XML namespace fix. Two issues in the XML-illegal-character /
name sanitisation it introduced:

- stripIllegalXmlChars iterated by char (UTF-16 code unit) and treated the
  surrogate range as illegal, so every supplementary-plane code point (emoji,
  CJK Ext-B, etc.) — legal XML 1.0 characters encoded as a surrogate pair — was
  silently deleted from example/default/enum values. It now iterates by code
  point and preserves the [0x10000-0x10FFFF] range, and logs a WARN when it
  actually strips anything.
- a ':' in an element/attribute name passed sanitisation (':' is a legal XML
  Name char) but, since this serializer manages prefixes itself, produced an
  unbound-prefix element. ':' is now treated as illegal in the sanitised name so
  output stays parseable namespace-aware.

Adds supplementary-plane-round-trip and colon-in-name regression tests.

fix(openapi): restore complete example generation and JSON-shaped XML response bodies (CI regression)

Build #985 on master failed 15 integration tests
(shouldReturnResponseByMatchingOpenAPIExpectationWithArrayParametersWithSpecAndResponse).
Two regressions from the recent OpenAPI hardening, both fixed here:

1. resolveSchemaExample was changed to SKIP a property that has no inline
   example and return a partial object. That dropped sample-only properties
   (petstore photoUrls/tags/status) from generated bodies. Returning null for
   the whole object is load-bearing — it makes the caller fall back to
   ExampleBuilder.fromSchema, which generates a COMPLETE example (explicit
   examples honoured, samples for the rest). Reverted to return null, with a
   comment so this isn't "fixed" into a partial object again.

2. Wiring XmlExampleSerializer into the response path changed long-standing
   behaviour (application/xml bodies were emitted JSON-shaped) to real XML,
   which broke the integration golden values across modules and exposed further
   XML-serializer issues (array wrapper naming). Generating real XML is reverted
   and deferred to a dedicated, properly-designed change; the response format is
   unchanged from prior releases. (XmlExampleSerializer and its unit tests are
   retained as ready-to-wire infrastructure for that future work.)

Strengthens OpenAPIConverterCorrectnessTest + its fixture to assert a schema
whose properties only partly carry inline examples still generates a COMPLETE
example (scalar, array, and enum properties without an example must appear).

fix(openapi): re-read a URL/file spec on import instead of serving a stale cached parse

The parsed OpenAPI is LRU-cached (up to 30 minutes) keyed by the spec reference
string, so re-importing a URL/file spec whose remote/file content had changed
returned the stale parse — incremental sync then computed pruning against the
old operations. HttpState.add(OpenAPIExpectation) now evicts the cache entry for
a URL/file spec before re-importing it, so the current content is read. Inline
payloads are keyed by content and need no eviction.

Adds an end-to-end test that evolves a file-backed spec and re-imports it with
NO manual cache eviction, asserting the removed operation is pruned (fails if
the import does not auto-evict).

fix(core): preserve OpenAPI 3.1 multi-element types arrays in schema serialization

AbstractSchemaSerializer only converted an OAS 3.1 `types` array to `type`
when it had exactly one element, then unconditionally removed `types`. A
multi-element 3.1 nullable idiom such as `type: ["string","null"]` was
silently dropped, so the emitted JSON schema lost its type entirely.

Translate `types` to the Draft-07 / OAS-3.0 form this serializer already
targets:
- single non-null type (+/- "null"): `type: <X>`, plus `nullable: true` when
  "null" is present
- multiple non-null types: `type` as a JSON-schema array of the non-null
  types (Draft-07 allows an array of types), plus `nullable: true` when
  "null" is present
- existing single-element behaviour unchanged

Only the current node is mutated (set type/nullable, then `types` is removed),
preserving the recurse-then-iterate invariant with no ConcurrentModification.
Example generation (ExampleBuilder.resolveOas31PrimaryType) is unaffected.

fix(core): meaningful, bounded OpenAPI validation error messages

The OpenAPI validators caught Throwables and surfaced
"... error: " + throwable.getMessage() verbatim to the control-plane
caller. When getMessage() was null this produced a useless
"OpenAPI response validation error: null", and raw untrusted exception
text reached the caller unbounded.

Introduce OpenAPIValidationErrors, a shared helper that builds a
meaningful, bounded, single-line error string: it states WHAT was being
validated (request vs response, operationId/path+method, and the aspect
such as body schema, status code, or header), names the exception type
via its simple class name when getMessage() is null (so the message is
never "...: null"), collapses whitespace/control characters to a single
line, and caps the cause text length so an oversized exception string
cannot bloat the result. The full throwable (with stack trace) is logged
at WARN via MockServerLogger so detail is not lost.

Apply consistently across OpenAPIRequestValidator,
OpenAPIResponseValidator, OpenApiContractTest, and OpenApiTrafficValidator.
The "status code not defined" message now also names the defined response
status codes. Validation PASS/FAIL decisions and result structure are
unchanged; only the human-readable error strings differ, and
already-meaningful messages are preserved.

Tests cover the null-message case (asserts the produced error carries the
operation/aspect context and the exception type, not the literal "null"),
the available-statuses naming, and the bounded single-line summary of an
oversized multi-line exception message.

fix(core): allow "not" property in httpRequest and openAPIDefinition matcher schemas

Request serializers (HttpRequestSerializer, HttpRequestDTOSerializer,
OpenAPIDefinitionSerializer, OpenAPIDefinitionDTOSerializer) emit a top-level
"not": true field for negated request matchers, but the JSON schemas these
validate against declared additionalProperties: false without a "not" property.
A serialized negated matcher therefore failed every schema branch and could not
be re-validated or re-imported.

Add "not": { "type": "boolean" } to the properties of httpRequest.json and
openAPIDefinition.json (binaryRequestDefinition.json and dnsRequestDefinition.json
already had it), and mirror the addition in the embedded OpenAPI model for
HttpRequest and OpenAPIDefinition to keep the published contract consistent.
additionalProperties: false and all other constraints are unchanged.

Add round-trip validator tests asserting a matcher JSON containing "not": true
validates with no errors for the httpRequest and openAPIDefinition branches
(verified the tests fail before the schema change and pass after).

feat(openapi): generate real XML response bodies for XML content types

When an OpenAPI response content type is XML (application/xml, text/xml,
or a +xml suffix) and there is no inline example, the generated example
is now serialised to a real, spec-correct XML body via
XmlExampleSerializer instead of the long-standing JSON-shaped string.

Fix XmlExampleSerializer array serialisation to follow the OpenAPI 3.x
XML Object rules precisely:
 - default (no xml.wrapped): an array property serialises as repeated
   elements named after the property (or items.xml.name), with no
   wrapper and no pluralisation — previously it auto-pluralised the
   wrapper and singularised items (e.g. <photoUrlss><photoUrl>...).
 - xml.wrapped: a wrapper element (the array's xml.name/wrappedName or
   the property name) contains item elements (items.xml.name or the
   property name).
 - anonymous items take a temporary name (and inherit the array's
   namespace/prefix) only for the duration of the recursive write, which
   is then restored — emitting exactly one element per item (no spurious
   <AnonymousModel> double-wrap) and never permanently renaming a shared
   cached $ref item used by more than one array.

Wire XmlExampleSerializer into OpenAPIConverter.buildHttpResponse and add
an isXmlContentType helper. The JSON and inline-example paths are
unchanged.

Update the integration golden
shouldReturnResponseByMatchingOpenAPIExpectationWithArrayParametersWithSpecAndResponse
(shared by the netty, war, and junit-jupiter integration suites) to the
new real XML body, and add focused unit tests parsing the serialised XML
with a namespace-aware DocumentBuilder (unwrapped vs wrapped arrays,
arrays of objects, attributes, shared-ref items, content-type detection).
docs(changelog): record OpenAPI follow-ups (real XML, multi-type arrays, not-schema, validation errors)

fix(openapi): render a null string example as an empty value, not the literal "null"

StringExample.asString() returned the literal text "null" for a null value,
which leaked into XML output as <field>null</field>. It now returns an empty
string, so a null string renders as an empty element. The live JSON path is
unaffected (it emits a real JSON null via JsonNodeExampleSerializer).

Adds an XmlExampleSerializerTest case asserting a null string property is an
empty element, not the text "null".

fix(openapi): render recursive XML schemas without dropping a shared property element

The XML serializer used each child Example's stored name as its element name. For
a recursive $ref schema (e.g. Node{left:$ref Node, right:$ref Node}) ExampleBuilder
reuses ONE cached Example for both properties, leaving its stored name as whichever
property built it last — so the body rendered two <right> elements and dropped
<left> (well-formed but silently wrong). The object branch now detects a child
Example shared under more than one key in the same object and renders it under the
property KEY instead of the unreliable stored name; a uniquely-placed child keeps
its own explicit name (e.g. a property-level xml.name). The child's name is applied
only for the recursive write and restored, so a shared instance is never
permanently renamed.

Adds a unit test (shared ObjectExample under two keys) and an end-to-end
OpenAPIConverter test (recursive application/xml schema asserts both <left> and
<right>); both fail without the fix.

fix(openapi): name XML array items after the array property, not the literal "array"

ExampleBuilder passed the array's type string ("array") as the array item's name,
which baked "array" into the item Example and defeated the XML serializer's
fallback (which names an item after the array property when the item name is
null). So an array whose items have no items.xml.name rendered <array> elements
(e.g. <array>...</array> instead of <tags>...</tags> / <animals>...</animals>).
JSON was unaffected (it keys objects by map entry, not Example name). Both array
build sites (ArraySchema and the OAS 3.1 type-array path) now pass a null item
name, so an item keeps its own items.xml.name when set, otherwise the serializer
applies the array property name.

Adds an end-to-end OpenAPIConverter test (array of scalars + array of objects,
neither with items.xml.name) asserting items render as <tags>/<animals>, never
<array>; it fails without the fix. The petstore golden (whose items DO set
xml.name) is unchanged.

fix(openapi): name XML elements after the property, not the schema $ref, for non-inlinable refs

ExampleBuilder resolved a $ref by naming the resulting Example after the schema
component name (e.g. "Tree"/"Node"). For the common case the parser inlines the
$ref before ExampleBuilder runs, so this never surfaced. But a recursive/circular
$ref cannot be inlined (e.g. Tree{children: array of $ref Tree},
Node{next: $ref Node}), so the resolved example carried the component name and
the XML body rendered <Tree>/<Node> elements instead of the property names
<children>/<next> — a component name is not an XML element name. The $ref is now
resolved under the current property name (the key / array context / xml.name),
not the bare ref; the $ref cache remains keyed by the ref string, so cycle
detection is unaffected. JSON output is unchanged (it keys by map entry).

Adds an end-to-end OpenAPIConverter test for a recursive array-of-$ref XML
schema asserting <children> (not <Tree>); it fails without the fix. The petstore
golden (non-recursive, inlined) is unaffected.

fix(openapi): write XML attributes before child elements regardless of declaration order

When an OpenAPI object schema declared an element-typed property before an
attribute-typed property (xml.attribute: true), XML example serialization wrote
the child element first, so the subsequent attribute write threw
"Attribute not associated with any element" (StAX requires attributes be written
immediately after the start element, before any child content). The exception was
caught upstream and the whole response body came back null/empty.

The ObjectExample branch of XmlExampleSerializer.writeTo now does two ordered
passes over the children — attribute-typed children first, then element-typed —
instead of iterating in property-declaration order, preserving the existing
shared-name save/restore logic. Property order in the schema no longer affects
attribute placement in the rendered XML.

Adds a regression test (and fixture) driving the full
spec -> buildExpectations -> response-body path with an element property declared
before its attribute property, asserting a well-formed non-empty body carrying
both the attribute and the child element.

feat(core): configurable default response headers

chokepoint just after CORS. Default empty = no behaviour change; the parsed

perf(core): avoid wasted allocations in the matcher hot path

Two behaviour-preserving allocation fixes in the per-request matcher path:

- HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher only extracts path parameters when the
  expectation actually declares path parameters. extractPathParameters
  cloned (or allocated) the request's path Parameters and ran the
  path-template regex on every match even when no {pathParam} templates
  existed; the result was unused in that case (the path-parameter matcher
  is blank and the post-match withPathParameters assignment normalises
  identically). When no path parameters are declared the request's own
  Parameters are reused, skipping the clone and the regex work.

- MatchDifference lazily allocates its differences map on the first
  recorded difference and uses a plain HashMap instead of a
  ConcurrentHashMap. A MatchDifference is request/evaluation-scoped and
  single-threaded, so no concurrent map is needed, and no map is
  allocated at all when nothing is recorded (always the case when
  detailedMatchFailures is off). getDifferences/getAllDifferences keep
  their existing contracts (null for an absent field, empty map when
  nothing was recorded).

fix(core): stop versions-map leak and make replaceValue O(log n) in expectation collections

Two memory/CPU fixes in the expectation CircularPriorityQueue and its
InMemoryExpectationKeyValueStore wrapper.

Fix 1 - versions-map eviction leak. The store kept a `versions`
ConcurrentHashMap (id -> AtomicLong) that was only pruned on
remove/compareAndRemove/clear. The backing queue evicts the eldest entry
on overflow past maxSize with no callback, so overflow-evicted keys leaked
their version entry forever. CircularPriorityQueue now exposes an
eviction listener (default no-op so existing users are unaffected) that
fires once per overflow-evicted element after it is removed from all three
backing structures; the store registers a listener that removes the
evicted id from `versions`. The map is now bounded by maxSize.

Fix 2 - replaceValue O(n) rebuild. replaceValue copied the whole
insertion-order queue to an ArrayList, found the index, cleared and
re-offered every element on each in-place update. The insertion-order
queue now holds keys instead of values (insertion order only matters for
eviction, and a key never changes on an in-place update), so replaceValue
is O(log n): it updates byKey and the sort skip-list and leaves the
insertion queue untouched, preserving the element's exact eviction slot.
add/remove/size/isEmpty/eviction adjusted to the key-based queue; add now
publishes to byKey before the insertion queue so concurrent readers never
see a queued key without a resolvable value.

The class now documents its single-writer mutation / eventually-consistent
read contract and the precondition that add() is not called for an
existing key. Adds tests proving the eviction listener fires exactly once
per overflow eviction and never on explicit remove/replace, that
replaceValue preserves eviction position, and that the versions map stays
bounded to exactly the surviving keys when far more than maxSize entries
are registered.

perf(core): skip matching executor for literal non-matches and bound the pool

RegexStringMatcher now short-circuits the timeout-protected regex executor
path when the value is a pure-ASCII literal (no regex metacharacters and all
characters <= 0x7F). For such a value NottableString.matches() — which compiles
with CASE_INSENSITIVE|UNICODE_CASE|DOTALL and does an anchored full match —
produces a result provably identical to the equalsIgnoreCase comparison that
already ran and failed, so a literal non-match no longer submits a task to the
thread pool. Non-ASCII values keep the regex path because UNICODE_CASE folding
can diverge from String.equalsIgnoreCase; the same guard is applied to the
matched value in the control-plane matched->matcher direction.

MatchingTimeoutExecutor replaces the unbounded cached thread pool with a
bounded ThreadPoolExecutor (core 0, max availableProcessors*2, SynchronousQueue,
60s keepalive, daemon threads). On saturation submission is rejected and treated
exactly like a timeout — the safe sentinel (non-match) is returned — so a burst
of slow patterns can never spawn unbounded threads or block a Netty worker. The
reversed-regex control-plane check is now evaluated once and reused for both the
match decision and the DEBUG "would match" trace, removing a double submission.

Adds tests proving a pure-ASCII literal non-match submits zero tasks to the
pool, a real regex still does, non-ASCII literals keep the regex path, and
covering the looksLikeRegex metacharacter classifier. Existing exact,
case-insensitive, regex, ReDoS-timeout, notted-string and numeric-comparison
behaviour is unchanged.

fix(core): matching pool saturation must never corrupt a match result

The bounded matching-timeout pool used a small cap (cores*2) with a
SynchronousQueue and AbortPolicy, and callWithTimeout converted a
RejectedExecutionException into the timeout sentinel (a non-match). Under
legitimate concurrent load with more in-flight evaluations than the cap,
submissions were rejected and a regex that would have matched silently
returned non-match — an intermittent correctness regression distinct from a
real timeout.

Raise the cap to a generous max(64, cores*16) so rejection is effectively
unreachable under realistic concurrency, and on any residual rejection run
the task inline on the calling thread returning its real result instead of
the sentinel. The inline path preserves the normal exception contract
(PatternSyntaxException still propagates) and clears any residual interrupt
flag; it logs a distinct WARN so operators can detect saturation. This trades
per-call timeout isolation for never corrupting a match result only under
extreme saturation — the correct trade for a mock server.

Add two regression tests in the sequential Surefire phase: a high-concurrency
test that fires hundreds of thousands of genuine matches and asserts zero
spurious non-matches, and a deterministic test that saturates the pool and
proves a rejected submission runs inline and returns its real result.

fix(core): scenario consume-then-skip and O(n^2) expectation registration

Two correctness/performance fixes in RequestMatchers.

Scenario consume-then-skip: firstMatchingExpectation and
firstMatchingEarlyExpectation called scenarioManager.matchesAndTransition()
up front, side-effecting the scenario to its new state before later gates
(percentage, clustered Times CAS, consumeMatch) could still skip the
expectation. A matching-but-skipped expectation therefore advanced the
scenario without ever being served. The gate now uses the pure
matchesState() check and the transition is applied only at the commit
point, after percentage and Times/CAS consumption succeed.

O(n^2) registration: on the default in-memory (non-clustered) backend,
add()/update() called reconcileFromBackend(), which snapshots the whole
backend into a HashMap and walks every entry; the backend store's put()
also fires an invalidation listener that calls reconcileFromBackend()
again, giving two full O(n) reconciles per add. reconcileFromBackend()
now returns early via a cheap eviction-only trim when the backend is not
clustered, restoring linear registration. The full remote-add/remote-update
reconcile is retained unchanged for clustered backends.

Adds a percentage-skip scenario regression test, a clustered remote-add
reconcile test, and migrates the remote-update reconcile test to a
clustered backend (the only path on which it is reachable).

fix(core): make commit-point scenario transition atomic (cross-node exactly-once)

The prior consume-then-skip fix moved the scenario transition to the
commit point but used the non-atomic scenarioManager.transitionState()
(an unconditional put). On a clustered backend this dropped the
documented cross-node "exactly one winner" guarantee
(docs/code/clustered-state.md): two nodes racing the same scenario step
(Started->Step1) both pass the pure matchesState() gate, both read
"Started", both serve, and both put("Step1").

firstMatchingExpectation and firstMatchingEarlyExpectation now apply the
required-state transition atomically via
scenarioManager.matchesAndTransition() — a CAS on the scenario-state KV
store. The gate-time matchesState() check is kept (so a percentage/Times
skip still does not transition); the commit-point CAS re-checks the state
atomically. Under single-writer (single-node default, in-memory backend)
the CAS always succeeds — no single-node regression. Under concurrency
(single OR multi node) exactly one racer wins; the loser clears
responseInProgress and falls through without serving, mirroring the
existing clustered Times-CAS lost-race handling.

The entry-state transition (no required state to CAS against) stays an
unconditional transitionState. The two blocks remain mutually exclusive.

matchesAndTransition is the correct primitive for BOTH the local and
clustered backends, so it is used unconditionally with no isClustered()
branch. The CAS runs after consumeMatch(): for the dominant unlimited-
Times case consumeMatch is a no-op, so a lost CAS loses nothing; for the
rare limited-Times + scenario case a lost CAS means a Times unit was
already consumed on this node — an accepted tradeoff, strictly better
than double-serving the same step.

Adds a guard test (scenarioStepShouldBeServedExactlyOnceAcrossTwoNodes)
that races two real clustered Infinispan nodes through the production
RequestMatchers serving path and asserts exactly one node serves the
Started->Step1 step — closing the gap left by
twoNodesCannotDoubleTransitionSameScenario, which only exercised
ScenarioManager directly. Verified the guard fails (got 2) against the
prior unconditional put and passes with the CAS.

Corrects the changelog wording: the reachable second-skip is the
percentage gate and the concurrent cross-node CAS race, not an
exhausted-Times gate.

feat(core): jsonPath/xPath request-body extraction in Velocity and JavaScript templates

The Mustache template engine already exposed jsonPath/xPath lambdas for

- New RequestBodyExtractionHelper centralises the extraction so all three

- Mustache refactored to delegate to the shared helper (no divergent

- Velocity: $jsonPath.find("$.field") and $xPath.find("/element/key").
- JavaScript (GraalJS): jsonPath('$.field') / xPath('/element/key') exposed
  as callable functions in the script scope.

Adds behavioural tests for both engines (JSON jsonPath, XML xPath, and a
missing-path case) and updates the response-templates consumer docs.

feat(openapi): honour more JSON-Schema constraints in example generation

ExampleBuilder now respects array minItems/maxItems, string pattern
(regex), numeric exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum, the time string
format, and minProperties on free-form objects when generating example
data, so generated examples are less likely to fail a consumer's own
validators.

- Arrays emit minItems items (clamped to a cap of 5) instead of always a

feat(core): per-upstream forward/proxy observability metrics and span attributes

Forwarded and proxied requests are now observable by the upstream they hit
and how it performed. The client-side Timing computed by NettyHttpClient was
already measured but discarded; it now feeds two new Prometheus metrics and

feat(core): add clusterSharedTimesEnabled opt-out for clustered Times CAS

Clustered limited-Times matching runs consumeTimesViaBackendCas on the
Netty request-worker (event-loop) thread. Each compareAndSet on a
REPL_SYNC backend is a synchronous replicated write, so under same-
expectation cross-node contention the worker can block for up to
MAX_CAS_RETRIES (10) replicated writes (the get() reads the local
replica and does not hit the network).

Add an off-by-default config property clusterSharedTimesEnabled
(default true, preserving the fleet-wide exactly-N guarantee). When set
to false, isClusteredLimitedTimes returns false and limited-Times
matching falls back to the node-local fast path with no synchronous
backend round-trip on the worker thread, trading exactly-N for lower,
more predictable matching latency in latency-sensitive clustered
deployments.

The single-node / non-clustered path is unchanged. Promote
MAX_CAS_RETRIES to a named constant and document the worst-case
worker-thread blocking bound and the opt-out in code and in
docs/code/clustered-state.md.

Tests: RequestMatchersStateBackendTest proves the shared CAS is used by
default (backend counter decremented) and bypassed when disabled
(backend counter untouched, node-local Times decremented); real-
Infinispan ClusteredTwoNodeTest adds sharedTimesCasBypassedWhenShared
TimesDisabled asserting the replicated counter is never decremented when
the knob is off.

fix(core): give matches() a non-torn view of the matcher criterion under concurrent update

A single HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher instance is shared between the control
plane (apply()/update(), single-writer) and the data plane (matches(), many
Netty event-loop threads). apply() reassigned this.httpRequest and ~13
non-volatile field matchers in place, sequentially, so a control-plane update to
an expectation racing live traffic could let an in-flight matches() observe a
half-rebuilt matcher (new httpRequest paired with a stale field matcher),
yielding a wrong match result or a transient NullPointerException.

Group every per-criterion compiled field (httpRequest, httpRequests, the method/
path/pathParameter/queryStringParameter/body/header/cookie/keepAlive/ssl/protocol
matchers and the jsonSchemaBodyParser) into an immutable Compiled holder built
fully inside apply() and published through one volatile reference. matches()
snapshots that reference once on entry and reads everything from the snapshot, so
it sees either the entire old criterion or the entire new one — never a torn mix.
The writer stays single-writer; only the reader's visibility/atomicity changes.

Behaviour is unchanged: apply()'s unchanged-request early return, the
httpRequests singletonList semantics, the cached-hashCode equals/hashCode
contract, toString and serialization (which read getHttpRequest()), and the
control-plane body-matching fallback are all preserved. excludedFields is updated
to exclude the new holder field (the reflective equals/hashCode/toString are
overridden for this class, so this only affects the toString fallback).

Adds HttpRequestPropertiesMatcherConcurrencyTest: one writer flips a shared
matcher between two criteria while eight readers match a fixed request that
matches neither criterion, so any true is an impossible torn-read fingerprint.
It fails reliably on the pre-fix code and passes on the fix.

perf(core): parse request body once per request in matching hot path

During firstMatchingExpectation's N-expectation scan, a request with an
XML body matched against M JSON-schema/JSON/JSON-path expectations had its
body re-parsed (XML DOM parse + ObjectMapper serialisation) once per
candidate expectation inside JsonSchemaBodyDecoder.convertToJson, even
though the conversion result is a pure function of the request body and
the target content type, not of the specific expectation.

Memoize the XML-to-JSON conversion on the HttpRequest via a transient,
JSON-ignored convertedBodyCache keyed by conversion target, so the body
is parsed once per request and reused across the scan. The cache is
invalidated by all withBody setters and excluded from equals/hashCode/
clone/serialization. Behaviour is unchanged: the same converted value is
returned, the original-body-string fall-back on parse failure is
preserved, and the XML branch still never propagates an exception.

The form-parameter branch is deliberately not cached because its output
depends on the matcher's parameterStyle; the JSON branch already does no
parsing.

perf(core): memoize request-side key/value conversion across expectation scan

The header/cookie/query/path-parameter matchers (MultiValueMapMatcher and
HashMapMatcher) reconstructed a NottableStringMultiMap/NottableStringHashMap
from the incoming request's entries on every matcher evaluation. During the
firstMatchingExpectation scan that rebuilt the same request-side structure once
per candidate expectation, allocating fresh entry lists on both sides each call.

Convert the request (matched) side once per request and reuse it across all
matcher evaluations: the converted form is memoized on the request-side
collection (KeysToMultiValues / KeysAndValues) and the derived entryList is
computed once on the immutable converted map.

Correctness:
- The memo is keyed by controlPlaneMatcher (two slots) because the converted
  form embeds a control-plane-sensitive RegexStringMatcher; a data-plane
  conversion is never served to a control-plane caller or vice versa.
- The memo is invalidated on every mutation. KeysToMultiValues clears it from
  isModified() (now concrete; Headers/Parameters call super.isModified());
  KeysAndValues clears it from each mutator. This covers query parameters that
  ExpandedParameterDecoder.splitParameters mutates in place mid-scan, so a
  re-split request never matches against a stale conversion.

Behaviour is identical: the memoized map is constructed with the same arguments
as before. New RequestSideMatcherMemoizationTest proves the conversion is reused
across evaluations, kept separate per control-plane flag, invalidated on
mutation, and that query-parameter matching is correct across multiple
expectations after an in-place split.

fix(core): notted key in MATCHING_KEY mode now asserts key absence

In KeyMatchStyle.MATCHING_KEY, getAll(matcherKey) collected values by
running the regex matcher over actual keys. A notted matcher key ("!X")
then "matched" every actual key NOT named X via the XOR not-semantics,
aggregating an unrelated bag of values rather than expressing the intended
"this key must be absent" assertion.

Special-case a notted matcher key in the MATCHING_KEY branch so it means
"no actual (non-notted) key matches the un-notted value", mirroring the
SUB_SET semantic in SubSetMatcher#nottedAndPresent. Non-notted MATCHING_KEY
behaviour and the entire SUB_SET path are unchanged. Headers/query/params
default to SUB_SET, so this only affects explicit MATCHING_KEY use.

Adds tests pinning the absent/present cases, a decisive regression test
where an aggregated value would have matched under the old code, and
empty-map, notted-regex, notted+optional, and mixed-key edge cases.

fix(core): harden control-plane body fast path against null stringification

The control-plane clear/verify/retrieve body fast path compared bodies via
String.valueOf(...).equalsIgnoreCase(...). When a body was null this collapsed
to the literal "null", so two absent bodies compared equal and a literal "null"
body filter could slip through the fast path against a request with no body.

Require both the filter and candidate request bodies to be non-null before the
stringified fast-path comparison; a no-body request now falls through to the
real body matcher rather than the string-collapse shortcut. The data-plane path
is untouched (the change is inside the controlPlaneMatcher branch).

Add a parameterized NOT-operator x fail-fast equivalence cube test pinning that
the duplicated NOT composition produces an identical verdict with matchersFailFast
on and off, matching the NOT-composition truth table, and add control-plane
"null"-filter body regression tests.

fix(core): meaningful closest-match diagnostic and at-most-once lazy matcher removal

W3-2: the closest-expectation "matched X/Y fields" log in
RequestMatchers.firstMatchingExpectation was computed against all 16
MatchDifference.Field constants (inflating the denominator with the
DNS/binary/OpenAPI/operation fields a plain HTTP request never exercises)
and a numerator derived from getAllDifferences().size(), which collapses
to at most one under the default fail-fast matching — so almost any
mismatch reported "matched 15/16". The denominator is now the
protocol-applicable field count (10 for HTTP, 3 for DNS, 1 for binary),
and the numerator is recomputed in the already-gated cold path
(no match AND INFO enabled) by re-evaluating the closest matcher with
fail-fast disabled and suppressMatchResultLogging set, counting the
applicable fields that actually failed. The hot serving scan is
unchanged and keeps fail-fast; no per-scan cost is added.

W3-4: several data-plane scans independently observe a matcher as
!responseInProgress && !active and each scheduled an async removal for
it. The removal is idempotent but the duplicate submissions wasted
scheduler and backend load under churn. AbstractHttpRequestMatcher now
CAS-guards the claim (tryScheduleRemoval), reset when the matcher is
reused in place, so only the first observer schedules the removal. The
clustered Times-CAS-exhausted removal paths are a different trigger and
are intentionally left unguarded. Actual matching, consumeMatch, and
Times are untouched.
docs(changelog): note wave-3 matcher fixes

fix(core): not() expectations match correctly with fail-fast matching on

The fail-fast early-non-match short-circuit in HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher
negated a partial "failed so far?" signal (failures != 0) through the NOT
operators. That is only sound with zero NOT flags: with an odd number of NOT
flags and zero failures accumulated so far, failures != 0 is false, which
applyNotOperators flips to true, so the matcher prematurely returned a wrong
non-match. Every field that matched before the first mismatching field thus
falsely short-circuited a NOT expectation, and matchersFailFast defaults to on.

Example: not(request().withMethod("GET").withPath("/test")) failed to match an
incoming GET /other even though it plainly is not GET /test. Affected the path,
header and body fields (method escaped only because it is evaluated first).

Only short-circuit when no NOT operator is in play, preserving the fail-fast
optimisation for the common (no-NOT) case; for NOT expectations evaluate every
field and rely on the single correct final applyNotOperators(failures == 0, ...).
Diagnostic accumulation and per-field failure bookkeeping are unchanged.

Extend the NOT x fail-fast equivalence cube to drive the mismatch on path,
header and body (not just method), asserting fail-fast and non-fail-fast verdicts
are identical and equal the NOT truth table, and add an explicit named repro.

feat(core): opt-in case-sensitive matching via matchExactCase

Add a new boolean configuration property matchExactCase
(MOCKSERVER_MATCH_EXACT_CASE, default false) that makes data-plane
request matching of the method, path and regex body case-sensitive
(exact case) when enabled. The default (false) preserves the historical
case-insensitive behaviour byte-for-byte.

When enabled, the equalsIgnoreCase fallback in RegexStringMatcher is
skipped and the regex is compiled without CASE_INSENSITIVE|UNICODE_CASE
for the method, path and regex-body matchers only. Header names and
values, cookie names and values, and query string parameters always
remain case-insensitive regardless of this setting (they use the
no-fixed-value RegexStringMatcher constructor, which keeps the default
case-insensitive behaviour). Control-plane matchers (clear/verify/
retrieve filters) also stay case-insensitive so administrative
operations are unaffected.

Plumbing: a new caseSensitive flag is threaded through the fixed-value
RegexStringMatcher instances (method/path in HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher
and regex body in BodyMatcherBuilder) via additive constructor overloads
that default to false; NottableString.matches gains an additive
matches(input, caseSensitive) overload caching a separate
case-sensitive Pattern. Property wired through ConfigurationProperties,
Configuration and ConfigurationDTO exactly like matchersFailFast.

Documented in mockserver.example.properties, configuration-reference.md
and the consumer configuration_properties.html. Tests cover both flag
states for method/path/regex-body, that exact string bodies stay
case-sensitive, and that headers/cookies/query stay case-insensitive
when the flag is on.

fix(core): null string request body leaves body unset, mirroring HttpResponse

HttpRequest.withBody((String) null) coerced null into an empty StringBody
(getBodyAsString() returned ""), whereas HttpResponse.withBody((String) null)
guards the null and leaves the body unset (getBodyAsString() returns null).

Harmonise the request side to the response side by guarding the null in the
HttpRequest.withBody(String) overload, so both message types treat a null
string body identically: the body field stays null, the request serialises
with no body field, and a request expectation built with a null string body
still match-alls bodies (unchanged). Passing an empty string is unaffected.

The (String, Charset) overload already guarded null; the byte[]/Body overloads
are intentionally left as-is. Real incoming requests with no body already
produced a null body via the decoder, so no new null-body code path is
introduced at any matcher, template, forward or serialisation call site.

Add comprehensive null-body coverage to HttpRequestTest.

fix(core): share request body-dispatch with response matcher for full parity

Response body matching previously used a stripped-down reimplementation of the
request body dispatch that was missing several behaviours: it did not convert an
XML or form actual body to JSON before a JSON/JSON-schema/JSON-path matcher,
ignored an optional template body, mis-routed a multipart matcher to the generic
string path, and only checked the decompressed (not the original/compressed)
bytes for a binary matcher. A JSON or XML matcher against a response with no body
could also trigger a swallowed internal NullPointer, producing a silent
non-match with no diagnostic.

Extract the request matcher's body dispatch into a single shared helper
(BodyMatching) parameterised over a small BodySource abstraction
(getBodyAsString / getBodyAsRawBytes / getOriginalBody / getFirstHeader and the
template body's optional flag), used by BOTH HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher and
HttpResponseMatcher. JsonSchemaBodyDecoder.convertToJson is generalised over a
BodySource so an XML/form response body converts to JSON too; the request path
keeps its per-request XML->JSON memoisation, control-plane BodyDTO re-parse
fallback, and MatchDifference diagnostics unchanged (the request adapter exposes
the existing cache and the originating request for the failure log).

The request hot path is behaviourally identical: branch ordering, the binary
original/compressed null-context dual-match, the currentField(BODY) side-effect,
the optional short-circuit, and the JSON-family exception handling all match the
previous inline code, and the full existing matcher suite passes with zero test
changes. The response side now matches the request side, including a clean
non-match (no swallowed exception) for a JSON/XML matcher against a no-body
response.

fix(core): correctness and robustness fixes in response-aware verification

Response-aware verification in MockServerEventLog had several verified
defects, all fixed here with proving tests:

- Response verification (verifyResponse and the response-sequence branch)
  counted MockServer's own auto-generated NO_MATCH_RESPONSE 404s, not just
  mock-produced responses. A new responseVerificationLogPredicate (the same
  filter as expectationLogPredicate: EXPECTATION_RESPONSE + FORWARDED_REQUEST)
  is used only by the verification paths; the shared requestResponseLogPredicate
  used by /retrieve is unchanged and still returns NO_MATCH_RESPONSE.
- A response-aware sequence supplying both httpRequests and httpResponses of
  different non-empty lengths padded the shorter list with nulls (a null matcher
  always matches), silently passing on the unspecified steps. It is now rejected
  with a clear error; request-only or response-only sequences stay valid.
- A recorded pair with a null request NPE'd in a request-constrained step and
  was masked as a generic exception; it is now treated as non-matching.
- A failing response-sequence message serialized the requests (often empty for
  a response-only sequence) instead of the responses; it now serializes the
  expected and recorded responses.
- An entirely-empty VerificationSequence passed vacuously; it is now rejected.
- A verification whose request-filter matcher build threw left the result future
  uncompleted and hung the caller; the two private retrieveLogEntries overloads
  now route a build failure to an empty stream so the consumer always completes.

test(core): align stale verification-sequence assertions with response-aware contract

A prior response-aware verification fix changed two failure messages, leaving
three pre-existing assertions on the old contract:

- a response-aware sequence (uses withResponses) now reports
  "Response sequence not found" instead of "Request sequence not found"
  (MockServerEventLogRequestLogEntryVerificationTest, AbstractProxyIntegrationTest)
- an entirely-empty sequence is now rejected with
  "No expectations, requests or responses specified in verification sequence"
  rather than vacuously passing (MockServerEventLogRequestLogEntryVerificationSequenceTest)

Update the stale assertions to the new contract. Request-only sequences keep
the "Request sequence not found" message and are unchanged.

feat(core): response matcher reason-phrase exact-case, cookies, and diff plumbing

Add three additive capabilities to HttpResponseMatcher:

- reason-phrase now honours the matchExactCase flag (parity with the response
  body), via the 4-arg RegexStringMatcher overload instead of a hardcoded
  case-insensitive matcher; default (false) behaviour is unchanged.
- structured cookie matching mirrored from the request matcher using
  HashMapMatcher: sub-set semantics (extra response cookies allowed), missing
  required cookies fail, notted cookie values honoured; no cookie template
  places no constraint.
- a matches(MatchDifference, HttpResponse) overload that records per-field
  differences while computing the same boolean as matches(HttpResponse) (which
  now delegates with a null context). Response fields reuse existing
  MatchDifference.Field constants (statusCode/reasonPhrase -> OPERATION,
  headers -> HEADERS, cookies -> COOKIES, body -> BODY) so no new enum constants
  are added.

Default response matching is unchanged unless a new field/flag is used.

feat(core): status-code range and operator matching for response verification

Add a nullable statusCodeRange expression to HttpResponse so response
verification can match a status by class range ("2XX" matches 200-299,
case-insensitive "2xx" accepted) or numeric operator (">= 400", "> 200",
"< 300", "<= 204", "== 201") instead of only an exact statusCode.

A new package-private StatusCodeMatcher evaluates the expression: blank
range falls back to exact-equality of statusCode (null exact matches all),
class ranges resolve to [N00, N99], and numeric operators reuse the existing
NumericComparisonMatcher rather than reimplementing operator parsing. An
unparseable expression is a clean non-match (logged at DEBUG), never a throw.

HttpResponseMatcher builds a StatusCodeMatcher only when an exact statusCode
or a statusCodeRange is set; with neither, status is unconstrained. When a
range is present it takes precedence over the exact code. Default behaviour
(no range, exact statusCode) is byte-for-byte unchanged, and statusCodeRange
is verification-only: it is never written to the wire when serving a response.

statusCodeRange round-trips in JSON (model and DTO serializers, DTO bean,
JSON schema and embedded OpenAPI model) and is omitted when null.

feat(core): detailedVerificationFailures closest-response diff for response verify

Response verification previously ignored detailedVerificationFailures: a
failing response verify returned only the serialized expected-vs-recorded
responses with no field-level guidance, while request verification has long
appended a closest-match diff via buildClosestMatchDiff.

Wire the same diagnostic into verifyResponse. On a failed response verify,
when detailedVerificationFailures is enabled and at least one mock-produced
response was recorded, buildClosestResponseMatchDiff runs the response
matcher against each recorded response (bounded by
maximumNumberOfRequestToReturnInVerificationFailure), picks the one with the
fewest differing fields, and appends a field-level diff (statusCode/
reasonPhrase under operation, plus headers, cookies and body) to the failure
message. The gating mirrors the request side exactly and the diff is
diagnostic only - it never changes the pass/fail result.

The MatchDifference is constructed with a non-null request (the verification
request when present, else an empty request() placeholder) so the TRACE
logging path that dereferences the request cannot NPE on a response-only
verify.

Scope: single-response verifyResponse only. The response-sequence failure
path is left as a follow-up.

Tests cover diff present when enabled (status and body), absent when
disabled, absent when no responses recorded, closest-by-fewest-fields
selection, and no NPE under TRACE logging.

feat(netty): opt-in upstream HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection pool + cached forward-proxy PEM

Add an opt-in connection pool to the forward/proxy client so idle keep-alive
HTTP/1.1 upstream connections are reused instead of opening a fresh TCP (+TLS)
connection per forwarded/proxied request.

P1 - forwardConnectionPoolEnabled (default false, byte-identical off-path):
- HttpForwardConnectionPool keys idle channels by host:port:scheme, honours
  HTTP keep-alive, evicts idle channels after forwardConnectionPoolIdleTimeoutMillis
  (default 30000), and degrades gracefully under saturation (surplus beyond
  forwardConnectionPoolMaxIdlePerKey, default 8, are closed not blocked).
- Only plain HTTP/1.1 is pooled. HTTP/2, HTTP/3, binary forwarding and
  proxy-tunnelled requests bypass the pool; streaming responses are excluded
  automatically because the streaming relay handler removes HttpClientHandler
  before the pool-return path runs.
- Connections the upstream closed or that returned Connection: close are never
  reused (acquire() re-checks isActive(); closeFuture evicts idle channels).
- HttpClientHandler returns the channel to the pool before completing the
  captured response future; RESPONSE_FUTURE is re-armed per reuse and the
  connection-error handlers are null-safe for idle pooled channels.

P2 - cache parsed forward-proxy PEM material by file *contents* (not path) so an
unchanged key/chain is parsed once while a rotated file is re-parsed.

Tests: new behaviour tests prove single-connection reuse on a same-upstream
burst, no reuse on Connection: close or server-closed channels, and no response
corruption under concurrent same-upstream load; plus configuration round-trip
coverage. Full mockserver-netty -am suite green.

feat(core): synthesize schema-valid GraphQL responses from a registered SDL/introspection schema

Add an optional schema field to the GraphQL expectation body (SDL text or an
introspection JSON result). When a matched GraphQL expectation carries a schema
and its response action has no body, MockServer synthesizes a schema-valid
{"data": {...}} response from the incoming query — respecting field types,
nullability, lists, nested objects, scalars (incl. common custom scalars),
enums, aliases, __typename, inline fragments and named fragment spreads. Only
the requested selection set appears in the response.

Implemented as a self-contained GraphQLResponseSynthesizer (graphql-java 22.3,
Java 11 bytecode — runs on the Java 17 floor) in a new org.mockserver.graphql
package. Wired at the response-synthesis layer in HttpResponseActionHandler via
a new handle(response, request, matchedRequest) overload; the two dispatch call
sites in HttpActionHandler pass the already-in-scope matched request (minimal,
flagged). Synthesis is fail-soft: an unparseable schema or non-GraphQL request
is logged at WARN and leaves the response body unset. A recursion-depth guard
bounds cyclic fragment spreads.

The schema field round-trips in JSON in both the nested graphQL form and the
flat body form (order-independent capture) and is included in equals/hashCode.

graphql-java is ceiling-pinned below the next major (>=25.0.0) in dependabot and
recorded in docs/operations/security.md, mirroring the checkstyle/infinispan
Java-17-floor precedent.

C1 (expose): add control-plane endpoint PUT /mockserver/contractTest that runs an
OpenAPI spec as contract tests against a live service. For each operation MockServer
builds a representative example request, sends it to the target baseUrl (reusing the
wired HTTP client via the existing replayHandler, with the same SSRF protection as the
forward and replay paths), and validates the response against the spec. Returns a
structured pass/fail-per-operation JSON report. An optional operationId restricts the
run to a single operation. Wired in HttpState.handle() alongside the existing verbs,
gated by controlPlaneRequestAuthenticated like its neighbours.

C2 (enforce): add config flag enforceResponseValidationForMocks (default false). When
enabled (alongside openAPIResponseValidation), a mock response that fails OpenAPI
response validation is replaced with a 502 describing the violations, mirroring the
proxy path's validateProxyEnforce. The default keeps the historical advisory-only
behaviour (violations logged, response returned unchanged).

Also guards OpenApiContractTest against specs with no paths block.

Tests: behavioural mock-path enforcement tests (flag off = unchanged, flag on = 502);
contract-test endpoint tests for conformant, violating, and missing-baseUrl cases;
config coverage (default, system property, instance setter override).

Docs: configuration_properties.html (flag) and using_openapi.html (endpoint).

fix(core): run contract-test loop off the Netty event loop

handleContractTest ran the blocking per-operation
replayHandler.apply(outbound).get(timeoutMillis) loop synchronously on
the Netty event-loop (workerGroup) thread. Because the outbound
NettyHttpClient shares the same workerGroup, the outbound I/O could be
assigned to the very thread parked in .get(), self-deadlocking the event
loop and forcing a timeout; even without deadlock it held a worker thread
for maxSocketTimeout x operationCount, starving every connection pinned
to that thread.

Offload the entire OpenApiContractTest.runContractTests run onto the
scheduler's executor and write the response / complete canHandle from
that off-loop worker, mirroring handleReplay. Input validation, the
control-plane auth gate, SSRF validateForwardTarget on baseUrl, 400
handling, status codes and the JSON report shape are unchanged.

Add tests proving the fix: an asynchronous replay future completed from a
separate thread (not completedFuture), asserting the calling thread
returns before the response is produced and the blocking .get() runs on a
different thread; plus a never-completing future asserting the
per-operation timeout is honoured rather than hanging.

perf(core): efficiency quick wins on log/matcher/serialization paths + dropped-event counter

Behaviour-preserving micro-optimisations in mockserver-core, plus one new
observable counter:

- MockServerEventLog.clear(): a null filter now short-circuits to "match all"
  instead of building a fresh empty (uncached, unique-correlation-id) matcher and
  scanning every entry through it. An empty matcher matched every entry anyway, so
  this is behaviour-identical while removing the per-clear uncached matcher rebuild.
- HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher: only allocate the JsonSchemaBodyDecoder when the
  body matcher is a JSON-type matcher (JsonString/JsonSchema/JsonPath) or the
  matcher is control-plane (the control-plane body path can build a JSON matcher
  from the candidate request's BodyDTO at match time and still needs the decoder).
- ObjectMapperFactory: cache custom-serializer export ObjectMappers by
  serializer-set signature (sorted serializer class names + serialiseDefaultValues)
  in a ConcurrentHashMap instead of rebuilding a full mapper per export call.

New observability (the only behaviour change):

- Dropped log events (disruptor ring buffer full) are now counted instead of
  dropped silently for INFO/DEBUG. MockServerEventLog exposes an always-available
  getDroppedLogEventCount(), mirrors drops to a new mock_server_dropped_log_events
  Prometheus counter (lazy, null-safe, off when metrics are disabled), and logs a
  single WARN on the first drop. Adds MockServerEventLogDroppedEventsTest.

Full mockserver-core suite green (7660 tests, 0 failures).

fix(core): clear(null) preserves request-less log entries

The efficiency quick-win for MockServerEventLog.clear() short-circuited the
clear-everything branch to match=true unconditionally, which changed observable
behaviour: request-less entries (getHttpRequests() is the length-0 array, e.g.
SERVER_CONFIGURATION / TRACE / WARN / EXCEPTION / CLEARED logged without a
request) were previously NOT cleared by clear(null) — the old per-request loop
only set matches inside the inner for, which never ran for a length-0 array.

Guard the short-circuit with requests.length > 0 so request-less entries survive
exactly as before, while still avoiding the uncached correlation-id matcher
rebuild and MatchDifference allocation (the perf win stands). Pin the preserved
behaviour with a test asserting a SERVER_CONFIGURATION entry survives clear(null)
while a request-bearing entry is removed. Tighten the changelog wording to
describe the length>0 guard rather than an unqualified "match all".

feat(core): one-command record round-trip via retrieve?forwardUnmatchedTo

Add an optional forwardUnmatchedTo=<upstream> parameter to the

session: subsequent traffic that matches no expectation is forwarded to
the upstream and recorded, and the same/next retrieve returns the
recorded expectations (deduplicated/templatized when enabled) in the
requested format (java/javascript/python/go/csharp/ruby/rust/php/json).

proxyRemotePort and attemptToProxyIfNoMatchingExpectation, run traffic,
then retrieve) for the common proxy-an-upstream then get-code flow.

80/443) and is SSRF-validated against the same forwardProxyBlockPrivate
Networks policy as the forward/replay paths BEFORE any state is mutated
or any connection is made: a blocked upstream returns 403 and a
malformed value returns 400, both leaving configuration untouched.
proxyRemoteHost/proxyRemotePort are made volatile since they can now be
set at runtime from the control plane and read on the Netty I/O threads.

fix(core): effective-config reports memoised default as (default), not runtime-set

readPropertyHierarchically caches every value it resolves, including the
built-in default of a property left unset in all tiers. effectiveConfiguration()

tier value, mislabelled it source=runtime-set with the concrete default value
(e.g. metricsEnabled unset reported value=[false] source=[runtime-set] instead
of value=[(default)] source=[default]). This broke the GET /mockserver/config
diagnostic on any running server once startup had read the property.

dedicated registry and only attribute a cached value to runtime-set when it
both came through a setter and differs from the static-tier resolution.

feat(core): Accept-header content-negotiation matching

Add an opt-in `accept:<media-type>` directive for key/value header (and
cookie/query/parameter) matching. When the expected value is written as
`accept:application/json`, the actual request `Accept` header is parsed per
RFC 7231 §5.3.2 — honouring q-values (default 1, q=0 excludes), subtype and
full wildcards, and most-specific-range preference — and the expectation
matches when the desired media type is acceptable.

Parsing is lenient (malformed ranges / q-values are skipped, never thrown);
a blank Accept header never matches. Negation uses the standard NottableString
`!` prefix (`!accept:text/html`).

Wired into RegexStringMatcher's key/value-map (numericComparison) branch,
mirroring NumericComparisonMatcher, so it is enabled only for header/cookie/
query/param matching and never leaks into the fixed-value method/path/body/
reason-phrase matchers. Existing exact/regex header matching is byte-for-byte
unchanged when the directive is not used.

feat(core): conditional and chainable response modifiers

Add two additive, backward-compatible opt-ins to HttpResponseModifier so
forwarded/proxied response header and cookie edits can be gated by a condition
and composed as an ordered chain.

A HttpResponseModifierCondition (statusCode, statusCodeRange such as "5xx",
responseHasHeader, requestHasHeader) restricts a modifier to apply only when the
in-flight response and optionally the original request match. A modifiers list
applies an ordered chain where each modifier observes the previous one's output;
a wrapping condition gates the whole chain.

HttpResponse.update gains a request-aware overload so conditions can reference
the request; the legacy two-arg form delegates with a null request and behaves
identically. The forward-template and override-forwarded-request action handlers
pass the original request through. DTO, JSON validation schemas, the Java
code-generation serializer, and the consumer OpenAPI spec are all updated so the
new shape round-trips and validates, while existing single-modifier expectations
serialize and behave byte-for-byte unchanged.

(grpcBidiResponse.messages[]) and rule response messages
