Templating is opt-in: response messages with no templateType are emitted
byte-for-byte unchanged (all existing bidi tests pass unchanged). JAVASCRIPT is
rejected at runtime for bidi stream responses since it constructs a full
response object rather than a renderable text fragment.

The control-plane JSON schema (grpcBidiResponse.json) now declares templateType
(enum VELOCITY/JAVASCRIPT/MUSTACHE, mirroring httpTemplate.json) on both the
eager-messages item and the rule-responses item, so a templated bidi expectation
is accepted over REST; previously additionalProperties:false rejected it,
making the feature unusable via the control plane. JsonSchemaExpectationValidator
tests cover both the eager-messages and rule-responses shapes plus an
unknown-templateType rejection.

Also hardens the DELAYED (delayMillis>0) message path on both transports: a
render/toProtobuf exception thrown inside a scheduled task is NOT routed to
Netty's exceptionCaught, so it previously escaped and left the stream hanging
with no grpc-status trailer. The scheduled write bodies (H2 writeAndContinue;
H3 writeNext and the eager emit) now wrap the work in try/catch and on failure
write an INTERNAL grpc-status trailer and run the chain bookkeeping
(activeChains-- / afterAll) so the stream terminates cleanly.

Adds an HTTP/3 end-to-end templating test (Http3GrpcBidiTemplatingTest)
mirroring the HTTP/2 GrpcBidiInterleavingMultiplexTest assertion.

test(core): de-flake connection-pool server-closed-channel reuse test

shouldNotReuseChannelTheServerClosedAfterResponding raced under parallel
Surefire: the server closing a pooled keep-alive socket and the client
observing the FIN are independent events. When the second request was
dispatched on the pooled channel before the client read the FIN, the write
to the half-closed socket failed with either SocketConnectionException
(handler removed before response) or a Connection reset SocketException -
the documented production contract (no silent auto-retry of a possibly
non-idempotent request). The test treated that clean failure as an error.

Make the test deterministic without weakening intent:
- the upstream now closes after responding for the FIRST connection only,
  so the replacement connection is stably reusable and the accepted count
  cannot drift above 2 under retries;
- the second request retries, tolerating only the server-closed-reuse race
  failures, until it succeeds on a fresh connection.

It still proves a server-closed channel is never silently reused (the
accepted-connection count must reach exactly 2). Test-only change; no
production code touched.

feat(core): request-driven template response delay

Add an opt-in delay form whose duration in milliseconds is computed by
rendering a Velocity or Mustache template against the incoming request, so
responses can be slowed in proportion to the request (e.g. larger payloads
respond more slowly). Delay gains optional template + templateType
(Delay.template(...)); a new DelayTemplateResolver renders the template via
the existing text template engines, parses the output as a whole number of
milliseconds, and falls back safely to the static value/timeUnit on a blank,
non-numeric, negative, or failed render. JavaScript is not supported (same
constraint as file-body templating) and falls back.

Resolution happens in HttpActionHandler where the request is in scope, for
every response/forward/error action delay, so static and statistical
(distribution) delays are unchanged byte-for-byte. Round-trips through
model -> DTO -> serializer; the JSON schema and embedded OpenAPI model allow
the new template/templateType properties (VELOCITY/MUSTACHE only).

feat(core): conditional (if-then-else) request matcher

Add an opt-in conditional request matcher form. Today request matching is
AND-only across the matcher fields (method/path/headers/body must all match).
The new ConditionalRequestDefinition lets an expectation express "IF condition
A matches THEN also require B ELSE require C":

  if (if.matches(request)) require then.matches(request)
  else                     require else.matches(request)

When the else branch is absent the expectation matches whenever the if guard is
false. Each branch reuses the existing request-matching machinery via
MatcherBuilder, so any request definition - including a nested conditional - may
be used as the if/then/else branch. The construct is additive and opt-in;
existing AND-only expectations are unchanged.

The matcher publishes its compiled branch matchers through a single volatile
holder (mirroring HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher) so concurrent control-plane
rebuilds never expose a torn view to data-plane reads.

Round-trips through DTO, serializer, deserializer (dispatched on the presence of
an "if" key) and the control-plane JSON schema. Branch types are limited to
httpRequest, openAPIDefinition and a nested conditional so the DTO mapping and
the conditionalRequestDefinition JSON schema stay in lock step. The consumer
OpenAPI spec gains a matching ConditionalRequestDefinition schema.

Existing schema-validation tests that assert anyOf error counts are updated for
the new requestDefinition member.

feat(core): JSON Patch (RFC 6902) and JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) on forwarded response bodies

An httpOverrideForwardedRequest / forward-template response modifier may now
carry an inline jsonPatch (RFC 6902 array of add/remove/replace/move/copy/test
operations) and/or jsonMergePatch (RFC 7386 object) that is applied to a
forwarded/proxied upstream response body when that body is valid JSON. This
lets a single field of a real upstream response be changed instead of replacing
the whole body.

The patches are applied in HttpResponseModifier.applyTo, the single application
site reached by both the override-forwarded-request and forward-template
handlers via HttpResponse.update, so no handler changes are needed. jsonPatch is
applied before jsonMergePatch. A non-JSON body, a malformed patch, or a failed
RFC 6902 test operation leaves the body unchanged so a forward never errors; an
absent patch is byte-for-byte unchanged. The body charset from the existing
Content-Type is preserved on the rewritten JSON body.

The patch engine reuses com.github.java-json-tools:json-patch, already on the
compile classpath transitively via json-schema-validator and now declared
directly and pinned so no new dependency is introduced.

The new fields round-trip through HttpResponseModifierDTO as inline JSON and are
added to the httpOverrideForwardedRequest / httpTemplate control-plane schemas
and the consumer OpenAPI spec.

feat(pact): provider-state preconditions on import, verify, and export

scenario-state mechanism so an imported interaction is gated on its precondition
being established before it is served or verified.

feat(import): GraphQL schema and AsyncAPI-to-HTTP expectation import endpoints

Add two control-plane spec-import endpoints alongside the existing OpenAPI,
WSDL and gRPC-descriptor imports.

PUT /mockserver/graphql accepts a GraphQL SDL document or an introspection
JSON result and creates one expectation per root operation type
(query/mutation/subscription). Each matches any operation of that kind via
AST_SUBSET matching and carries the schema on its GraphQLBody so a
schema-valid {"data": {...}} response is synthesized per request, reusing the
existing GraphQLResponseSynthesizer. An optional ?path= query parameter
overrides the default /graphql request path. The new GraphQLExpectationGenerator
lives in mockserver-core (graphql-java is already a dependency).

PUT /mockserver/asyncapi/http accepts an AsyncAPI 2.x/3.x spec (JSON/YAML, or a
{spec, channelPathPrefix} wrapper) and creates one GET expectation per channel
returning that channel's schema-aware example payload over plain HTTP, so
example messages can be served without a live Kafka/MQTT/AMQP broker. The new
AsyncApiHttpExpectationGenerator reuses the existing AsyncApiParser and
MessageExampleGenerator; it lives in mockserver-async and is reached from
HttpState through a new generateHttpExpectations method on the
AsyncApiControlPlane SPI, returning the expectations as a serialized JSON array
so core needs no compile-time dependency on the parser. The existing
PUT /mockserver/asyncapi broker-publishing import is unchanged.

Raw .proto import is deferred: it requires a protoc compile step and a
toolchain, which is out of scope here; compiled gRPC descriptors continue to
import via PUT /mockserver/grpc/descriptors.

Malformed specs return 400; the AsyncAPI HTTP import returns 501 when the
mockserver-async module is absent. Error response bodies are built with Jackson
so arbitrary exception text cannot corrupt the JSON.

fix(core): make forwarded response-time header deterministic under test clock pin

The x-mockserver-response-time-ms header on logged forwarded/proxied
responses was computed from raw System.nanoTime() deltas, so
HttpActionHandlerTest assertions that hardcode the header as "0" flaked
intermittently with "1".

Add a mockable monotonic TimeService.nanoTime() that mirrors the existing
mockable-clock pin pattern: when a test pins time (per-thread FixedTime or
global GlobalFixedTime) both the start and end reads return the same
constant, so the elapsed delta is deterministically 0. In production (no
pin) it returns real System.nanoTime() unchanged - monotonic semantics and
overhead are unchanged (one volatile fast-path read). Unlike now(), it does
not consult the controllable freeze() clock, since elapsed-time measurement
must stay monotonic.

Route all 12 response-time nanoTime sites in HttpActionHandler
(forwardStartNanos / responseTimeMs / streamResponseTimeMs) through it. The
test keeps its clean exact "0" assertions - no normalisation band-aid.

feat(core): synthesize schema-valid gRPC responses from loaded descriptors

A matched gRPC expectation with a successful (grpc-status 0) response and no

The new GrpcExampleSynthesizer builds a real DynamicMessage (guaranteeing a valid
instance that round-trips through GrpcJsonMessageConverter) and walks the message's
fields emitting deterministic, type-correct placeholders: scalars, enums (first
declared value), nested messages, repeated fields (single element), map entries,
oneof (first field only), and the protobuf well-known types. Recursion is bounded
so self-referential schemas terminate safely.

Wired into GrpcToHttpResponseHandler at the existing no-body branch; explicit
response bodies are always used as-is and never overwritten.

fix(ui): make body-contains filter use substring matching

The "Body contains" request filter emitted a bare string as the body
matcher, which the server's BodyDTODeserializer turns into a StringBody

label, placeholder and intent. A request whose body merely contained the
term did not match.

Emit an explicit STRING matcher DTO ({ type, string, subString: true })
from the filter so the server builds a contains-matching StringBody.
Saved presets still store the plain body string, so older presets load
unchanged.

Add a behavioural test (buildBodyMatcher + matchesStringBody) proving a
containing body matches while a non-matching body does not, and that the

fix(ui): named-example picker preserves all operations on import

The server treats operationsAndResponses as an operation filter -
OpenAPIConverter only generates an expectation for an operation whose
operationId is a key of that map. Sending only the picked operation's
entry therefore silently dropped every other operation in the spec.

When any example is pinned, emit a default-preserving empty-string entry
for every operationId discovered in the inline spec, overriding only the
picked ones with { statusCode, exampleName }. An empty-string value is
read by the converter as a blank response key, selecting the first
defined response with no named example - identical to the operation's
server default. When no example is pinned the map is omitted entirely,
unchanged.

fix(ui): synthesize operationIds for id-less operations in example picker

The Import OpenAPI named-example picker collected only operations that
declare an explicit operationId. The server, however, synthesizes an id of
the form "<UPPERCASE_METHOD> <path>" for any operation without one
(OpenAPIParser.synthesizeOperationIds) and then filters generation by that
synthesized key (OpenAPIConverter). So a spec mixing an example-bearing,
id-bearing operation (which the user pins) with an id-less operation still
silently dropped the id-less operation, because its synthesized key was
absent from operationsAndResponses.

discoverAllOperationIds() now replicates the server's synthesis byte-for-
byte for id-less (or blank-id) operations, emitting "<METHOD> <path>" so
every id the server will use is present in the map with a default-
preserving "" value. A behavioural test mixes a pinned id-bearing
operation with an id-less one and asserts the id-less operation still
imports under its synthesized key.

The spec is sent as a JSON string (the server reads it with

test(core): tolerate closest-match diff suffix in sequence-verify assertion

The field-level closest-match diff added for sequence verification failures
appends a 'closest match diff:' block after the stable failure message, which
broke ControlPlaneIntegrationTest#shouldVerifySequenceNotFoundWithMaximumNumberOfRequestToReturnInFailure's
exact equalTo assertion. Relax it to startsWith so it asserts the full stable
prefix while tolerating the appended diagnostic block.

fix(core): de-duplicate CA in TLS certificate chain for Java 17 mTLS

certificateChain() appended the configured CA unconditionally, so a supplied
x509CertificatePath PEM that already ended with the CA (a full leaf+CA chain)
produced [leaf, CA, CA]. Java 17's PKCS12 keystore rejects the duplicate with
KeyStoreException: Certificate chain is not valid, so the server failed to start
its TLS context (Java 21 tolerated it, masking the bug). Only append the CA when
it is not already present; add a regression test covering the leaf+CA PEM path.

test(container): stop silently dropping failed container tests from the tally

logTestResult recorded a failure to FAIL_LOG only AFTER dumping container logs,
and container-logs ran a bare, unscoped 'docker-compose logs' that returns
non-zero when the project has no/crashed containers. Under the test scripts'
set -euo pipefail that non-zero aborted logTestResult before the FAIL_LOG write,
so a real failure (e.g. docker_compose_with_mtls) printed 'Failed:' yet never
reached the blocking tally and the build went green. Record the failure before
the diagnostic dump and make container-logs project-scoped and non-fatal.

build(docker): harden Maven Central downloads and support local CA proxy

Docker image builds had no download retry tolerance and no corporate-CA trust
outside the graaljs variant, so a transient DNS/connection blip on repo1.maven.org
failed the whole build (e.g. graaljs 'Resolving repo1.maven.org... failed:
Try again') and builds behind a TLS-inspecting proxy could not run locally.

- Add GNU-wget retry config (tries/timeout/waitretry/retry_on_host_error/
  retry_connrefused via /etc/wgetrc) after each apk add in all six download
  Dockerfiles. Safe no-op on BusyBox wget.
- Extend the ca-bundle.pem corporate-CA trust mechanism (previously graaljs-only)
  to the base, root, snapshot, root-snapshot and clustered Dockerfiles, guarded by
  [ -s ] so CI and published images are byte-identical when no bundle is supplied.
- Add docker/ensure-ca-bundle.sh helper; populate ca-bundle.pem from
  MOCKSERVER_LOCAL_CA_BUNDLE for local builds; wire it into the container-test
  harness and the release/snapshot/helm build scripts; gitignore the bundles;
  document the workflow in docs/infrastructure/docker.md.

feat: connection-lifecycle fault injection + preemption simulation

Extends per-host TCP chaos with response-path lifecycle faults (mid-response RST,
slow-close, HTTP/2 GOAWAY) via PUT /mockserver/tcpChaos, and adds PUT/GET/DELETE
/mockserver/preemption to simulate a Kubernetes rolling-update / spot-reclaim drain:
cordon new exchanges (GOAWAY on HTTP/2, 503 + Connection: close on HTTP/1.1), report
the live in-flight count, auto-uncordon after a TTL, without stopping the JVM.
Destructive RSTs feed the chaos auto-halt breaker (which now also clears the TCP chaos
registry); graceful drain signals do not. Off by default; zero cost when inactive.

feat(core): SLO resilience verdicts (verifySLO endpoint + windowed SLI tracker)

Adds an opt-in windowed SLI sample store and a PUT /mockserver/verifySLO control-plane
endpoint that evaluates latency-percentile and error-rate objectives over forwarded
traffic and returns a structured pass/fail SloVerdict (200 PASS / 406 FAIL / 400).
Off by default (sloTrackingEnabled); record path is a no-op when disabled. Pairs with
chaos experiments to assert a system stays within its objectives under fault.
feat(core): upstream forward retry policy and circuit breaker with metric
feat(cli): mockserver import subcommand and client import method

feat(core): opt-in structured-output enforcement for LLM completions

Add an opt-in `enforceOutputSchema` flag on `Completion`. When enabled
alongside a declared `outputSchema`, a mocked LLM completion whose
configured body does not conform to the schema now fails loudly with a
provider-correct error (HTTP 502 via LlmErrorBodies, plus the
x-mockserver-structured-output-invalid diagnostic header) instead of
returning the non-conforming body. This models a real provider's strict
response_format:json_schema mode, which guarantees schema-valid output.

The check runs before dispatch on both the streaming and non-streaming
paths (after chaos, which takes priority as a transport-level failure
independent of the body), so a strict streaming completion with a
non-conforming body never begins streaming.

Enforcement is opt-in and back-compatible: the default (unset/false)
keeps the existing fail-soft validate-and-log behaviour (diagnostic
header only); the flag has no effect without an outputSchema; and a
blank, absent-text, or malformed schema remains a no-op that can never
produce an enforcement error. Exposed via the expectation-JSON field,
the Completion builder, and the mock_llm_completion MCP parameter.

feat(core): API-driven load generation via Load Scenarios (/loadScenario)

Adds an opt-in control plane (PUT/GET/DELETE /mockserver/loadScenario) that drives
outbound traffic at a target. A LoadScenario is an ordered list of request steps with
per-step Delay think-time and a CONSTANT/LINEAR ramp profile; request fields are
template-rendered per iteration via a new 'iteration' context object. Runs in-process on
a non-blocking scheduler firing through the existing forward HTTP client (core stays
decoupled via an injected sender), feeding the metrics histograms and SLO sample store so
a run can be asserted with verifySLO. Off by default and bounded by hard caps on virtual
users, in-flight requests, request rate, duration, and steps.
feat(core): WASM richer ABI (method/path/headers), authoring SDK, and wasm/test endpoint
feat(client): timeout-aware eventual and negative-within-timeout verification

feat(core): generate schema-valid responses from an inline JSON schema

Add a `generateFromSchema` response field that takes a plain inline JSON
Schema (not a full OpenAPI document) and, at response time, synthesizes a
schema-valid JSON body from it by reusing the existing OpenAPI example
generation engine (ExampleBuilder/SampleDataGenerator). The inline schema
is wrapped in a minimal OpenAPI document and parsed with the same
OpenAPIParser, so types, required, enum, default, arrays, nested objects,
$ref and allOf are all honoured without reimplementing any generation logic.

Additive and back-compatible: it only fires when the response has no
explicit body (an explicit body always wins), and an unparseable schema is
logged at WARN and leaves the body unset rather than failing the request.
The field round-trips through the model/DTO serializers, the Java-code
serializer and the expectation JSON schema.

feat(core): general-purpose rate limiting (rateLimit expectation clause)

A protocol-agnostic rateLimit clause on an expectation returns a deterministic 429
with Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* headers once a matched expectation exceeds its rate,
for testing client backoff/retry without a chaos profile. Supports fixed_window and
token_bucket algorithms and a named shared counter. Off by default; node-local counter
store bounded by rateLimitMaxNamedQuotas.

feat(core): retry/backoff recovery primitive (recoverAfter: fail N times then succeed)

A new opt-in recoverAfter clause on httpResponse returns a failure response
(configurable, default 503) for the first failTimes matches then the configured
success response, for deterministic client retry/backoff testing. Optional
idempotencyHeader scopes the attempt counter per request-header value; the counter
registry is bounded (LRU). Independent of Times; a response without the clause is
unchanged.

feat(core): drift alerting webhook (push notification on breaking drift)

When driftAlertWebhookEnabled=true and a webhook URL is set, MockServer fires a
fire-and-forget HTTP POST to that URL when a drift of configurable severity is detected,
so SREs don't have to poll GET /mockserver/drift. Severity is the LLM semantic
classification when present, else a structural fallback by drift type; default threshold
BREAKING. Per-signature cooldown de-dup (bounded). Off by default; fail-soft (a webhook
failure never affects drift analysis or the served response).
feat(core): opt-in OpenAPI request validation during mock matching

feat(core): control-plane audit logging (GET /mockserver/audit)

An opt-in, append-only, bounded in-memory audit log of control-plane mutations
(method, path, operation, source address, best-effort principal, outcome), captured at
the single post-auth choke point so every control-plane op is recorded once. Stores no
headers or bodies and strips query strings (safety by omission); best-effort UNVERIFIED
principal from JWT sub / mTLS CN. Retrieve via auth-gated GET /mockserver/audit; cleared
on reset. Off by default.

feat(core): expose regex capture groups to response templates

When an expectation matches a request path with a regular expression
containing capture groups, the captured values are now available to
Mustache, Velocity and JavaScript response/forward templates via two new
request-model fields:

  request.pathGroups       numbered groups, 1-based aligned with
                           java.util.regex (index 0 = whole match)
  request.namedPathGroups  Java named groups (?<name>...), keyed by name

The groups are extracted post-match by HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher using
the same Pattern flags the path matcher uses (case-insensitive by default,
DOTALL only under matchExactCase) so extraction succeeds for exactly the
requests that matched. The fields are cleared before each match so a
skipped candidate's groups never leak onto a request served by a different
expectation. Extraction is gated on the matcher path containing '(' so the
literal/path-parameter case pays nothing, and is best-effort (never throws,
never affects which expectation matches).

Additive and back-compatible: existing template fields are unchanged, the
new fields are transient and excluded from request identity/JSON/clone, and
both are empty when the matched path had no capture groups.

perf(forward): enable upstream connection pool by default

Baseline k6 A/B showed the opt-in upstream HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pool, shipped
off by default, left forward/proxy workloads opening a fresh TCP (and TLS)
connection per request — exhausting ephemeral ports under sustained load
(21% request failures at 750 rps, 68% at 1500 rps, BindException: Can't
assign requested address). Defaulting forwardConnectionPoolEnabled=true takes
the identical runs to 0% errors with no latency regression, and matches
standard HTTP client keep-alive behaviour.

The pool only reuses plain HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections keyed by host,
port and scheme, re-checks liveness on acquire, and falls back to a fresh
connection for HTTP/2, HTTP/3, binary, streaming, proxy-tunnelled, and
Connection: close responses. Set forwardConnectionPoolEnabled=false to restore
the historical fresh-connection-per-request behaviour.

Verified: 415 forward/proxy tests across mockserver-core and mockserver-netty
pass; the connection-pool opt-out test now sets the flag explicitly rather than
relying on the (now flipped) default.

perf(templates): cache parsed Velocity templates instead of re-parsing per render

The Velocity engine re-parsed the template string on every render, which
dominated the per-iteration cost of load scenarios (and added avoidable cost to
all response/forward templating). It now caches the parsed template via
Velocity's native string-resource cache (StringResourceLoader + getTemplate +
Template.merge) and reuses it across renders. Rendering goes through Velocity's
own merge path, so #stop, macros, scope control and error handling are
unchanged and output is byte-for-byte identical. The parsed-template cache is a
bounded access-ordered LRU (cap 1000) and parse failures fall back to the
original path so invalid-template error messages are preserved.

Measured with JMH (-prof gc): 55-79% faster and 46-74% less allocation per
render from simple to complex templates. Adds a ForwardPathBenchmark to the
benchmark module as the regression guard, plus regression tests for #stop and
macro rendering on both cold and warm cache, cache-overflow eviction, and
concurrent rendering of a shared cached template with per-iteration state.

Known follow-up: the per-engine string-resource repository registration is not
torn down (bounded constant growth, ~2 engines per server lifetime).

test(perf): add k6 forward-path regression guard for the connection-pool default

The existing load.js exercises the control plane; this adds a forward-path
scenario that guards the forwardConnectionPoolEnabled default. It drives
sustained forward load (SUT forwards to a separate loopback upstream) up to the
rate at which the old per-request-connection default failed, and gates on the
forward error rate staying ~0. If pooling ever regresses to a fresh connection
per request, the host exhausts ephemeral ports (BindException) and the gate
trips.

Validated both directions: 0% errors at the new default (pool on); 80% errors
with -Dmockserver.forwardConnectionPoolEnabled=false at peak, confirming the
guard actually catches the regression.

perf(templates): share stateless Velocity functions/helpers across renders

Building a Velocity render context previously copied the ~26 built-in template
functions and helpers into a fresh context on every render. Those bindings are
stateless, so they are now hoisted into a single immutable context layer built
once per engine and chained behind the per-render context. Only genuinely
per-request state - the request, per-iteration values, and request-scoped tools
($json/$xml/$import, which hold per-request parse state) - is built fresh per
render, so output and thread-safety are unchanged (the shared layer is read-only
during merge; an unmodifiable map fail-fasts on any accidental write).

Measured with JMH (-prof gc): a further ~1 KB/op less allocation and 30-67%
faster per render on top of the parse-once template caching. Adds a concurrency
regression test (30 threads) asserting each render sees only its own request
state and a distinct $uuid.

fix(forward): revert connection-pool default to off; never pool a malformed-response channel

Defaulting the upstream connection pool on (06fac9328) regressed object-callback
and websocket-callback forwarding: MockServer's own error() action (raw bytes /
drop-connection) poisons the client HTTP codec on a channel that still reports
active with no Connection: close, so the channel was returned to the pool and a
later reuse received undecoded leftover bytes -> the response future never
completed (502 / 20s timeout). Reproduced in ExtendedNettyMockingIntegrationTest
and WebsocketCallbackRegistryIntegrationTest with pooling on; green with it off.

Revert forwardConnectionPoolEnabled to false (opt-in, the previously-shipped
default) so the regression is resolved, and harden the pool-return path so that
even when pooling is enabled a reply that did not decode as a cleanly framed
HTTP response (status outside 100-599, e.g. the 999 sentinel for an invalid
message) is never returned to the pool. Pooling remains available opt-in for
plain-HTTP forward workloads where it gives the port-exhaustion win.

Adds shouldNotReuseChannelAfterMalformedNonHttpResponse (proven to hang without
the gate). Docs/changelog reworded to off-by-default/opt-in.

fix(core): dispatch local callbacks off the server worker event loop

Local object and class callbacks (response and forward) ran inline on the
Netty server worker event-loop thread. If the callback made a blocking loopback
call back to the same server (e.g. reusing the same client to register another
expectation), it blocked that worker thread waiting for a reply that itself had
to be read on a worker thread - a self-deadlock, broken only by the socket
timeout. It was previously masked because each request tended to land on a
different worker; it becomes deterministic once upstream connections are pooled
(all callbacks pin to one reused connection's worker).

Dispatch the local callback body onto a dedicated unbounded executor
(SynchronousQueue-backed cached pool, daemon 'MockServer-LocalCallback' threads,
60s idle reaping) so the worker loop is freed to read the loopback reply. A
bounded pool is deliberately NOT used: a recursively-triggered inner callback
must always get a fresh thread, otherwise it would deadlock behind blocked outer
threads. Synchronous (WAR/servlet) mode still runs inline; the websocket/remote
dispatch path is unchanged (already async); response routing, in-flight
accounting and per-callback delay are preserved. This makes callbacks robust
against blocking loopbacks independent of connection pooling.

Measured off-loop hop cost ~5.9us per local callback (immaterial vs a forward).

perf(forward): enable upstream connection pool by default (safe-by-default)

Re-enable forwardConnectionPoolEnabled by default. Pooling reuses upstream
HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections, eliminating the ephemeral-port exhaustion that
makes proxy/forward-heavy load fail: k6 A/B on this build shows 0% errors at 750
and 1500 rps with pooling on, versus 21% / 59% errors (116k BindExceptions) with
it off. Set forwardConnectionPoolEnabled=false to restore per-request
connections.

Three mechanisms make on-by-default safe:
- a dedicated forward/proxy event-loop group, disjoint from the server worker
  group (sized by clientNioEventLoopThreadCount), so a reused channel is never
  pinned to a server worker thread;
- off-event-loop local callback dispatch (separate commit) so a blocking
  loopback inside a callback cannot deadlock the worker that must read its reply;
- a fail-closed channel-quiescence gate: a connection is returned to the pool
  only if the response was cleanly framed AND the codec has no leftover bytes,
  so error()/raw/desynced replies are never reused.

Verified: the previously-deterministic loopback-callback deadlock is gone
(passes ~2s, was a 20-71s timeout), full failsafe + proxy suites green with
pooling on across repeated runs, pooled reuse and the off-by-default opt-out both
preserved, and no forward throughput/latency regression (p50 0.32ms @1500 rps).

perf(core): drop duplicate inbound body copy and per-matcher MatchDifference alloc

Two allocation reductions on the request hot path, each proven by JMH -prof gc
with zero behaviour change (review-final PASS):

- The inbound mapper materialised the request body into a byte[] and then called
  byteBufToBody, which allocated and re-read a SECOND identical body-size byte[].
  Feed the already-materialised bytes straight to bytesToBody. Removes exactly one
  body-size byte[] per request-with-body (-1.2KB at 1KB body, -262KB at 256KB),
  and is faster.
- firstMatchingExpectation allocated a fresh MatchDifference per candidate even
  when detailedMatchFailures is off (the default), i.e. one throwaway shell per
  expectation per non-matching request. Reuse a single instance across the scan
  when detail is off (fresh per-matcher only when on, so diagnostics are
  unchanged). A 1000-expectation EXACT no-match scan drops from ~56KB/op to ~65B/op.

Adds InboundDecodeBenchmark; the existing MatchingBenchmark covers the second.

fix(core): make log-timestamp formatting and regex-memo publication thread-safe

Two concurrency bugs on the request/log hot path (review-final PASS, each with a
concurrency regression test):

- LogEntry shared one mutable static SimpleDateFormat formatted concurrently from
  the log handler and retrieve/export threads. SimpleDateFormat is not
  thread-safe, so under load timestamps were corrupted (and occasionally threw
  ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException). Replaced with an immutable DateTimeFormatter
  producing byte-identical output (same pattern, local timezone). The new
  LogEntryTimestampConcurrencyTest reproduces ~175k cross-contaminated reads
  against the old code.
- NottableString memoised its compiled Patterns in non-volatile fields (unsafe
  publication + first-burst recompile races). Made the two fields volatile; a
  duplicate Pattern.compile under a race is harmless.

Also adds MetricsIncrementBenchmark: it documents (and guards) a DROPPED change
- removing the per-increment synchronized in Metrics looked like a win but JMH
  showed it regresses the shared-counter hot path 6-13x (the lock serialises the
  AtomicLong CAS), so Metrics is intentionally left unchanged.

ci(buildkite): never cancel running master builds (scope cancel to !master)

Every pipeline had cancel_intermediate_builds enabled, but most child pipelines
(container-tests, performance-test, infra, the per-client and release pipelines)
had an EMPTY branch filter, so cancellation applied to all branches including
master. A fresh master commit then cancelled the previous still-running build
before it could report — which (a) left that commit untested and (b) surfaced as
a misleading FAILURE on the parent pipeline whose trigger step was waiting on the
cancelled child. This hit the long-running container-tests (~20m) and
performance-test pipelines hardest.

Set cancel_intermediate_builds_branch_filter = "!master" uniformly via the
for_each so master builds always run to completion and report true pass/fail,
while feature/PR branches still cancel superseded runs to save agent VMs. Queued
(not-yet-started) builds are still skipped on all branches (they report as
'skipped', not red). Applied via terraform; verified all 20 pipelines now carry
the !master filter.

perf(core): cache the JavaScript template engine and render concurrently

The GraalVM JS template engine was the only template engine not caching: every
matched request using a JS template built and tore down a fresh GraalVM Context,
re-parsed and re-evaluated the script, and re-injected ~26 bindings - and all JS
renders across the server serialized on one synchronized lock. Now a single
shared Engine + a bounded parsed-Source LRU (keyed by script+variant, mirroring
the Mustache cache) are reused, and each request thread renders on its own
ThreadLocal Context (a GraalVM Context is single-threaded; the Engine is the
thread-safe sharing point), so the global lock is removed.

Output is byte-for-byte identical (every binding rewritten per render; the
iteration binding is removed when absent so it can't leak between renders;
per-render-fresh uuid/now/rand preserved). Graceful degradation when GraalVM is
absent is unchanged. JMH: -93% allocation and ~14x faster single-threaded, ~10.5x
higher throughput at 8 threads. Adds JavaScriptTemplateBenchmark + a concurrency
isolation test and an iteration-binding-leak test.

perf(core): cache compiled OpenAPI schema validators across requests

When validating requests/responses against an OpenAPI spec, each request
re-serialized the operation schema and compiled a fresh networknt Schema +
SchemaRegistry (response path: once per declared response header). The spec parse
was already cached but the per-operation validator was not. Cache the compiled
validator in a bounded content-keyed LRUCache (SHA-256 of the schema JSON, 250 /
30min, participating in clearAllCaches) and reuse it; each call still gets a
thread-confined wrapper carrying its own logger, so only the immutable compiled
Schema (networknt-documented thread-safe for validation) is shared. Validation
verdicts and error messages are byte-identical (proven against a freshly-built
validator); a changed schema yields a different key so there is no stale-validator
hazard. JMH: ~50-66% less time and allocation on the validation path; the win
grows with schema size. Adds a race-free LRUCache.getOrCompute, cache tests
(registered in both Surefire phases) and OpenApiValidationBenchmark.

fix(core): share one process-wide GraalVM Engine to stop a native-resource leak (CI fork timeout)

The recent JavaScript-template-engine caching change built a fresh native
GraalVM Engine per JavaScriptTemplateEngine instance plus a per-instance
ThreadLocal<Context>, neither ever closed. Because the engine is constructed
per call (ResponseTemplateTester), per action-handler, and directly in tests,
native Engines accumulated in the single reused Surefire fork — each pinning
Truffle/compiler threads and native memory — exhausting it and killing the
mockserver-core test fork on the 1800s timeout (6300+ tests run, 0 failures).

Fix: the Engine is now a single lazily-initialised process-wide instance
(initialization-on-demand holder), shared across all template engines — the
standard GraalVM scaling pattern — so native Engines are O(1) per JVM instead
of O(instances). Added close() to PolyglotRunner + JavaScriptTemplateEngine
(disposes this thread's Context and removes the ThreadLocal); ResponseTemplateTester
closes its per-call engine. Contexts stay per-instance because the
allowHostClassLookup class filter is per-Configuration — sharing them would
weaken the Java.type(...) security boundary; a new test confirms 50 engines
share one Engine, and the class-lookup security tests still pass. Rendering
output is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Reverts e5a555864 ("cache the JavaScript template engine and render
concurrently") and its follow-up 82045ea4b ("share one process-wide GraalVM
Engine"). The JavaScript engine source (JavaScriptTemplateEngine, PolyglotRunner,

fix(load): keep load-generation traffic out of the request event log

A running load scenario recorded its generated requests in the bounded
request event log (maxLogEntries), so a sustained run filled the log and
evicted real and LLM traffic -- emptying the Traffic, Trace and LLM Optimise
views (and the dashboard log) while the load ran.

LoadScenarioOrchestrator now marks each generated request with an
x-mockserver-load-generated header (the run id); MockServerEventLog.add()
skips any entry whose request carries it, so load traffic never enters the
ring buffer. Throughput/latency metrics and SLO samples are recorded
client-side in recordResult(), independently of the event log, so they are
unaffected.

Verified: an 18s run that sent ~9,500 load requests left recorded requests
at 55 and the optimisation report at 27 calls (previously a 20s run wrote
~10,500 entries and evicted everything). New
MockServerEventLogLoadGeneratedSuppressionTest covers suppression,
interleaving and ordering.

fix(load): driver-only load-log suppression via in-process marker, gated by config

The load-log suppression added in 574bb8662 stamped each generated request with
the WIRE header x-mockserver-load-generated and had MockServerEventLog.add() skip
it. That header travelled on the wire to the upstream target, so the target
MockServer also dropped the load traffic from ITS event log — breaking
LoadScenarioIntegrationTest (the target logged nothing) and, in real use,
silently disabling request logging on any MockServer being load-tested.

Replace the wire header with a config-gated, in-process-only marker:

- New property loadGenerationSuppressEventLog (Boolean, default TRUE) in
  ConfigurationProperties / Configuration / ConfigurationDTO (mirrored in all five
  DTO places, so the ConfigurationDTOTest round-trip guard passes). Default keeps
  the server's own load traffic out of its request event log; set false to log it.
- HttpRequest gains an @JsonIgnore transient `loadGenerated` marker, excluded from
  equals/hashCode/clone/JSON — it is not part of request identity and is never
  serialized to the wire, so it cannot reach an upstream target.
- LoadScenarioOrchestrator sets the marker on the rendered request (only when the
  property is true) instead of adding the header; MockServerEventLog.add()
  suppresses on the marker. The LOAD_GENERATED_HEADER constant is removed.

Suppression is now strictly driver-side: the upstream target logs load traffic
normally. LoadScenarioIntegrationTest asserts both — the target receives the
traffic (no leak) and the driver does not log it (suppression works through the
real Netty forward path). Verified: ConfigurationDTOTest 24/0, suppression test
3/0, MockServerEventLogTest 13/0, LoadScenarioIntegrationTest 5/5 consecutive.

perf(ui): code-split Monaco editor out of the main dashboard bundle

and point the three consumers at the wrappers. Monaco now splits into its

chunk. Suspense shows an editor-sized spinner so there is no layout jump;
chunk-load failures are handled by the existing app-level ErrorBoundary.

fix(release): sync mockserver-client-node lockfile to 7.2.0

The 7.2.0 version-bump (commits 64620f213, 0642067b2) updated
mockserver-client-node/package.json to 7.2.0 and its mockserver-node
devDependency to 7.2.0, but update-version-references.sh excludes
package-lock.json from the bump and never regenerates it — so the lock
stayed pinned at 7.1.0. That makes `npm ci` hard-fail with EUSAGE
("lock file's mockserver-node@7.1.0 does not satisfy mockserver-node@7.2.0")
across the mockserver-node CI pipeline and the main pipeline's node trigger.

The release's npm publish step regenerates and commits this lock after
publishing mockserver-node, but build #58's npm job died before reaching
mockserver-client-node, leaving master with an inconsistent lock.

(npm install --package-lock-only). Verified `npm ci` passes; diff is the

fix(release): make changelog rollover idempotent across re-runs

update-version-references.sh rolls the changelog by replacing the
always-present "## [Unreleased]" header with a fresh Unreleased section
plus a dated "## [RELEASE_VERSION]" section. The step runs on full,
maven-only AND post-maven, so every retried full run or post-maven
re-run matched "## [Unreleased]" again and inserted ANOTHER
"## [RELEASE_VERSION]" block — duplicating the section once per run.

This is what produced the duplicate 7.1.0 entries (its many
"update version references to 7.1.0" commits), cleaned up by hand in
af8d1a3e5. A 7.2.0 post-maven re-run would have duplicated 7.2.0 too.

Guard the rollover: skip it when a "## [RELEASE_VERSION]" header already
exists (version dots regex-escaped, anchored with the literal closing
bracket so there is no prefix/wildcard false-match). The other
version-reference updates are already idempotent (fixed-value writes and
OLD_VERSION->NEW replacements), so only the changelog needed the guard.
Verified by a triple-run simulation: first run inserts, subsequent runs
skip, exactly one header remains.

feat(docker): cap JVM heap at 75% of container memory limit

Add -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 to the java ENTRYPOINT in both the default
and clustered Docker images so the in-memory request/expectation rings
size off a bounded heap instead of an unbounded ~25% default, preventing
OOM-kills that were misdiagnosed as hangs. The flag only applies when the
user has not set an explicit heap, so it is a safe default; an explicit
-Xmx (via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or -Xmx) disables it and changes the cap.
Because JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS is prepended before the entrypoint args, the
entrypoint MaxRAMPercentage is applied last and wins, so only -Xmx (not a
second MaxRAMPercentage) overrides it.

Add a documented app.jvmOptions knob (with an -Xmx example) and a
commented example resources block (requests/limits) to the Helm
values.yaml, keeping the empty defaults. Update the Helm README, the
Docker running include, and the performance-tuning consumer doc to
reflect the 75% heap cap, the override semantics, and the need to set an
explicit container memory limit (so heap and the heap-derived ring sizes
are bounded).

fix: render OpenAPI format: date/date-time examples as ISO strings not epoch-millis

An inline example on a `type: string, format: date` (or date-time) schema is
deserialised by swagger-parser into a java.util.Date / OffsetDateTime. When a
property carried an explicit example, that raw temporal object was handed to the
Jackson writer, which serialised it as epoch-millis (e.g. 1611964800000) instead
of the ISO string the spec author wrote. The generated-sample path in
ExampleBuilder already stringifies dates correctly; the explicit-example path in
OpenAPIConverter.resolveSchemaExample bypassed it.

Normalise Date/OffsetDateTime examples back to their schema string form
(yyyy-MM-dd UTC for DateSchema, ISO toString for DateTimeSchema) before
serialisation, mirroring ExampleBuilder. Regression since 6.0.0.

Closes #2370

fix: inject MockServerClient into @Nested test classes without IllegalArgumentException

Issue #1979 added enclosing-class traversal so a @Nested inner test class could
inherit the MockServerClient field declared on its outer class. But injection
still set the field on the inner test instance, while the field belongs to the
outer class - throwing IllegalArgumentException for any @Nested test.

Resolve the correct target object per field: walk outward from the test instance
via the synthetic enclosing-instance reference until reaching an instance the
field declaring class accepts, then set it there; skip (no-op) if unreachable.
The simple non-nested case is unchanged. Regression since 6.0.0.

Closes #2371

fix(core): prune stale transitive deps so downstream dependencyConvergence passes (#1970)

Consumers that depend on mockserver-core (or mockserver-netty) and run
maven-enforcer's dependencyConvergence rule saw conflicts for guava, jsr305,
rhino, libphonenumber, snakeyaml, commons-*, slf4j-api, jackson-* and
jakarta.xml.bind-api. Those versions are pinned only in the parent
dependencyManagement (which is not transitive), while swagger-parser, json-patch,
velocity and protobuf-java-util drag in older transitive copies.

Prune the stale transitive edges with <exclusion>s — the resolved classpath is
unchanged because the pinned/newer versions already win nearest-wins — and
declare jackson-dataformat-yaml and jsr305 directly so a single version of each
reaches consumers. A throwaway consumer of both mockserver-core and
mockserver-netty now passes dependencyConvergence (was 15 conflicts, now 0);
the module's own enforcer still passes. (The mockserver-client-java half was
fixed in 7.1.0.)

Also remove a JVM-global read from OpenAPI example generation: ExampleBuilder
read ConfigurationProperties.generateRealisticExampleValues() deep inside
generation, so tests toggling that global could leak into reader tests under
parallel execution. The decision is now carried per-run by GenerationOptions
(nullable realisticValues; null defers to the global, so production behaviour is
unchanged), also exposed via a "realisticValues" entry in the reserved
__generationOptions__ import options map. GenerationOptionsTest and
OpenAPIConverterGenerationOptionsTest now drive realistic mode through the
options instead of mutating the global and move into the parallel Surefire phase;
ExampleBuilderRealisticValuesTest still exercises the global flag and stays
sequential. Full mockserver-core unit suite green (1,945 tests).

feat(templates): let Mustache response templates read scenario state by name

Velocity ($scenario.get('x')) and JavaScript (scenario.get('x')) could already
read scenario/captured state in a response template; the Mustache engine now
exposes the same via a section lambda - {{#scenario.get}}name{{/scenario.get}} -
where the state name is the section body (jmustache cannot pass a method argument
inline the way Velocity and JavaScript can, so this mirrors the existing
jsonPath/xPath section lambdas). This completes capture -> template value reuse
across all three template engines.

- MustacheTemplateEngine exposes "scenario" as an immutable Map whose get is a
  stateless Mustache.Lambda resolving the live ScenarioManager lazily; built once
  and shared safely across render threads
- new MustacheScenarioStateTemplateTest, registered in both Surefire phases like
  its Velocity/JavaScript siblings since it mutates the global event bus
- flip the Mustache capture integration test from negative to positive
- document the per-engine syntax on the Stateful Scenarios page with accordion
  tabs for Velocity, JavaScript and Mustache (Mustache braces wrapped in raw)

Coordinated-omission-corrected load-injection latency + HDR histogram

Measure per-request load latency from when an iteration becomes due (before
in-flight permit / RPS token acquisition) so queueing delay under an overwhelmed
target is included, not hidden. Source per-run percentiles (incl. new p999Millis)
from an exact per-run HDR histogram, available even with metrics disabled. Surface
droppedIterations (due but never dispatched due to in-flight, RPS, or RATE VU cap)
so a truncated latency distribution is visible.

In-run load-scenario thresholds with verdicts and abort-on-fail

Add LoadThreshold (LATENCY_P50/P95/P99/P999, ERROR_RATE, THROUGHPUT_RPS with a
reused SloObjective.Comparator) and scenario-level thresholds/abortOnFail/
abortGraceMillis. Evaluate live on the control tick against the run's own HDR
histogram and counters (never the global SLO store); expose verdict (PASS/FAIL),
abortedByThreshold and per-threshold observed values on the status DTO so a load
run becomes a CI gate. abortOnFail terminates the run on breach after the grace
window via the existing stop path.

Load-scenario summary report (JSON + JUnit-XML)

Add GET /mockserver/loadScenario/{name}/report returning a portable per-run
report (counts, error rate, CO-corrected p50/p95/p99/p999, dropped iterations,
threshold verdict + per-threshold observed values) for a running or finished run.
?format=junit emits JUnit-XML so a load run surfaces as per-threshold test cases
in CI, with a breached threshold rendered as a failure. Report is derived from
the existing per-run status snapshot; no new dependency.

Cross-step capture / correlation in load scenarios

A load-scenario step can declare captures (BODY_JSONPATH, HEADER, BODY_REGEX with
optional defaultValue) that extract a value from its response into a per-iteration
variable later steps reference in templated path, body and headers (e.g.
Authorization: Bearer {{iteration.captured.token}}). Enables login->token->use
flows without a scripting engine. Captured vars are scoped to one virtual-user
iteration so correlation is race-free and never leaks across users or iterations.
Reuses the existing template engines and Jayway JsonPath; no new dependency.

Generate a load scenario from an OpenAPI spec

Add PUT /mockserver/loadScenario/generateFromOpenAPI: reuse the OpenAPI parser,
operation resolver and ExampleBuilder to emit one load step per operation (example
bodies, target from servers[0] or an explicit override) with a conservative default
profile, validate it, and register it as LOADED for editing. Spec acceptance
(inline/URL/file) and SSRF posture match the existing openapi/expectation endpoint;
no new dependency.

Generate a load scenario from recorded traffic

Add PUT /mockserver/loadScenario/generateFromRecording: convert requests recorded
in proxy/recording mode into a LoadScenario - VERBATIM (one step per recorded
request in order) or TEMPLATIZED (dedupe by method + templatized path, ordered by
frequency). Optional requestFilter selects recordings and target repoints them.
Reuses the event-log retrieval and the shared route templatizer; clones requests
before retargeting so the recorded log is never mutated; validates and registers
LOADED for editing.

Named load shapes (SPIKE / STAIRS / RAMP_HOLD)

A load profile can use a declarative shape instead of explicit stages: SPIKE,
STAIRS or RAMP_HOLD, each driving VU or RATE. Shapes expand into ordinary stages
via LoadProfile.getStages() so the orchestrator is unchanged and the same caps and
runtime behaviour apply. Serialization stores the shape (raw stages + shape), never
the expansion, so round-trips expand exactly once.

Adaptive pacing (think-time) for load scenarios

Add LoadPacing (NONE / CONSTANT_PACING / CONSTANT_THROUGHPUT) targeting a fixed
per-VU iteration cycle: the closed-model loop delays the next iteration by
max(0, cycle - elapsed) so a fast iteration waits out its cycle and an overrun
starts immediately. Composes with per-step thinkTime; one-shot RATE iterations and
in-flight latency measurement are unaffected.

Data feeders for load scenarios

Add LoadFeeder: per-iteration parameterized data from inline rows or raw CSV/JSON
data, exposed to templates as iteration.data.<column> in path, body and headers.
Strategies: CIRCULAR (cycle, default), RANDOM, SEQUENTIAL (each row once then the
run completes). Mirrors the cross-step capture mechanism; rows resolved unmodifiable
and scoped per iteration; CSV via the existing helper and JSON via Jackson, no new
dependency and no external-source fetch.

Weighted step selection for load scenarios

Add LoadStep.weight and LoadScenario.stepSelection (SEQUENTIAL default / WEIGHTED).
WEIGHTED runs exactly one step per iteration, chosen by cumulative-weight random,
to model mixed workloads (e.g. 70/20/10). SEQUENTIAL behaviour is unchanged: the
iteration runs over a per-iteration step list (the full ordered list for SEQUENTIAL,
a single weighted pick for WEIGHTED) threaded through the dispatch chain, preserving
capture/pacing/feeder/RATE/closed-model behaviour.

Document new load-injection features on the consumer site

Extend mock_server/load_injection.html to cover corrected latency + p999/dropped
iterations, in-run thresholds/verdict/abort, summary report (JSON/JUnit), cross-step
capture, generate-from-OpenAPI and generate-from-recording, named load shapes,
adaptive pacing, data feeders and weighted step selection, with curl examples and
updated model/endpoint/variable tables.

Surface new load-injection features in the dashboard UI

Extend LoadScenarioPanel + loadScenario types/helpers: run view now shows p999,
droppedIterations, threshold verdict + per-threshold results and a JSON/JUnit report
download; the author form gains editors for thresholds/abortOnFail, per-step captures,
named shape vs explicit stages, pacing, data feeder, and stepSelection + per-step
weight, plus generate-from-OpenAPI and generate-from-recording actions.

Correct load-generation doc: dashboard UI is no longer deferred

The Wave-4 UI work shipped the load dashboard fields/actions; remove the UI from
the deferred list (client libraries and codegen remain the only deferred surface).

fix(core): preserve original JSON request body bytes through retrieveRecordedRequests

HttpRequest.getBodyAsOriginalRawBytes()/getBodyAsRawBytes() returned
pretty-printed JSON instead of the exact bytes received over the wire for
application/json requests. The JSON body serializers re-parsed the body to a
JSON tree and never emitted the original rawBytes, so the client deserializer
rebuilt the value pretty-printed and JsonBody fell back to json.getBytes().

Both JsonBodySerializer and JsonBodyDTOSerializer now emit a base64 rawBytes
field whenever the exact bytes cannot be reconstructed from the canonical JSON
value (rawBytes != writeValueAsBytes(parsedTree)), restoring byte-for-byte
fidelity on round-trip. Canonical bodies are unchanged, so no output bloat.

Closes #2374

fix(core): send mock response bodies verbatim with Content-Encoding header

Setting Content-Encoding: gzip/deflate on a mock response caused MockServer to
re-compress the bytes passed to withBody(...) before writing them to the wire,
double-compressing already-gzipped bodies (gzip(gzip(body))) and making it
impossible to control the exact wire bytes or advertise an encoding that does
not match the body.

Remove the unconditional re-encode from MockServerHttpResponseToFullHttpResponse
so mock response bodies are written exactly as supplied and the Content-Encoding
header is emitted literally. The forward/proxy request path is untouched: the
client pipeline's HttpContentDecompressor already strips Content-Encoding from
proxied upstream responses, so the response mapper never re-compressed genuine
proxy traffic, and request forwarding still re-compresses bodies decompressed on
ingest.

Closes #2375

test(core): align matcher mismatch-log golden string with JsonBody rawBytes serialization

The mismatch-log assertion in HttpRequestPropertiesMatcherLogTest still
expected the pre-rawBytes JsonBody form for a matcher built from

Since JsonBody/JsonBodyDTO serializers now emit a base64 rawBytes field
whenever the original bytes differ from the canonical re-serialization,
the serialized matcher body now includes type/json/rawBytes. The direct
serializer tests were already updated; this is the one transitive
consumer that was missed.

fix(core): scope JSON body rawBytes emission to recorded-request retrieval only

Commit b4d818def (#2374) made JsonBodySerializer/JsonBodyDTOSerializer
emit a base64 rawBytes field whenever a JsonBody's stored bytes differ
from the canonical re-serialization of its parsed JSON, to preserve
byte fidelity through retrieveRecordedRequests. That condition also
fires for matcher/expectation bodies built from non-canonically-spaced
JSON (e.g. json("{ \"some_field\": \"some_value\" }")), leaking base64
rawBytes into human-readable mismatch diagnostic logs, matcher
toString() output, and active-expectation listings.

Scope rawBytes emission to the recorded-request retrieval output only,
via a per-call Jackson SerializerProvider attribute "emitRawBytes":

- JsonBodySerializer/JsonBodyDTOSerializer now emit rawBytes only when
  the attribute is set (short-circuiting the expensive canonical
  re-serialization off the non-retrieval path).
- RequestDefinitionSerializer.serializeRecordedRequests writes through
  objectWriter.withAttribute("emitRawBytes", true); the generic
  serialize overloads (shared with matcher serialization and
  verification diagnostics) stay clean.
- HttpState type=requests JSON retrieval uses serializeRecordedRequests.
- HttpRequestDTOSerializer serializes the body via
  provider.defaultSerializeField so the per-call attribute propagates
  through the compact DTO path (writeObjectField drops it).

Matching is unaffected: it is in-memory against live HttpRequest
objects, the JSON matcher is built from getValue() not rawBytes, and
BodyDTODeserializer still always reads rawBytes when present, so
retrieveRecordedRequests round-trips byte-for-byte (#2374 preserved).
Diagnostic logs and matcher/expectation output return to the clean
pre-b4d818def form.
