bodyToByteBuf(body, contentType, chunkSize) and split() now handle a null body instead of throwing NullPointerException when a chunked response has no body.

fix(core): safely publish body-deserializer ObjectMapper statics

convert the unsynchronised lazily-initialised static ObjectMapper/ObjectWriter fields to private static final eager initialisation, removing a data race / unsafe-publication hazard.

fix(core): avoid double response write and stuck future on websocket callback disconnect

when a callback client has disconnected the forward-object-callback handler wrote the response twice and left a CompletableFuture that never completed (pinning a scheduler thread until timeout); it now writes once, unregisters the callback, and returns. Response/forward callback registry entries are unregistered on every disconnect branch.

fix(core): remove JS template lock bottleneck, drop Velocity ImportTool, harden template/OpenAPI caches

JavaScriptTemplateEngine no longer serialises all executions through an engine-wide lock (each call already builds its own GraalVM context); removed the Apache Velocity ImportTool (SSRF/file-read); eager static ObjectMapper and double-checked engine accessors; OpenAPIParser uses getOrCompute to avoid a parse/mutation race; JsonSchemaValidator bounds the meta-schema retry.

fix(core): round-trip proxy/scope config properties and fail fast on invalid logLevel

controlPlaneScopeMapping, proxyPass mappings and proxyRemoteHost/Port now round-trip through PUT /mockserver/config (and are enforced by the DTO drift guard); an unrecognised logLevel throws a clear error instead of an NPE at start-up; the canonical mockserver.perExpectationMetricsEnabled key is accepted with the legacy key as fallback.

fix(netty): stop blocking the event loop in connection delay and proxy handshakes; bound relay aggregators

connection-delay no longer Thread.sleeps on the event loop (deferred non-blocking first read); awaitUninterruptibly() removed from the relay/SOCKS/426 paths; CONNECT-relay aggregators bounded to maxRequestBodySize; DashboardWebSocketHandler client registry access synchronised and static writer safely published; McpSessionManager.getSession() expiry made atomic.

fix(core): add outbound read timeout and harden TLS context/cert factories

non-pooled outbound HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 client pipelines get a read timeout so a stalled upstream cannot pin a connection/future; KeyStoreFactory warns about its trust-all context; removed the JVM-wide https.protocols system-property side effect; generated certificate validity is anchored to issuance time; connect-timeout narrowing is capped.

fix(core): bound LLM caches/quota registry and harden LLM concurrency and inputs

LlmCompletionService cache is a bounded LRU (no racy wholesale clear); LlmQuotaRegistry evicts expired windows under a cap; HttpLlmResponse.getConversationMatcher uses correct double-checked locking; SemanticPromptMatcher caps and delimits user input; StreamingPhysicsExpander clamps jitter and guards tokensPerSecond.

fix: cap gRPC gzip decompression and harden async broker mock lifecycle

gRPC gzip frames are capped on decompressed size (decompression-bomb guard, with tests); async publish/subscribe lifecycle is synchronised; Kafka send failures are logged via callback; subscribers expose a health flag after a broker disconnect; gRPC proto temp files created with restrictive permissions.

fix(core): prevent lost write under concurrent CAS swap in clustered state

InMemoryKeyValueStore compareAndSet/compareAndRemove use identity guards and conditional remove/replace so a concurrent remove+put swap can no longer drop a valid write; RequestMatchers reconcile simplified and postProcess uses an O(1) id-keyed lookup with a scan fallback; InfinispanBlobStore javadoc corrected.

fix(core): enforce rate-limit cap atomically and export all chaos fault types

RateLimitRegistry enforces the named-counter cap inside compute (no same-key TOCTOU); OtelMetricsExporter mirrors the full chaos fault-type set; observeLoadRequest reuses one label-value array; the RPS token bucket re-reads the clock under its lock.

fix(core): security hardening for control-plane auth and identity mocking

control-plane JWTValidator is now stateless (Nimbus processor configured once) so concurrent requests can no longer be checked against another request's key/claims policy; RemoteJWKS and OIDC discovery fetches use bounded timeouts and a size cap; mTLS authentication rejects expired/not-yet-valid client certificates; mock OIDC client-secret comparison is constant-time; expired mTLS test fixtures regenerated.

fix(core): unregister memory-monitor listeners on stop and fix scheduler/log races

MemoryMonitoring.stop() unregisters its log/expectation listeners (was a permanent leak) and writes its CSV via try-with-resources; scheduler thread numbering uses an AtomicInteger; LogEntry override cache uses a single atomic holder; MockServerEventLog.clear iterates the deque directly on the single disruptor writer thread.

fix(client): thread-safe client init/event-bus and zero-alloc matcher-listener notification

MockServerClient.getNettyHttpClient() uses double-checked locking (was an EventLoopGroup leak under concurrent first-use) and getMockServerEventBus() uses computeIfAbsent; BreakpointWebSocketClient restores the interrupt flag; JsonStringMatcher matcher node published via volatile; MockServerMatcherNotifier uses a copy-on-write listener array for zero-allocation notification.

fix(core): exclude control-plane paths from early (respondBeforeBody) matching

EarlyMatchingHandler runs before the control-plane dispatch in HttpState.handle(), so a catch-all respondBeforeBody expectation (e.g. seeded from an initialization file) could hijack the server's own management API and answer PUT /mockserver/reset, /status, etc. firstMatchingEarlyExpectation now returns no match for requests under the reserved /mockserver control-plane prefix, so those always fall through to the control plane. This also fixes an order-dependent flake in HttpProxyViaLoadBalanceIntegrationTest where a leaked seeding global made @Before reset() return 404.

Adds HttpStateTest.shouldNotEarlyMatchControlPlaneRequestsAgainstCatchAllRespondBeforeBody; verified data-plane early matching still works via RespondBeforeBodyIntegrationTest.

fix(ui): download load-scenario report via fetch instead of window.open

CodeQL flagged js/client-side-unvalidated-url-redirection in LoadScenarioPanel:
the "download report" action called window.open on a URL whose host/port come
from the dashboard's own query string (useConnectionParams reads
window.location.search), a client-side open-redirect sink.

Replace loadScenarioReportUrl (URL string) with fetchLoadScenarioReport, which
fetches the report through the same control plane as every other call and
returns a Blob plus a sanitized filename. The panel saves it via a temporary
<a download> object-URL link (cleanup deferred past the synchronous click), so
there is no navigation a crafted dashboard link could redirect, and the report
downloads as a named .json/.xml file. Errors flow through the existing
runAction/HumanErrorAlert path. Adds focused unit tests for the new helper.

docs: mandate linear master history (rebase, never merge commits)

Reintegration must keep master a strictly linear history: rebase the
unit branch onto the master tip and fast-forward push — never create a
merge commit (no git merge, --no-ff, non-rebase pull, or intermediate
integration branch). When several worktrees are ready, rebase them
sequentially under the merge lock.

Updates the AI-SDLC spec (§8.4 + glossary), the worktree-workflow,
git-safety and operating-model rules, the /worktree-merge command, and
the AGENTS.md Git Policy. Codifies the rebase-only flow the merge
command already used and retires the older integration-branch pattern
that left merge commits in history.

test(netty): de-flake experimental HTTP/3 gRPC integration tests

The QUIC client connected single-shot with the connect deadline (5s) equal to the client idle timeout (5s) and the server idle timeout was also 5s, so a slow handshake or a stream paused at a breakpoint under cumulative single-JVM load tore the connection down with no retry (~14% flaky). Fixes (test-only; server/product code is correct): bounded connect retry (3 attempts) with full per-attempt channel + EventLoopGroup teardown; client and server http3 idle timeouts raised to 30s (decoupled from the 8s per-attempt connect deadline); the doneQueue completion signal is now assertNotNull-checked before reading frames; and UDP port binding is retried. Validated with 20/20 consecutive full-set runs (previously ~1-in-7 failing).

perf(test): opt-in tuned JVM + overridable core pinning for the perf server

Additive, opt-in env for perf-test-run.sh so a measurement re-run can produce
latency-tuned documentation figures:

- PERF_SERVER_JAVA_OPTS -> JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS on the perf server/upstream
  containers (e.g. "-XX:+UseZGC -Xmx8g") to cut GC-pause tail latency. Request
  logging is deliberately left on so the growth phase stays meaningful.
- PERF_SERVER_CPUS / PERF_UPSTREAM_CPUS / PERF_K6_CPUS override the cpuset
  pinning (e.g. hand k6 more cores to drive higher arrival rates).

Unset env -> byte-for-byte identical docker run argv (verified on Bash 3.2 and
modern bash via argv-assembly harness). Defaults unchanged (0-5 / 6 / 8-13).

feat(ui): cookieless dashboard usage analytics (PostHog, default-on, opt-out)

Add anonymous, cookieless usage analytics to the dashboard UI to drive UI
usability decisions (tab popularity, feature usage, friction points). Uses a
self-hosted PostHog instance in cookieless mode (persistence: memory,
autocapture and session-recording off) loaded as a gated lazy first-party
chunk — never Google Analytics, no cookie, no cross-site identifier.

Ships inert: with the default-empty endpoint/key the activation gate
short-circuits, so out of the box nothing is sent. It activates only when an
operator (or the project build) supplies dashboardAnalyticsEndpoint +
dashboardAnalyticsKey.

Privacy properties:
- Fail-closed activation: enabled AND endpoint AND key AND not Do-Not-Track AND
  not Global Privacy Control AND not opted-out AND online AND not webdriver AND
  not IDE-telemetry-suppressed.
- Only a closed set of coarse events (app_open, view_change, feature_used,
  error_shown) with enumerated/whitelisted params (tab id, app version, theme,
  surface, feature/error enums). No request or mock data — no URLs, hostnames,
  headers, bodies, expectation contents, ports, or file paths can be sent.
- First-run disclosure banner with one-click opt-out (localStorage), reactive to
  activation; respects DNT/GPC; all analytics calls fail silently.

Server config (mockserver-core), exposed via GET /mockserver/configuration:
- dashboardAnalyticsEnabled (boolean, default true) — master kill switch
- dashboardAnalyticsEndpoint (string, default empty) — PostHog api_host
- dashboardAnalyticsKey (string, default empty) — PostHog write-only project key

Disable globally with -Dmockserver.dashboardAnalyticsEnabled=false or
MOCKSERVER_DASHBOARD_ANALYTICS_ENABLED=false.

Includes consumer docs (configuration_properties + new dashboard_privacy page),
architecture docs (dashboard-ui.md), and unit/integration tests covering the
gating, privacy-invariant enum drops, and banner reactivity.

docs(website): rewrite Scalability & Latency with real k6 + JMH figures

Replace the historical Java-13 Apache Bench/Locust headline with current,
reproducible figures measured by the perf pipeline (pinned-box build #64,
six server cores, ZGC):

- throughput/latency knee: sub-ms median with ~0.5 ms p99 to 16k req/s,
  sub-ms median through 32k, single-instance ceiling ~36k req/s on six cores
- matcher scaling: the candidate index is up to 177x faster than a linear scan
  at 5,000 expectations and stays ~flat as expectations grow
- latency distribution at the knee, and HTTP vs HTTPS+HTTP/2 median by action

Add the testing methodology (open-model arrival-rate load -> no coordinated
omission, the smoke/load/sweep/stress/soak/regression/growth/microbench ladder,
core-pinning, median+MAD regression detection) and the architectural reasons
MockServer scales. Demote the Java-13 closed-model numbers to a clearly labelled
Historical appendix.

Charts are committed PNGs regenerated from the pipeline JSON by
images/perf-charts/render_perf_charts.py (with the source data under data/).
Add a #scalability_configuration anchor to the performance_configuration include
so the deep link resolves.

feat(llm): encode cached/reasoning token usage and reasoning content blocks

Provider codecs now emit Usage.cachedInputTokens/cacheCreationTokens/
reasoningTokens using each provider's native usage key, and Completion
gains additive reasoningText/reasoningSignature fields encoded as
provider-native reasoning/thinking content blocks (Anthropic thinking +
signature with streaming deltas, OpenAI Responses reasoning, Gemini
thought, Ollama thinking). All emission is gated on the field being set,
so output is byte-identical when unset and the request matcher is
unaffected. Threads the new fields through the httpLlmResponse schema and
the usage-inference copy path.

feat(openapi): validate request parameters and generate example parameter requests

OpenAPIRequestValidator now validates path/query/header/cookie
parameters (required-presence + per-parameter schema) in addition to
the request body, across every validation surface (contract/traffic
validation, verify_traffic, forward-validate). Parameter example-value
logic is factored into a shared OpenApiParameterExamples helper, and a
new additive OpenAPIConverter.buildExampleRequests emits concrete
example requests with path/query/header/cookie parameters.

Schema validation is conservatively skipped for array/object parameters
serialised in a non-JSON style and for untyped/composite (OAS 3.1)
schemas, so valid requests are never false-positived; required-presence
is still enforced. Full style/explode decoding is a deferred follow-up.

feat(pact): translate non-literal matchers into Pact v3 matchingRules on export

The Pact exporter previously degraded regex, JSON-schema and XPath
matchers to literal example values, losing contract semantics. It now
emits a Pact v3 interaction-level matchingRules object: regex rules for
path/query/header values MockServer treats as regex, type rules for
schemaString params/headers, per-property type rules for jsonSchema
bodies, and an XPath-keyed regex rule for xpath bodies. Additive —
literal-only interactions export byte-identically (no matchingRules
emitted). path/query/header rules round-trip back through PactImporter;
body-category rules are exported for external consumers only.

perf(log): decouple Disruptor ring size from maxLogEntries and coalesce listener notifications

Adds a dedicated ringBufferSize knob (MOCKSERVER_RING_BUFFER_SIZE,
default min(maxLogEntries,16384) rounded to a power of two) so the
in-flight LMAX ring no longer pre-allocates one LogEntry shell per
retained entry — at maxLogEntries=100000 the ring drops from 131072 to
32768 slots (~14.7MB to ~3.7MB) while the retention deque still holds
maxLogEntries. Small deployments are unchanged.

Async log-listener notifications are now coalesced: rapid adds set a
dirty flag and a single ~250ms-windowed task fires one updated() to
listeners instead of a full retrieve+serialize per add. Synchronous
notifications (stop) stay immediate; the coalescing task is cancelled on
stop. Verification/retrieval drain the disruptor and query directly, so
they are unaffected.

feat(verify): server-side eventual verification via optional timeout

Verification and VerificationSequence gain an optional timeout (millis,
capped at 60s). When set and the first evaluation fails, the server
re-evaluates on each new log event until the verification passes or the
deadline elapses, returning success as soon as satisfied (and the last
failure on timeout) — so async-app tests no longer need client-side
polling (#1713). The wait is fully asynchronous (transient log listener
+ scheduled deadline, single-completion guard, no Netty I/O thread held,
listener/future always cleaned up). Intermediate re-evaluations suppress
their verification log entries so exactly one outcome is logged. Timeout
null/absent/0 is byte-identical to the existing single-shot path.

feat(forward): opt-in HTTP/2 upstream forwarding

Adds forwardProxyHttp2Enabled (default false). When enabled, forward
actions preserve the inbound request protocol so an HTTP/2 request is
forwarded to the upstream as HTTP/2 (over TLS+ALPN, reusing the existing
HTTP/2 client stack); a request with no protocol stays HTTP/1.1. When
disabled the forwarded protocol is nulled exactly as before, so default
behaviour is byte-identical. HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) is not supported
(non-secure h2 auto-downgrades to HTTP/1.1) and h2 forwards are not
pooled — both documented.

feat(llm): add CSV optimisation-report export and Prometheus optimisation gauges

The optimisation report endpoint (and the export_optimisation_report MCP
tool) now accept format=csv, returning an RFC-4180 CSV with per-call rows
plus a totals/verdict summary section (numbers locale-pinned to '.').
Three callback gauges expose the latest optimisation verdict to
Prometheus and OTLP — mock_server_llm_estimated_waste_usd,
mock_server_llm_cache_hit_ratio, mock_server_llm_one_shot_rate — read
from a snapshot pushed when the report is built (0 before any build /
after reset). Single global gauges, no per-model labels.

feat(clients): A2A declarative mock builders across all clients + SLO/chaos parity

Adds an A2A (Agent-to-Agent) declarative mock builder to the Node,
Python, Ruby, Go, .NET, PHP and Rust clients, porting the Java
A2aMockBuilder: agent-card, JSON-RPC tasks/send|get|cancel, optional SSE
streaming, and push-notification config + delivery. Each builder
generates expectations wire-equivalent to the Java builder.

Also adds the verifySLO and startChaosExperiment control-plane helpers to
the Node, Python and Ruby clients (Go/.NET/PHP/Rust already had them),
completing SLO/chaos client parity. Load-scenario helpers were already at
full parity and are unchanged.

feat(auth): optional data-plane authentication on mocked endpoints

Adds opt-in authentication for the data plane (today auth is
control-plane/CONNECT-only). New config (default off, so behaviour is
byte-identical when disabled): dataPlaneAuthenticationRequired plus basic
(username/password/realm), bearer (token), and api-key (header/value)
schemes; any configured scheme that matches is accepted. A shared
DataPlaneAuthenticationGate enforces it before action dispatch on every
HTTP transport — HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC, and HTTP/3 — writing 401 +
WWW-Authenticate on failure. Control-plane endpoints and the liveness
probe are never gated, so a locked-down server stays administrable and
k8s probes keep working. Fails closed when required-but-unconfigured;
secrets use constant-time comparison, are never logged, and are
@JsonIgnore'd from GET /mockserver/configuration.

feat(client-java): add verifySLO and startChaosExperiment helpers

Completes SLO/chaos client parity (Go/.NET/PHP/Rust already had these).
verifySLO(SloCriteria) wraps PUT /mockserver/verifySLO, returning the
SloVerdict on PASS/INCONCLUSIVE and throwing SloVerdictAssertionError (an
AssertionError carrying the verdict) on a 406 FAIL, matching the existing
verify(...) convention. startChaosExperiment(json) wraps
PUT /mockserver/chaosExperiment. Reuses the core SLO model + serializer
(extended with serialize(SloCriteria)/deserializeVerdict).
docs(plans): mark client callback parity complete in roadmap

perf(test): add load-injection scale harness (Envoy sink) + opt-in CI step

Measure how much HTTP load MockServer can INJECT as a load generator and how that
scales by running instances in parallel:

- mockserver-performance-test/stack/inject/: docker-compose with an Envoy
  direct_response sink + N cpuset-pinned MockServer injectors + Prometheus.
  run-inject.sh raises the load-generation caps (the default 500 req/s silently
  throttles), drives a RATE stair (per-instance ceiling) and a fixed-rate hold
  across N instances (scaling), aggregates by the per-trigger run_id metric label,
  and asserts throttled/errors ~= 0 and Envoy-received ~= injected before trusting
  a number. cpuset pinning is opt-out (empty *_CPUS clears it).

- .buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-test-inject.sh + guard dispatch: opt-in only
  (PERF_INJECT / [perf-inject] marker); never runs on the normal daily perf build.
  Runs N in {1,2,4,6} on the pinned perf queue and uploads inject-ceiling.json +
  inject-scale.json artifacts.

No MockServer code change. Committed fixtures document the JSON contract consumed
by the chart renderer.

test(no-dependencies): guard shaded jar boot with a populated mockserver.properties (#2344, #2338)

Boots the mockserver-netty-no-dependencies uber jar with a mockserver.properties
file containing a sensitive key and asserts no ExceptionInInitializerError /
NoClassDefFoundError, that the sensitive-redaction path ran during static init,
and that a mock is served. Closes the seam where a class reachable only while
reading a populated property file could be missing from the shaded jar yet
undetected on the full-classpath unit tests.

test(dashboard): guard dashboard Content-Length is UTF-8 byte count, host-independently (#2347)

Strengthens DashboardHandlerTest to assert the declared Content-Length equals the
UTF-8 byte length AND differs from the ISO-8859-1 length, and adds
DashboardContentLengthCharsetForkTest run in a dedicated maven-surefire execution
forked under -Dfile.encoding=ISO-8859-1 so a revert to content.getBytes()
(default charset) is caught in CI regardless of the host locale. The fork test
skips (not false-passes) on any JVM that ignores the override. The default
surefire execution restates the inherited include/exclude set so no other tests
are dropped.

test(core): assert legacy cert backstop files stay byte-identical to canonical (#2232)

The pre-monorepo backstop copies (CA cert .pem and petstore openapi .json) live
outside the Maven module set so nothing validated them; they could silently rot
and break legacy clients' hardcoded raw URLs. This test fails loud if the repo
root cannot be located and byte-compares each backstop against its canonical copy.

ci(release): assert helm podSecurityContext renders and index.yaml/OCI chart integrity (#2320, #2282, #2281)

helm-validate.sh now renders with podSecurityContext.fsGroup set and asserts the
field appears, instead of rendering to /dev/null (which only caught parse
errors). verify.sh now HARD-checks that every chart version listed in the live
index.yaml resolves (not just the released version), and that the OCI chart was
published to ghcr.io/mock-server/charts/mockserver.

ci: silence Maven transfer-progress dot-spam in CI builds

CI Maven runs without a TTY, so Maven's interactive progress monitor emits one
dot per line and floods the build log. Add -B --no-transfer-progress to the CI
(non-TTY, docker-context) Maven invocations. Local-dev scripts and
mockserver/.mvn/maven.config are left alone so interactive progress is unchanged
for developers.

ci: upload only failing tests' logs and print an end-of-log pass/fail summary

Stop blanket-uploading per-class *-output.txt for every passing test. A new
java-collect-failures.sh copies only failing classes' TEST-*.xml + matching
-output.txt into mockserver/target/failed-tests/ and prints a passed/failed/
skipped summary at the end of the log. The build step is wrapped so the build's
exit code is preserved (red stays red) and the collector never fails the build.
TEST-*.xml are still uploaded, so junit-annotate and java-summarize are unaffected.

test(core): stop JavaScriptTemplateEngineTest busy-loops starving the parallel test fork

The two tests ran GraalJS for-loops of 1,000,000,000 iterations. GraalJS runs
interpreter-only on stock OpenJDK (no Truffle JIT), so each loop took ~14s, and
shouldHandleMultipleHttpRequestsInParallel runs 3 concurrently in the parallel
Surefire phase — on a CPU-constrained CI agent this blew past the 1800s fork
timeout and hung mockserver-core (master red for builds #1227-#1235). The tests
assert output correctness and concurrent engine thread-safety, not timing, so
shrinking the loops to 1,000,000 keeps their intent while removing the hang. Full
core suite now completes in ~1:48 instead of timing out.

perf(test): inject harness — fat-injector ceiling, derived-rate scaling, complex-scenario ceiling

Fix two issues a first CI run exposed and add an empirical complexity data point:

- Per-instance ceiling now runs ONE fat 8-core injector with a finer 2k-step
  stair (2k..20k) so it finds a clean CPU-bound plateau instead of overshooting.
- Scaling now drives lean 2-core injectors at a rate DERIVED from a lean 2-core
  ceiling probe (floor(0.8 x clean ceiling)), not a hardcoded 30k that collapsed
  every instance into errors.
- Add a COMPLEX-scenario ceiling: a 1-request-per-iteration POST with a ~1.25 KB
  Velocity-templated body + feeder, measured on the same fat injector + stair, so
  the page can show measured rps/core simple vs complex (a real complexity factor).
- Envoy: add a minimal Lua body-drain filter so POST-with-body requests stay
  keep-alive (direct_response does not drain the body, which otherwise closes the
  connection and churns the injector pool); bodyless GETs skip it, so the simple
  ceiling is unaffected.

perf-test-inject.sh runs simple ceiling -> complex ceiling -> scaling sweep on the
opt-in [perf-inject] build. No MockServer code change.

feat(templates): add configurable JavaScript template execution timeout

A runaway or malicious JavaScript response template (e.g. an infinite loop) could
pin the data-plane worker thread indefinitely; GraalJS runs interpreter-only on
stock OpenJDK so it cannot even be JIT-accelerated. A per-evaluation watchdog now
cancels a template that exceeds javascriptTemplateExecutionTimeout (millis,
default 5000; 0 or negative disables) via Context.close(true), surfacing a typed
JavaScriptTemplateTimeoutException. The property round-trips through Configuration
and ConfigurationDTO. The default is a bounded behaviour change: templates running
longer than 5s are now cancelled unless the timeout is raised or disabled.

fix(load): compute load-scenario error rate over completed requests

evaluateThresholds computed ERROR_RATE as failed/requestsSent, but requestsSent
is incremented at dispatch while failed/succeeded are incremented at completion,
so in-flight requests diluted the rate (a 3-request all-500 scenario transiently
read 2/3=0.667 instead of 1.0, intermittently failing thresholdBreachedYields
FailVerdict). Use the completed count (succeeded+failed) as the denominator so the
verdict only ever observes settled outcomes. THROUGHPUT_RPS keeps the dispatched
count by design. Terminal error rate is unchanged; only mid-flight/STOPPED
snapshots are corrected.

feat(spring): map breakpointTimeoutMillis and javascriptTemplateExecutionTimeout in @MockServerTest

The Spring MockServerPropertyCustomizer translated only a curated subset of
properties, so mockserver.breakpointTimeoutMillis and the new
mockserver.javascriptTemplateExecutionTimeout fell through to the unknown-property
warning and were ignored when set via @MockServerTest(properties = {...}). Add
both to the Long-property cases so they apply to the per-test Configuration, with
a round-trip test.

feat(core): opt-in keep-warm forward connection pool + tuned TCP keepalive

Two additions to the outbound forward client (shared by forwarding, proxying and
load injection), both defending against connection inefficiency/staleness:

- Opt-in keep-warm pool: forwardConnectionPoolKeepAlive (default false) +
  forwardConnectionPoolMaxTotalPerKey (default 2000). When enabled, release
  retains warm keep-alive connections up to maxTotalPerKey instead of closing
  down to maxIdlePerKey, so sustained high-rate low-latency forwarding/injection
  reuses connections instead of churning a fresh one per request. Default off =>
  effectiveIdleCeiling() returns maxIdlePerKey and the release/acquire path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged. Bounded per key and reaped by the existing idle timeout.

- TCP keepalive on the forward client: forwardSocketKeepAlive (default true) sets
  SO_KEEPALIVE on both forward bootstraps; on the native epoll transport it also
  tunes TCP_KEEPIDLE/INTVL/CNT via forwardSocketKeepAlive{IdleSeconds,IntervalSeconds,
  Count} (60/15/4, ~120s dead-peer detection). Epoll options are guarded so NIO
  platforms are unaffected. Complements the isActive/closeFuture/idle-reaper checks
  for faster half-open detection during active use and when the idle timeout is raised.

Reviewed (review-final + security-auditor) and tested (httpclient + configuration +
forward/proxy netty integration, 230+ tests green). Connections remain keyed by
host:port:secure so keep-warm never widens reuse scope across upstreams or TLS.

docs(ai-sdlc): add cost/duration optimisation telemetry to the spec

Add §18.6 (activity-time instrumentation) and §18.7 (parallelism
utilisation and serialisation metrics) so the integration can measure
where the time and resource cost of delivering a feature/fix actually
goes, and target optimisation effort accordingly.

Cost and duration are made distinct optimisation targets with different
levers:
- cost: largest total time/token categories, including rework that never
  lands first-pass (T5, T6, T10);
- duration: the critical path, not total work (T9, P6 "duration tax").

New requirements: T1-T11 (per-stage time + token/cost, activity taxonomy,
wait-vs-work and on/off-critical-path distinction, validation broken down
by check type, critical-path tracking, rework/discarded-work cost,
feature/fix-level roll-up reconciled to cycle time) and P1-P6 (achieved
parallelism vs effective limit, serialisation-cause capture, cap-bound
vs decomposition-bound, duration tax vs theoretical best).

Woven into §17 OP4, §18.3, §21.1, §21.5, Appendix A/B/C.

fix(ai-sdlc): close fail-open Claude /commit and classify command/skill/script/settings files as control

The Claude /commit skill was a degraded 4-step copy missing the control
class, changelog gate, review-final/gated-approval/separation-of-duties,
eval-harness gate, operator-halt check, and 8-iteration cap — so a Claude
session shipped control changes fail-open. Bring it to full parity with the

fix(security): escape backslashes in A2A regex pattern and validate report-download URL scheme

Resolve two CodeQL code-scanning alerts.

rb/incomplete-sanitization (#65, high): the A2A custom-task-handler builder
inlined a user regex messagePattern between the /.../ delimiters of a JSONPath
=~ literal but escaped only the / delimiter, so a pattern ending in a lone
backslash (or containing \/) could escape the closing delimiter and break out
of the regex literal into the surrounding JSONPath/JSON. The same defect was
present in every client library. Replace the inline escaping in all 8 clients
(Java, Node, Python, Ruby, Go, Rust, PHP, .NET) with a single-pass scanner that
preserves valid regex escape sequences (\d, \/, \\) and only neutralizes the
delimiter-breakout. Output is byte-identical for normal patterns; per-client
regression tests added.

js/client-side-unvalidated-url-redirection (#64, medium): the dashboard
load-scenario report download passed a URL assembled from user-configured
connection params to window.open without checking its scheme. Parse the URL and

fix(proxy): relay streamed forward responses by request intent (fixes opencode header timeout)

opencode proxying LLM traffic through MockServer failed with "Provider response
headers timed out after 10000ms". Root cause (confirmed against a live server):
opencode's OpenAI Codex backend streams Server-Sent Events with NO Content-Type
header, and the forward client only relayed a response incrementally when it saw
Content-Type: text/event-stream. So MockServer aggregated the whole 10-30s stream
before sending any headers, and the client timed out.

The forward path (HttpActionHandler -> NettyHttpClient) now also relays as a
stream when the CLIENT's request asked for one — an Accept: text/event-stream
header, or a JSON body with "stream": true. NettyHttpClient sets an
EXPECT_STREAMING_RESPONSE channel attribute (reused + fresh paths);
StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator switches to streaming on either the response
content-type or that request intent. Still gated by streamingResponsesEnabled and
still overridden by DISABLE_RESPONSE_STREAMING (FORWARD_REPLACE). Ordinary
non-streaming forward traffic is unaffected.

Resilience: on switching to streaming, the per-request socket read timeout
(maxSocketTimeout, ~20s, armed on non-pooled channels) is replaced by the
stream-appropriate idle bound (streamIdleTimeoutSeconds, 60s), so a streaming LLM
response that pauses >20s between chunks (model reasoning) is not killed.

Tests: NettyHttpClientStreamingIntentTest (request-intent detection units);
4 StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator EmbeddedChannel cases (intent streaming,
no over-trigger, disable-wins, read-timeout removal); 2 StreamingProxyResponse
integration cases over the forward path (no-content-type SSE upstream delaying
completion 2s — first byte arrives <1.5s with stream:true, >=1.5s without).

Content-Type: UTF-8 text (SSE/JSON/plain) is stored as a readable STRING, while

perf(retrieve): serialize REQUEST_RESPONSES off the log-consumer thread

Retrieving REQUEST_RESPONSES serialized the whole result set inside the Consumer
callback passed to MockServerEventLog.retrieveRequestResponses, which the LMAX
disruptor runs inline on the single log-consumer thread. A large retrieval (many
captured streaming bodies under a high maxLogEntries × maxStreamingCaptureBytes)
therefore (a) raced the response-future timeout (TimeoutException) and (b) stalled
all further logging while it ran — the ring buffer could fill and drop events.

New helper HttpState.awaitRetrieve(...) has the consumer thread hand back only the
(cheap, already-materialised + redacted) list via a CompletableFuture; the caller
thread then serializes. Applied to every REQUEST_RESPONSES format (JSON, log
entries, HAR, OpenAPI, Postman, Bruno, cURL). Exception handling mirrors the prior
outer handler; serialized output is byte-identical for the same log contents.

This is a general improvement (any large recorded responses, not just LLM): big
retrievals no longer time out, and live request logging is no longer blocked
during a retrieve. Tests: a 2000 × 64KB-body retrieve now completes in ~300ms
(vs the 90s timeout), and a thread-name assertion proves serialization runs off
the log-consumer thread.

feat(forward): stream HTTP/2 forwarded responses + forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade

Rebuild the HTTP/2 forward client on the multiplex stack (Http2FrameCodec +
Http2MultiplexHandler) so a streamed upstream response (Server-Sent Events) is
relayed incrementally instead of being aggregated to completion before its head
reaches the proxy client. Each stream reuses the existing HTTP/1.1 streaming
machinery (StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator + StreamingResponseRelayHandler)
on a new per-stream child initializer; the request is dispatched onto a fresh
stream by a tail outbound handler so NettyHttpClient is unchanged. Non-streaming
HTTP/2 responses still aggregate to a complete response.

Add opt-in forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade (default off): forward a secure (TLS)
request upstream over HTTP/2 via ALPN even when the inbound client is HTTP/1.1,
with automatic HTTP/1.1 fallback when the upstream does not negotiate h2. Fixes
the header timeout some streaming upstreams exhibit, where the SSE response head
is sent immediately over HTTP/2 but withheld over HTTP/1.1. HTTP/2 forwards are
not pooled.

Tests: Http2StreamingProxyResponseIntegrationTest (incremental h2 SSE relay,
non-streaming aggregation, ALPN h1 fallback); HttpForwardActionHttp2Test upgrade
precedence cases. Existing h1 streaming, h2 forward/proxy/stream-error, and
ConfigurationDTO drift tests remain green.

fix(redaction): mask query-string + SSE-body credentials, fail closed on unparseable secrets

Fixture redaction (HAR/Postman imports, the LLM optimisation report, the MCP
capture tools) previously masked only sensitive headers and named JSON body
fields. It now also:

- masks the VALUES of credential-bearing query parameters by default (key,
  api_key, apikey, access_token, token, signature, sig, and the AWS SigV4
  X-Amz-Signature / X-Amz-Security-Token) — e.g. Gemini's ?key= API key;
- redacts configured fields inside each Server-Sent-Events data: payload of a
  streamed body, preserving the event structure and non-JSON markers ([DONE]);
- fails closed when a body (or an SSE data: payload) is configured for field
  redaction, cannot be parsed, yet still mentions a configured field name —
  replacing it rather than leaking the raw secret. Ordinary unstructured bodies
  (plain text, HTML, decoded binary) that mention no configured field are left
  unchanged, so legitimate captured content is preserved.

fix(retrieve): serialize large retrieve + optimisation report off the log-consumer thread

GET/PUT /mockserver/retrieve serialized the (potentially large, e.g. captured
streaming bodies) result list INSIDE the single disruptor log-consumer thread's
callback. With many large captured bodies this could exceed the retrieve future
timeout AND stall all further logging — filling the ring buffer and dropping
events — while the serialization ran on the one log-processing thread.

The LOGS, REQUESTS and RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS branches now use the existing
awaitRetrieve(...) helper (already used by REQUEST_RESPONSES): the consumer
thread only materializes the already-redacted list (cheap), and the expensive
serialize(...) runs on the caller thread. RECORDED_EXPECTATIONS additionally
moves postProcessRecordedExpectations(...) to the caller thread (it re-enters
the log ring buffer, so running it off the consumer is also safer).

HttpRequestHandler.handleOptimisationReport now builds the report on the
scheduler instead of the Netty event loop (retrieve + redact + render of large
captured traffic must not block the event loop); the response is written from
the scheduler thread via ctx.writeAndFlush, so status/body/content-type and
error handling are unchanged. Responses are byte-for-byte identical.

fix(streaming): streamIdleTimeoutSeconds=0 truncated streams at 20s instead of disabling the bound

streamIdleTimeoutSeconds is documented to REPLACE the per-request socket read
timeout (maxSocketTimeout, default 20s) for streaming responses, so a streamed
response with an inter-chunk pause longer than 20s (e.g. an LLM reasoning gap)
is not cut off. But switchToStreamingMode only removed the socket read timeout
inside the 'if (streamIdleTimeoutSeconds > 0)' block, so setting it to 0
(disabled) paradoxically LEFT the 20s socket timeout armed and truncated
long-paused streams.

The socket read timeout is now always removed once a response switches to
streaming. With a positive streamIdleTimeoutSeconds the stream is bounded by
that idle timeout (default 60s, unchanged); with 0 it runs unbounded, as now
documented. Only the two config-present forward pipelines (HTTP/1.1 and the
HTTP/2 child) reach this code; relayOnly and null-config callers are unaffected.
Adds a regression test for the 0 case and documents 0=disabled (with a
resource-exhaustion caveat) in the consumer configuration reference.

fix(pool): arm an in-flight read timeout on pooled connections so a stalled reuse times out

With the opt-in forward connection pool enabled, a pooled keep-alive channel
carries no ReadTimeoutHandler while it sits idle in the pool (a blanket one
would fire during legitimate idle keep-alive and tear down a healthy
connection). But a request IN FLIGHT on a pooled channel — a reused connection,
or a fresh pooled channel's first request — was left unguarded, so an upstream
that connected/kept-alive but then never sent the response hung the request
until the far larger forward future timeout (90s) or indefinitely.

NettyHttpClient.armPooledInFlightReadTimeout(channel) now adds a
ReadTimeoutHandler(maxSocketTimeout) at the two pooled dispatch sites (the
reuse path and connectFresh's post-connect write), and
HttpClientHandler.tryReturnToPool removes any ReadTimeoutHandler by type before
pool.release so the idle pooled channel is unguarded again. A streaming
response strips it earlier (StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator removes it by

fix(proxy): apply forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade to the transparent-proxy forward path

forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade was honoured only by matched forward() expectations
(HttpForwardAction), not by the transparent (unmatched) proxy path that most
LLM/agent capture uses. So a coding-assistant CLI proxied over HTTP/1.1 (e.g.
opencode) was always forwarded to the upstream over HTTP/1.1 — and some
streaming SSE backends (notably the OpenAI Codex endpoint
chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses) withhold the response head over
HTTP/1.1 and only flush at completion. MockServer's streaming relay DOES engage
(the request carries stream:true so EXPECT_STREAMING_RESPONSE is set), but it
has nothing to relay until the end, so time-to-first-byte collapses to total
time and the CLI sees a streaming header timeout.

HttpActionHandler.handleUnmatchedProxyForward now applies the same protocol
selection as HttpForwardAction at both unmatched-forward dispatch points (the
main no-breakpoint path and the breakpoint-continuation executeUnmatchedForward):
when forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade is set and the request is secure, forward upstream
over HTTP/2 via ALPN (falling back to HTTP/1.1 if the upstream declines). Only
the opt-in flag + secure case is affected, so the default path is byte-identical;
HTTP/2 is TLS-only (NettyHttpClient downgrades a non-secure h2 request anyway).

Adds UnmatchedForwardHttp2UpgradeIntegrationTest: a TLS upstream with
protocol-discriminated expectations proves the unmatched forward upgrades an
HTTP/1.1 secure inbound to HTTP/2 with the flag on, stays HTTP/1.1 with it off,
and never upgrades a non-secure request.

docs(capture): enable forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade for transparent-proxy LLM capture

The npm run capture launcher now starts MockServer with
forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade=true, and the capture README's standalone command and
the configuration-properties page recommend it for transparent-proxy capture —
so streaming SSE backends (notably opencode's OpenAI Codex endpoint) send the
response head immediately over HTTP/2 instead of withholding it over HTTP/1.1
and surfacing as a streaming header timeout. ALPN falls back to HTTP/1.1, so it
is safe for every provider.

feat(metrics): record the protocol each forward connection negotiates to the upstream

Adds mock_server_forward_upstream_protocol{upstream_host,protocol} — a Prometheus
counter incremented in HttpClientInitializer at the ALPN-resolution point of each
forward/proxy client connection (configureHttp1Pipeline -> http1_1,
configureHttp2Pipeline -> http2), plus a matching DEBUG log.

This closes an observability gap: the recorded request only carries the INBOUND
protocol (e.g. HTTP/1.1 from a CLI), never whether the FORWARD leg negotiated
HTTP/2 — so there was no way to confirm forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade is taking effect
without packet capture. A forward stuck on http1_1 to a backend that withholds
its streaming SSE head over HTTP/1.1 (a cause of high forward time-to-first-byte)
is now visible in the Metrics dashboard. Null-guarded no-op when metrics are
disabled; the DEBUG log is gated. Tests + docs included.

docs(capture): raise maxSocketTimeoutInMillis so slow LLM streaming heads aren't 502'd

Bad Gateway; once the head arrives the streaming relay takes over and
streamIdleTimeoutSeconds governs the per-chunk pace. (The first-token latency
itself is the model's compute time — not a MockServer delay — and a CLI whose
own request timeout is shorter than the upstream first token must raise it
CLI-side.)

fix(ui): mirror live traffic count into ref via effect, not during render

fix(streaming): release the live StreamingBody from retained streaming log entries

A captured streaming (SSE) forward/proxy exchange logs a FORWARDED_REQUEST entry
built from a clone of the response. clone() copies the live StreamingBody
reference, and the completion listeners set the FIXED captured bytes as the body
but never cleared that reference — so every retained log entry pinned the live
StreamingBody (its <=256KB capture buffer, the upstream EventLoop, and the
onChunk/requestMore callbacks) for the entry's lifetime in the ring buffer,
roughly doubling per-entry memory and holding event-loop-adjacent objects.

setCapturedStreamingBody now clears the streaming reference on the log copy
(one place, covering all four streaming-completion sites). clone() is unchanged,
so the live response and other clone consumers still get the streaming body;
only the retained log copy is cleared. Adds HttpActionHandlerStreamingLogBodyTest.

(The companion pendingChunks-cap change was dropped after review showed it would
silently drop relayed client bytes — pendingChunks is already bounded by
auto-read backpressure to a single read batch, so there was nothing to fix.)

feat(ui): collapse a multi-turn LLM conversation into one growing trace thread

A stateless coding-assistant CLI (the OpenAI Codex backend used by opencode)
resends its entire growing conversation/reasoning context on every turn, so
consecutive recorded requests each carried a message list that is a growing
prefix-superset of the previous one. The Trace view rendered each as a full
-history blob, which read as endless near-duplicates.

Adds a pure, unit-tested groupConversationTurns(): consecutive entries collapse
into one conversation when each entry's request-message signature list is a
strict leading PREFIX of the next AND same provider kind AND same host; per turn
it exposes only the NEW messages (delta beyond the previous turn). GroupedConversationView
renders one growing thread (per-turn deltas; response/model/tokens on the last
turn, system prompt on the first). Single-turn groups render exactly as before.
Grouping is conservative (edited history / different provider / different host
never merge) and non-destructive — raw per-request data stays reachable.

fix(proxy): stream a no-Content-Type SSE response through the CONNECT proxy to the client

When capturing a coding-assistant CLI through MockServer as a transparent HTTPS
(CONNECT) proxy, the response relayed back to the client switched to streaming
only when the upstream sent Content-Type: text/event-stream. The relayOnly
StreamingAwareHttpObjectAggregator on the CONNECT loopback had no streaming-intent
hint (EXPECT_STREAMING_RESPONSE is set only on the forward-client channel), so a
backend that streams SSE WITHOUT that header — notably the OpenAI Codex endpoint
used by opencode — was aggregated to completion before being relayed to the
client, even though the forward leg streamed it.

UpstreamProxyRelayHandler now propagates the client's streaming-intent to the
loopback channel per request (set on the downstream/loopback channel just before
the request is written): EXPECT_STREAMING_RESPONSE=TRUE when the request carries
Accept: text/event-stream or a JSON body matching "stream":true, else cleared.
EXPECT_STREAMING_RESPONSE is made public and a netty-FullHttpRequest equivalent of
NettyHttpClient.requestExpectsStreamingResponse is added. Only explicit client
intent triggers streaming, so ordinary buffered responses (incl. chunked-without
-Content-Length servlet responses) are unaffected, and the body read is
non-destructive (no reader-index/refcount change).

Adds ConnectProxyStreamingResponseIntegrationTest (real CONNECT+TLS tunnel to a
no-Content-Type SSE upstream): stream:true -> incremental first byte; plain GET
-> buffered; ordinary response relayed unchanged. Fails decisively without the fix.

fix(http2): complete HTTP/2 client round trip when server replies on a server-initiated stream

The HTTP/2 forward/client multiplex stack (Http2FrameCodec + Http2MultiplexHandler)
installed an inbound-stream handler that RST-reset any server-initiated (inbound)
stream. MockServer's own non-multiplex HTTP/2 server (the HttpToHttp2ConnectionHandler
path) returns some responses — e.g. gRPC reflection and websocket object-callback
forwards — on a fresh server-initiated (even) stream instead of echoing the request's
stream id. The strict multiplex client treated that response stream as an unsolicited
inbound stream and reset it, so the response was discarded and the request's stream
never completed: direct HTTP/2 round trips and HTTP/2 forwards hung until timeout
(TimeoutException / ReadTimeoutException). The previous InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter
client tolerated this because it correlates at the connection level, not by stream id.

Since the client disables server push (pushEnabled=false), an inbound stream can only
be such a misattributed response, so route it through the same per-stream response
pipeline (Http2ForwardStreamChildInitializer) instead of resetting it. A spec-compliant
upstream answers on the client-initiated stream and never creates an inbound stream, so
the same-stream path and the incremental SSE streaming feature are unchanged.

Restores GrpcReflectionIntegrationTest and HTTP2ExtendedMockingIntegrationTest while
keeping Http2StreamingProxyResponseIntegrationTest, UnmatchedForwardHttp2UpgradeIntegrationTest
and HttpForwardActionHttp2Test green.

feat(ui): MCP Health latency prefers an externally-measured x-mcp-latency-ms hint

The MCP Health panel derives latency from the proxy timing or MockServer's own
response-time header. For traffic where MockServer didn't time the underlying
call — notably the stdio-MCP capture bridge, which times the real out-of-band
MCP exchange and forwards it as x-mcp-latency-ms — that response time only
reflects MockServer's tiny processing time, making a slow stdio MCP server look
fast. exchangeLatencyMs now prefers x-mcp-latency-ms (request header) over the
response-time header, so a slow stdio MCP server shows its true latency (and the
slow flag). Proxy timing still wins when present; normal traffic is unaffected.

feat(capture): reverse-proxy launcher mode + stdio MCP capture bridge

Two capture-tooling additions:

- npm run capture --reverse-proxy HOST[:PORT] runs MockServer as a REVERSE
  (port-forwarding) proxy to a single upstream instead of a forward/HTTPS_PROXY
  proxy; the tool points its BASE URL at MockServer (OPENAI_BASE_URL is set). This
  route uses the same streaming + forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade path as the forward
  proxy (not the CONNECT loopback), so it also isolates whether a streaming
  timeout is CONNECT-specific. opencode's Codex backend is not base-URL-overridable
  (subscription-pinned), so reverse mode suits standard-API tools.

- scripts/llm-proxy-capture/mcp-stdio-capture.mjs — a passthrough bridge you
  register in place of a STDIO MCP server's command. It relays the child's stdio
  byte-for-byte (the CLI is unchanged) while tee-ing each JSON-RPC exchange to
  MockServer over HTTP, so a stdio MCP server (e.g. chrome-devtools-mcp, which an
  HTTP proxy can never see) appears in the AI · MCP Health panel alongside the LLM
  traffic — per-server call count, error rate (JSON-RPC errors tee'd as 5xx), the
  methods, and real per-call latency (forwarded as x-mcp-latency-ms). A
  prototype/PoC of proxying a stdio process, not a hardened tool.

fix(proxy): apply forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade to the proxyPassMappings reverse-proxy route

handleProxyPass (the proxyPassMappings reverse-proxy path) forwarded with
httpClient.sendRequest directly and never applied the HTTP/2-upgrade protocol
selection the matched-forward and transparent/unmatched-forward paths use — so a
streaming SSE backend reached via a proxy-pass mapping (e.g. the OpenAI Codex
endpoint) stayed on HTTP/1.1 and withheld its response head until completion.

Applies the same guard (forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade && clonedRequest.isSecure() ->
withProtocol(HTTP_2)) before the proxy-pass sendRequest. clonedRequest.isSecure()
reflects the mapping's isTargetSecure() (https scheme), so only an opt-in flag +
secure target triggers it; the default path is byte-identical. Completes the
forwardProxyHttp2Upgrade coverage across all three forward routes.

Adds ProxyPassMappingHttp2UpgradeIntegrationTest (TLS upstream with protocol-
discriminated expectations): flag-on+secure -> upstream sees HTTP/2; flag-off ->
HTTP/1.1; non-secure target -> HTTP/1.1.

fix(config): accept InMillis timeout property names (silently-ignored overrides)

The forward/proxy first-byte wait (maxSocketTimeout), the socket connect wait
(socketConnectionTimeout) and the websocket-callback wait (maxFutureTimeout) are
exposed by the Java API (Configuration.*InMillis()) and the
/mockserver/configuration JSON under their unit-bearing `...InMillis` names, but
ConfigurationProperties read the system property / environment variable only under
the unit-less names (mockserver.maxSocketTimeout / MOCKSERVER_MAX_SOCKET_TIMEOUT,
etc.). So setting the natural -Dmockserver.maxSocketTimeoutInMillis (the name shown
everywhere else) was silently dropped and the default stood - long enough to 502 a
healthy but slow first-byte response (e.g. a reasoning LLM backend that takes >20s
to emit its first token when proxied/forwarded).

Accept the `...InMillis` system-property / env-var names for all three timeouts as
exact synonyms via a small read-with-alias helper. The two names are
interchangeable; the primary (unit-less) key is read first, so a value applied at
runtime via the programmatic setter is never silently overridden by a launch-time
alias, and the alias is honoured whenever the primary is unset. The new names are
declared as MOCKSERVER_* constants so the reflective recognised-key registry
accepts them.

Adds ConfigurationTest reproduction tests (fail on old code, pass now), notes the
alias in the configuration-properties consumer doc, and corrects the capture README.

feat(core): bound event-log memory and capture proxied requests to disk

Proxying large request/response bodies (LLM tool schemas, growing
conversation context, accumulated SSE) retained every exchange in full in
the in-memory event log, which is bounded only by entry count
(maxLogEntries), never by size, so a long capture session could exhaust
the heap and crash the proxy.

Add three opt-in properties:
- maxEventLogSizeInBytes: byte-budget eviction of the event log, the OOM
  guard, evicting the oldest entries once retained body bytes exceed it
- persistRecordedRequestsToDisk + persistedRecordedRequestsPath: append-only
  NDJSON archive of every proxied exchange, full bodies, flushed per line,
  so the complete session survives even as the in-memory window evicts
- maxLoggedBodyBytes: in-memory body-truncation valve

All three compose in MockServerEventLog.processLogEntry: clone, write full
bodies to disk (FORWARDED_REQUEST only), truncate in-memory copies, add to
the deque weighed by LogEntry.estimatedHeapSize. The NDJSON archive honours
redactSecretsInLog so credentials are masked on disk as in the dashboard.
The launch-with-llm-capture.sh capture launcher now enables a 2g heap, a
256MB byte budget and disk capture by default. Internal and consumer docs
and the changelog are updated.

fix(proxy): stop HTTP/2 client hang when forwarding to an HTTP/2 upstream

An HTTP/2 client through the forward/CONNECT proxy hung when MockServer
forwarded to an upstream that also served HTTP/2. Netty's
InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter tags the decoded upstream response with a synthetic
x-http2-stream-id header carrying the upstream stream id; that internal header
leaked through the response mappers and was re-emitted to the client, so the
response was written on the wrong stream id and the client's HTTP/2 codec
rejected it (PROTOCOL_ERROR / GO_AWAY), hanging the request until timeout.

FullHttpResponseToMockServerHttpResponse.setHeaders now skips the Netty
x-http2-* extension-header family (STREAM_ID/SCHEME/PATH/STREAM_DEPENDENCY_ID/
STREAM_WEIGHT/STREAM_PROMISE_ID) so they never enter the response model;
MockServerHttpResponseToFullHttpResponse defensively removes x-http2-stream-id
before deriving the id from the protocol-guarded field, keeping that field the
single source of truth. HTTP/1.1 clients and directly-mocked HTTP/2 responses
are unaffected; captured/recorded responses also no longer carry the internal
header.

Locked by mapper unit tests that fail when the fix is reverted; a both-legs-
HTTP/2 CONNECT-proxy integration case adds end-to-end coverage.

fix(core): derive functional maxExpectations/maxLogEntries defaults when JMX heap max is undefined (-1)

native image of the shaded jar) heapAvailableInKB() went hugely negative and
the derived maxExpectations/maxLogEntries defaults collapsed to <= 0, so
expectations were accepted with 201 but silently dropped and the log ring
buffer dropped every event from startup. Fall back to Runtime.maxMemory()
when the JMX max is <= 0, floor heapAvailableInKB() at 0, and floor both
derived defaults at the dev-mode minimum (1000) so the store stays
functional. Documented the floor in the consumer configuration page and

feat(telemetry): selectable OTLP metrics aggregation temporality (cumulative | delta)

Add mockserver.otelMetricsTemporality (default cumulative, unchanged behaviour)
so the OpenTelemetry metrics exporter can report counters/histograms as
per-interval deltas instead of cumulative running totals. Delta is preferred by
backends such as New Relic: a delta counter carries only the change within the
interval, so the backend need not track a monotonic series per producing
pod/instance, reducing time-series cardinality.

- OtelMetricsExporter.startIfEnabled() chains
  AggregationTemporalitySelector.deltaPreferred() onto the OtlpHttpMetricExporter
  builder only when the value resolves to delta; resolution is fail-safe
  (isDeltaTemporality: trimmed, case-insensitive, locale-independent; null/blank/
  unknown keep cumulative and never throw). The cumulative path is byte-for-byte
  the previous builder chain.
- Reclassify the two monotonic counter mirrors (mock_server_slow_requests_total,
  mock_server_http_chaos_injected_total) from observable gauges to observable
  counters so delta applies to them; gauges stay gauges. OTLP-only — the
  Prometheus scrape endpoint remains cumulative.

security(http3): validate QUIC source address + restrict CONNECT-UDP relay (SSRF)

Two defence-in-depth fixes to the experimental HTTP/3 (QUIC) server (off by
default, http3Port=0), both previously self-documented risks in docs/code/http3.md.

1. Source-address-validating retry tokens. Replace Netty's InsecureQuicTokenHandler
   (plaintext, trivially forgeable token) with SourceAddressQuicTokenHandler, which
   binds the client IP into an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by a per-server random secret. Tokens
   are source-address bound and unforgeable, so a forged-source Initial packet cannot
   obtain a valid token, mitigating QUIC address-spoofing / traffic amplification.
   Correct for IPv4 and IPv6.

2. Restrict the CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) relay. Add http3ConnectUdpAllowedTargets
   (comma-separated host / host:port allowlist, default empty): when non-empty only
   matching targets are relayed, others refused with 403. Also honour the existing
   forwardProxyBlockPrivateNetworks policy (via InetAddressValidator) so private /
   loopback / link-local / cloud-metadata targets are refused when that flag is on.
   Defaults preserve existing behaviour unless a restriction is opted into.

as a response template against the triggering request, instead of being a
fixed string.

  gRPC grpcStreamResponse renders per-message templateType (already on the
  model) in the eager server-stream handler.
- A shared StreamTemplateRenderer renders each payload against the request
  using the same engines and context (request fields, jsonPath, built-in
  helpers, faker, scenario) as HttpResponseTemplateActionHandler, with lazy
  per-handler engine caching. SSE renders a per-event copy (never mutates the
  stored event); WebSocket renders text frames before breakpoint interception
  (binary frames are never templated).
- JavaScript streaming payloads are supported via a new
  TemplateEngine.renderTemplateText(...) that executes the template's
  handle(request) and coerces the return to text (string verbatim, otherwise
  JSON.stringify'd) through PolyglotRunner's new rawText mode. If GraalJS is
  absent, a JAVASCRIPT template fails loudly with the same clear error the
  response-template path uses rather than degrading silently.

feat(matchers): match expectations on client-certificate subject/issuer/fingerprint

Add a clientCertificate request matcher so an expectation can match on the
mutual-TLS client certificate a request presents. The presented chain was already
captured on HttpRequest.clientCertificateChain (TCP + HTTP/3) but no matcher
referenced it.

ClientCertificateMatcher matches against the leaf certificate (index 0 - the
client's own certificate) by:
- subject: Common Name, full subject Distinguished Name, or any Subject
  Alternative Name (DNS/IP/email/URI)
- issuer: issuer Common Name or full issuer Distinguished Name
- fingerprintSha256: SHA-256 of the leaf's DER encoding (colons/whitespace and
  case normalised)

Each criterion is a NottableString (regex / ! negation / optional). Negation uses
De Morgan semantics across the candidate strings (AND) so !X only matches when no
candidate form is X. Wired into HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher's immutable Compiled
holder and the MatchDifference diff (new CLIENT_CERTIFICATE field). Serialization,
deserialization and the httpRequest JSON schema updated.

Non-breaking: an expectation without a clientCertificate matcher behaves exactly
as before, and a request presenting no chain never matches a non-blank criterion.
Matching only - mTLS authentication (MTLSAuthenticationHandler) is unchanged.

fix(streaming): relay content-type-less streams over CONNECT + HTTP/2 upstream; header-only FORWARD_REPLACE keeps streaming

streaming and could make the client time out waiting for response headers. A
header-only modification (status/headers/cookies, no body change) is now applied
to the streamed response head while the body chunks are relayed untouched; only a
body-affecting modification (a body/schema response override, a JSON body
patch/merge-patch modifier, or a response template) still disables streaming.

perf(startup): create the forward-client event-loop group lazily on first proxy use

The forwardClientGroup (clientNioEventLoopThreadCount threads, default 5)
was created in the LifeCycle constructor even for pure-mock servers that
never forward. It is now created on first forward/proxy action:
LifeCycle.getForwardClientEventLoopGroup() double-checks a volatile field
under forwardClientGroupLock; MockServer passes the accessor as a
Supplier<EventLoopGroup> through HttpActionHandler to NettyHttpClient
(existing EventLoopGroup constructors delegate). WAR servlets pass their
existing group unchanged.

The disjoint-group self-deadlock invariant is preserved exactly: the lazy
group is always a new group, never the server workerGroup. Create-vs-stop
races are fail-closed: an accessor that wins the lock while stopping
immediately shuts the fresh group down, so no event-loop group can leak.

Measured with U1+U3: host fat-jar bind 489ms / ready 804ms (from 562/919
baseline); mock-only servers start 5 threads lighter.

feat(llm): semantically-plausible deterministic embeddings via n-gram feature hashing

Replace hash-seeded uniform-random deterministic embedding vectors with
seeded FNV-1a n-gram feature hashing (word unigrams/bigrams + boundary
char 3-grams, signed hashing, sublinear TF, L2 normalisation) so
same-input+seed+dimensions vectors stay deterministic while similar
texts now get meaningfully higher cosine similarity, enabling offline
RAG-retrieval ranking tests. Locale-independent tokenisation
(Locale.ROOT) and graceful empty-vector handling for non-positive
dimensions. API shape and the non-deterministic random path unchanged.

fix(security): constant-time SOCKS5 credential compare and deeper mTLS client-cert validation

Extract the constant-time comparison into a shared
authentication/ConstantTimeEquals utility (MessageDigest.isEqual over
UTF-8 bytes), use it for SOCKS5 proxy username/password checks that
previously used String.equals, and delegate the existing data-plane
comparison to it. Harden MTLSAuthenticationHandler from
checkValidity+direct-signature to single-cert PKIX CertPath validation
per configured CA plus Extended Key Usage enforcement (EKU present must
include clientAuth or anyExtendedKeyUsage; absent EKU still allowed per
RFC 5280 practice). MockServer-generated client certs already carry
clientAuth so existing setups keep working; failures stay fail-closed
with unchanged client-facing messages.

docs(website): navigation aids on the four hardest-to-traverse pages

Add a client-side filterable property index (plus clustering and blob
store section anchors) to configuration_properties.html, an
OpenAPI-vs-WSDL capability overview table to using_openapi.html, a
retrieval-methods quick-reference table (REST path, Java client method,
