table to proxy/configuring_sut.html. All anchors validated against
rendered includes; the filter is inline self-contained JS with no
external resources.

feat(wasm): envelope v2 with query params and cookies, and test-rule wiring in both editor extensions

Add version 2 of the match_request envelope carrying
queryStringParameters (name to value array) and cookies alongside the
existing method/path/headers/body, so WASM rules can route on query
params and cookies. The change is strictly additive: v1 modules ignore
the new fields, proven by running the unchanged prebuilt v1 module
under a v2 envelope through the real chicory runtime. The Rust SDK
gains query_param/cookie/version accessors and a new rust-request-v2
example module. POST /mockserver/wasm/test is now wired into the
VS Code extension (mockserver.testWasm command) and the JetBrains
plugin (TestWasmModuleAction), mirroring the existing module-list and
upload actions.

feat(metrics): dual-publish _total Prometheus counters for the five monotonic count metrics

Publish true monotonic Counters (mock_server_requests_received_total,
mock_server_expectations_not_matched_total,
mock_server_response_expectations_matched_total,
mock_server_forward_expectations_matched_total,
mock_server_llm_chaos_injected_total) alongside the legacy _count
gauges so PromQL rate()/increase() work correctly without renaming or
breaking the dashboard UI and existing Grafana dashboards. Counters
increment in lock-step with the gauges from the same call sites,
survive server reset (gauges still zero as documented), and mirror to
the OTLP export as observable monotonic sums. Serialize the two
globally-stateful metrics test classes with the existing MetricsLock
ClassRule and pin the reset contract with a dedicated test.

feat(llm): OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live voice/WebSocket event mocking

Add scripted event codecs for the two dominant realtime voice APIs as
a thin layer over the existing httpWebSocketResponse primitive — no
new action type, DTO, or schema. OpenAiRealtimeCodec emits the GA
event protocol (session.created/updated, conversation.item.created,
response lifecycle with output_audio_transcript/output_audio/
output_text deltas and response.done usage); GeminiLiveCodec emits the
BidiGenerateContent flow (setupComplete, serverContent modelTurn with
inlineData audio and outputTranscription, generationComplete,
turnComplete, usageMetadata). RealtimeMockBuilder in the Java client
wires codec output into WebSocket expectations, converting per-event
gaps into cumulative monotonic delays so the concurrently-scheduled
frames stay ordered. Audio payloads are placeholders; event-protocol
fidelity is the target. Unimplemented protocol corners are explicitly
documented per provider.

feat(async): Kafka Avro with Schema Registry, AMQP subscribe/verify, and MQTT 5

Close the three audit-verified async broker parity gaps. Kafka values
can now be Avro in the Confluent wire format (magic byte + schema id)
for both publish and subscribe/verify, with schema resolution against a
Schema Registry URL or registry-less inline schemas, built on Apache
Avro rather than the Confluent serde stack (licensing and dependency
weight; documented). AMQP gains the subscribe/verify side, mirroring
the publisher's queue and routing-key binding resolution. MQTT 5 is
supported via Paho mqttv5 selected by mqttProtocolVersion: 5 (v3
default unchanged), adding user-property headers on publish and
consume. Unknown kafkaValueFormat or mqttProtocolVersion values are
rejected loudly. Validated against live brokers (RabbitMQ, Mosquitto,
cp-kafka) via Docker-gated Testcontainers tests. Protobuf payloads and
Schema Registry authentication remain documented deferrals.

feat(import): WireMock, Mountebank, and Mockoon migration importers

Add one-shot importers converting WireMock stub JSON (single stub,
array, or mappings export), Mountebank imposter JSON (http/https), and
Mockoon environment JSON into MockServer expectations via the existing
PUT /mockserver/import endpoint (?format=wiremock|mountebank|mockoon,
plus JSON-structure auto-detection that fails loud on ambiguity). Every
unmappable construct emits a structured warning in the new
{expectations, warnings} response body — never a silent drop; legacy
HAR/Postman/Pact imports keep their bare-array response. Faithful
semantics verified against each tool: WireMock priority 1-is-highest
maps to (5 - p) so explicit priorities outrank default-priority
catch-alls, Mountebank single-response repeat stays unlimited, default
case-insensitive regex predicates keep (?i), and Mockoon :param paths
regex-escape literal segments. Imported fixtures pass through the same
credential redaction as HAR/Postman via a new action-preserving
redaction path.

feat(ui): log-pressure eviction banner and bulk select/clear on expectations and traffic

Surface ring-buffer eviction where users look: a dismissible warning
banner on the Dashboard and Traffic views polls the existing
/mockserver/metrics endpoint (15s, paused when the tab is hidden,
stopped permanently when metrics are disabled) and warns when
mock_server_dropped_log_events_total grows — the leading cause of
verification intermittently failing — linking to the maxLogEntries
guidance. Add a Select mode to the expectations list and traffic view
with per-row checkboxes, select-all over the visible filtered rows,
and confirm-gated bulk delete/clear batching the existing single-row
operations with partial-failure toasts; traffic Select mode is
mutually exclusive with the two-row compare mode, and the clear
confirmation notes that clearing matches by request shape so identical
logged requests clear together.

feat(grpc): forward proxy with decoded recording and replay

Bring the record-then-mock workflow to gRPC, which was previously
mock-only. A new fail-safe GrpcForwardTranslator encodes a decoded
JSON gRPC request back to framed protobuf for the upstream (forcing
HTTP/2, adding te: trailers, stripping internal x-grpc-* headers) and
decodes the upstream's framed response to JSON, re-stamping the gRPC
method and status headers. Wired at HttpForwardAction.sendRequest for
all six FORWARD action types and at the anonymous/reverse-proxy send
sites, with the decode composed into the memoized response override so
the caller and the FORWARDED_REQUEST log entry both see decoded JSON —
making recorded gRPC exchanges directly replayable as mocks. Upstream
trailers are now folded into the response model (framing-critical
names excluded by Netty, no-duplicate guard, x-http2-* skipped) so
trailer-form grpc-status from real gRPC servers is preserved on relay,
in recording, and on replay. Unary and client-streaming requests plus
unary and server-streaming responses ship; bidirectional streaming
forward and no-descriptor passthrough are documented boundaries.
Non-gRPC forwarding is byte-for-byte unaffected.

feat(openapi): style/explode parameter validation and discriminator/readOnly/writeOnly example generation

Decode array/object parameters from their OpenAPI style/explode
serialisation (query form/spaceDelimited/pipeDelimited/deepObject,
path simple/label/matrix, header simple, both explode values, spec
defaults applied) into type-aware JSON before schema validation,
closing the documented deferred gap where such parameters were skipped
unless already JSON-shaped. Decoding is fail-open exactly where the
old code was, so valid requests stay valid; genuinely non-conforming
values now return the documented 400. Example generation gains a
Direction: oneOf/anyOf discriminators pick a concrete subschema and
stamp the mapping key, readOnly properties are omitted from request
examples and writeOnly from response examples, with direction-less
legacy callers unchanged and the allOf normalisation untouched.

feat(observability): server Grafana dashboard, Helm ServiceMonitor, and durable NDJSON audit sink

Ship a standalone importable Grafana dashboard for the server metric
family (request/match/forward rates via the new _total counters,
latency percentiles, expectation levels, chaos, dropped log events,
JVM) under examples/grafana. Add a disabled-by-default Prometheus
Operator ServiceMonitor template to the Helm chart (interval, labels,
relabelings configurable; chart version unchanged). Add an optional
auditLogFile property (empty default off, wired through the full
config trio) appending one JSON line per control-plane AuditEntry to
an NDJSON file — a separate fail-soft observer of the same entries the
in-memory audit ring holds, so the ring's non-durable contract is
unchanged and a reset no longer erases the trail it records.

feat(client): fluent MockServerClient.builder() covering all construction dimensions

Add a discoverable fluent builder over the eight constructor overloads
(configuration, host/port/contextPath, port future, secure, proxy
configuration, control-plane JWT as string or supplier, request
override) with localhost:1080 defaults, loud mutual-exclusion between
the port-future and host/port/contextPath dimensions, and pure
delegation to the existing constructors and with-setters so behaviour
is unchanged and no constructor is deprecated.

feat(matchers): JWT-claims request matcher and allOf body composition

Add a jwt request matcher that routes on claims inside a JWT carried
in a configurable header (default authorization with Bearer prefix):
per-claim exact/regex/negated criteria plus issuer, audience, and
algorithm convenience fields, decoded with base64url and Jackson only.
Signatures are deliberately NOT verified — this is test routing, not
authentication, and is documented as such; malformed or absent tokens
are a clean non-match and negated criteria match vacuously when the
claim is absent. Add an ALL_OF body type composing existing body
matchers that must all match the same body (e.g. jsonPath + jsonSchema
+ regex), honouring per-component and composite negation. Both are
rolled out through the full wire surface: model, DTOs, serializers,
strict and non-strict deserializers, JSON schemas, matcher engine, and
MatchDifference diagnostics. Typed client-library wrappers are a
follow-up; the REST wire format works everywhere today.

test: run StreamTemplateRendererTest in the sequential Surefire phase

The first JavaScript render in the class pays the GraalJS/Truffle
context cold-start, which under parallel CPU contention exceeds the 5s
javascriptTemplateExecutionTimeout and has kept CI red since 5b23d6d17
(build 1354). Mirror the existing treatment of the sibling template
engine test classes: exclude from the parallel phase, include in the
sequential phase, keeping the production timeout untouched.

feat(editors): no-Docker binary-bundle launch in the VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin

Both editors can now start MockServer from the self-contained jlink
binary bundle on machines without Docker: resolve a locally-installed
bundle via a settings path, or download the platform bundle for the
extension's own version from the GitHub release with mandatory SHA-256
sidecar verification (fail-closed — a missing or unfetchable sidecar
aborts unless the user explicitly consents), unpack to the extension
cache, and spawn the launcher with start/stop/status tracking and log
streaming. The JetBrains process is destroyed on IDE shutdown via a
registered shutdown task; VS Code cleans up in deactivate. Downloads
require explicit user confirmation, the version setting is validated
before URL and path use, and archive entries are checked for path
traversal before extraction.

feat(llm,scim): subword streaming tokenization and SCIM list sorting

Rewrite TokenCounter as a dependency-free GPT-style subword
approximation (leading-space absorption, case and letter-digit splits,
CJK density, punctuation handling) validated against cl100k_base —
English prose within about 15 percent. Streaming can emit
subword-sized deltas via the new streamingPhysics.subwordStreaming
flag across all five chat codecs; the flag defaults off so existing
golden fixtures and whole-word wire output stay byte-identical. Add
sortBy/sortOrder to the SCIM CRUD list endpoint (nested dotted paths,
case-insensitive, missing-attribute entries last, stable, applied
between filter and pagination) with loud 400s for invalid input and
sort.supported=true in ServiceProviderConfig.

feat(wasm): ABI v3 shape_response export for WASM-computed dynamic responses

WASM rules can now shape the response, not just match the request: a
module exporting shape_response receives a version-3 envelope with the
matched request and the response the expectation would return, and
returns a partial update (status replaced, headers merged with empty
values removing a header, body replaced; 0 opts out). Fully backward
compatible — modules without the export behave exactly as before, and
modules with both exports match first then shape. Fail-safe: traps,
invalid JSON, out-of-bounds or oversized returns (1 MiB cap) fall back
to the unshaped response with a once-per-module warning, never a 500.
Wired at the response-materialisation layer for static RESPONSE
actions (documented boundary), with the shaped response flowing to
logging and recording. The Rust SDK gains shape-response macros and
helpers with a new rust-shape-response example module, and POST
/mockserver/wasm/test can exercise shaping against a candidate
response.

feat(testcontainers): Ruby and PHP modules, wired clients, and version-matched default images

Add Testcontainers modules for Ruby (testcontainers-mockserver gem,
PUT /mockserver/status readiness probe) and PHP (getMockServerClient
helper — the base class owns getClient), bringing container support to
eight languages. Every polyglot module now exposes a wired MockServer
client helper pointing at the mapped host and port, and derives its
default image tag from the installed client version with a latest
fallback instead of the stale hard-pinned mockserver-7.0.0. Go keeps
documented construction guidance instead of a bundled client because
the Go client module lacks the /v7 semantic-import-versioning suffix,
which would make a bundled dependency unresolvable for consumers.
Release-pipeline registration for the new modules is a separate gated
follow-up.

feat(config): seeded template faker and per-host upstream client mTLS

Add templateFakerSeed (long, default 0 keeps the current unseeded
behaviour) so the template faker helper produces deterministic sample
data across Velocity, Mustache, and JavaScript engines for
reproducible fixtures, and forwardProxyClientCertificatesByHost — a
host=certificateChainPath;privateKeyPath map (case-insensitive host
match) letting the forward proxy present a different client
certificate per upstream host for outbound mTLS, falling back to the
global pair; unmapped hosts share one cached SSL context so the cache
stays bounded. Both properties are wired through the full
configuration trio and covered by the reflective DTO drift guard.

feat(proxy): WebSocket passthrough with frame recording

Relay WebSocket upgrades through to a real upstream when a request in
proxy mode has no matching mock — or matches a plain HttpForward —
completing the 101 handshake both sides and relaying text/binary/
ping/pong/close frames over plain or TLS upstreams. Upstream trust
honours the forward-proxy client TLS configuration, the private-network
SSRF block (forwardProxyBlockPrivateNetworks) is enforced before
connecting, and per-frame backpressure pauses the flooding side when a
peer's outbound buffer saturates. Relayed frames are recorded as a
FORWARDED_REQUEST transcript (direction/opcode/payload, bounded by
webSocketProxyMaxRecordedFrames and an 8MB cap) so dashboard and
retrieveRecordedRequests show WebSocket traffic; an opt-in
webSocketProxyIdleTimeoutSeconds reaps idle relays. HTTP/2 extended
CONNECT and the delay/rateLimit/chaos/breakpoint/drift features on a
matched forward are documented boundaries (Times and verify still
apply).
improved linking in external docs to the fast tests content

test: run CoreMiscConfigurationTest in the sequential Surefire phase

CoreMiscConfigurationTest mutates JVM-global system properties
(templateFakerSeed, forwardProxyClientCertificatesByHost) but was
added without registering it in the sequential phase, so
GlobalStateMutationGuardTest failed the core build (master red on
d134f9630 onward). Exclude it from the parallel phase and include it
in the sequential phase, the established pattern for global-state
tests.

build(release): automate Homebrew, Scoop, winget, Chocolatey, SDKMAN, and asdf publishing

Add release-pipeline components that render each package manager's
manifest from the real jlink binary-bundle assets and their published
.sha256 sidecars, and publish per channel: Homebrew tap formula, Scoop
bucket, asdf/mise plugin (repo pushes), plus winget, Chocolatey, and
SDKMAN. Each component follows the existing pattern — full,post-maven
release-type gate, --dry-run/--execute, and a graceful exit 0 when its
secret or target repo is not yet configured or the bundle assets are
absent — so the pipeline never fails for an unconfigured channel. The
three repo-push channels clone a tokenless URL and inject auth per git
command via http.extraheader with an EXIT-trap work-dir cleanup, so no
credential is ever written to disk. Wired into a soft-fail Package
Managers group after the Binary Bundles step. Publishing prerequisites
(tap/bucket/plugin repos and vendor secrets) are documented per channel
and remain to be configured before any channel goes live.

fix(editors): harden binary-bundle extraction shell-out and use current IntelliJ platform APIs

VS Code: the Windows archive-extraction step built a PowerShell command
by interpolating the bundle paths into the -Command string. Pass them
through the process environment instead and read them back as
$env:MOCKSERVER_ARCHIVE_PATH / $env:MOCKSERVER_DEST_DIR, so no path is
concatenated into the command text — closing CodeQL
js/shell-command-constructed-from-input (a path containing a quote or
semicolon can no longer break out).

JetBrains: the plugin used the Decompressor single-File constructors
and extract(File) — removed in the 2026.2 platform (NoSuchMethodError)
and deprecated earlier — and the @ApiStatus.Internal ShutDownTracker to
kill the launched process on IDE close. Switch to the Path-based
Decompressor overloads and register the shutdown cleanup against the
application Disposable via Disposer, preserving the destroy-on-shutdown
behaviour. verifyPlugin is now Compatible against all six recommended
IDEs (243 through 262) with no gated API findings.

fix(vscode): spawn the bundled java directly instead of via cmd.exe (CodeQL #67)

The prior fix hardened the archive-extraction shell-out but not the
actual flagged sink: the binary launcher ran bin/mockserver.bat through
spawn("cmd.exe", ["/c", launcher, ...]), so the version-derived bundle
path was handed to a shell interpreter (js/shell-command-constructed-
from-input). Replace the launcher indirection with a direct spawn of
the bundle's runtime/bin/java executable — java -jar mockserver.jar
<serverArgs> — on every OS, with no cmd.exe and no shell. The bundle
root is derived for the cached, configured-directory, and
configured-launcher-file cases, and both the java executable and jar
are existence-checked with a clear error. MOCKSERVER_JAVA_OPTS keeps
its word-split semantics and JVM-args-before-jar ordering; the process
is tracked as java directly (cleaner stop on Windows). Confirmed with
the CodeQL CLI: the alert reproduces on the old code and is gone on the
fix across all five CWE-078 command-injection queries.

feat(llm): stream subword-sized deltas by default

Make subwordStreaming the default for streamed LLM responses so a
streamed response emits finer, subword-sized deltas out of the box,
closer to a real provider's per-token cadence. The default resolves at
a single point (TokenCounter.streamingTextTokens): unset or null
physics now means subword; only an explicit
streamingPhysics.subwordStreaming=false restores whole-word deltas.
The streaming golden fixtures were regenerated through the codec
golden harness. Behaviour change: a stream now carries more, smaller
deltas at the same tokensPerSecond, so its total duration is slightly
longer and the per-provider streaming wire output is finer-grained;
per-event physics timing is unchanged.

feat(client): expose the jwt and allOf matchers in the OpenAPI spec and Node types

Add the jwt request matcher and the ALL_OF body matcher (shipped
server-side) to the OpenAPI spec (new Jwt schema referenced from
HttpRequest; ALL_OF member with bodyAllOf in the Body union) and to the
generated Node client type definitions, so Node users get typed
support and the published spec is accurate. The Java client already
exposes both via the shared core model (jwt()/withJwt and
allOf(...)/withBody), and every other client library can send them over
the REST wire format. Documents Java and Node examples for both
matchers.

feat(client): jwt and allOf matchers in the Python, Ruby, PHP, Rust, and .NET clients

Add typed builders for the jwt request matcher (claims with exact/regex
and !-negation, plus issuer/audience/algorithm/header/scheme) and the
ALL_OF body matcher (bodyAllOf composing existing body matchers) to the
five hand-written clients, mirroring each client's existing matcher
idiom and emitting the exact server wire format. Also adds the
correctly-keyed regex and jsonPath sub-body factories these clients
needed so an allOf composition actually matches server-side; the Ruby
regex body factory previously emitted a value key the server parsed as
a literal string rather than a regex, which is now corrected.

feat(go): /v7 module path, jwt/allOf matchers, and a bundled Testcontainers client

Add the required Semantic Import Versioning suffix to the Go client
module (github.com/mock-server/mockserver-monorepo/mockserver-client-go
/v7) so it is properly go-get-able as a dependency — updating the
module line, all internal and example imports/requires/replaces, and
the release/publish scripts (the publish tag is mockserver-client-go/
v7.x.y, whose major matches the suffix). Add typed jwt request-matcher
and allOf body-matcher builders to the Go client matching the other
libraries. With SIV fixed, the Go Testcontainers module now bundles the
client and exposes container.Client(ctx) returning a ready client
pointed at the mapped host and port, replacing the previous
manual-construction-only guidance.

build(release): publish the Ruby and PHP Testcontainers modules on release

Register tc-ruby (RubyGems, testcontainers-mockserver) and tc-php
(Packagist via subtree-split mirror) as release-pipeline components,
mirroring the existing tc-* components. Each renders/prepares from the
module source, publishes via the sanctioned load_secret path (tc-ruby
reuses the existing RubyGems secret; tc-php pushes the subtree split to
the Packagist mirror using http.extraheader auth with EXIT-trap
cleanup, no token on disk), and graceful-skips (exit 0) when its
credential or mirror repo is not configured so the release never fails
for an unconfigured channel. tc-ruby self-bumps its own version.rb to
match the release version. Wired into the publish group as soft_fail
steps.

fix(ui): report real server errors in debug-mismatch, tighten network-error detection, re-show log-pressure banner after restart

- debugMismatch: read the response body as text before JSON.parse so a
  non-2xx with an empty or HTML body reports the real status instead of
  'Failed to connect to MockServer'
- isNetworkError: classify by fetch-failure message heuristics instead of
  treating any TypeError as a network failure, so programming errors are
  no longer masked as connectivity problems
- LogPressureBanner: detect dropped-events counter regression after a
  server restart and reset the dismissal so fresh drops re-show the banner

fix(ui): keep dashboard state and filters intact across WebSocket errors and reconnects

- reconnect re-sends the last requested request filter instead of the
  filter captured when the socket first connected, so a server restart
  no longer silently streams unfiltered data behind an enabled filter
- an error-only push (sent when a filter fails deserialization) no longer
  blanks the log, expectation, and request panels; arrays are only
  reconciled when present in the message
- data pushes only clear push-sourced errors, so user-action errors such
  as a failed clear are no longer wiped within a second

fix(client-python): Body.regex now matches as a regex, not a literal string

The Python client's Body.regex emitted {"type":"REGEX","string":value},
but the server's body deserializer treats a string value-key as a
literal StringBody regardless of the type field, so Body.regex(...) only
ever matched the pattern text literally. Emit the schema-correct
{"type":"REGEX","regex":value} so it matches as a real regex, and
remove the redundant same-cycle regex_match factory. A live-server
integration test proves a pattern now matches by regex rather than
literal text.

fix(ui): keep paused breakpoint exchanges across view changes and make frame editing UTF-8 safe

- paused exchanges now accumulate in the app-lifetime callback client
  instead of component state, so navigating away from the Breakpoints
  view no longer silently discards exchanges pushed while unmounted
  (previously the client request hung until the server-side timeout with
  no way to resolve it from the UI)
- stream-frame modify/inject encode via TextEncoder/TextDecoder so UTF-8
  frame bodies (LLM streams) round-trip correctly, and encode failures
  surface in the dialog instead of throwing uncaught in the click handler
- the callback WebSocket now reconnects indefinitely with capped backoff
  instead of giving up after 20 attempts
- resolveRequest/resolveResponse no longer mutate held header objects and
  handle both object-form and list-form headers

fix(templates): surface invalid template output as a distinct failure event instead of a silent 404

When a response or forward template rendered output that failed
HttpResponse/HttpRequest schema validation, the failure was logged as a
generic untyped ERROR and the fallback 404 was logged as
EXPECTATION_RESPONSE, so a broken template looked like a successful mock
response in the dashboard. The shared template-output deserializer now
emits a request-correlated TEMPLATE_GENERATION_FAILED event carrying the
validation error and the rendered output, styled as an error in the
dashboard log. The 404 client response is unchanged.

feat(ui): add a Try It Now path to the get-started view

fix(ui): stop composer edits from silently stripping expectation fields the form does not model

Editing an expectation in the dashboard rebuilt its JSON from the form
alone and re-registered it under the same id, destructively dropping
scenario bindings, namespaces, response sequences, cross-protocol
scenarios, gRPC bidi responses, and matcher fields such as keepAlive,
socketAddress, and protocol.

The form now acts as an overlay: on edit or duplicate the original JSON
is retained and the form-generated JSON is merged onto it, so modeled
fields are authoritative from the form while everything else passes
through unchanged. The action slot is only replaced when the form
actually models the original action; quick-mock updates own the slot
only for plain static responses and otherwise preserve the original
action. An info alert lists the preserved fields in both quick and
advanced modes, and the review diff shows the exact merged payload that
is registered.

test(llm): reconstruct streamed text before asserting in LlmAgentLoopE2eTest

build(docker): run the standard and local images on a JDK 25 runtime

Re-apply the two closed dependency PRs properly: bump the standard and
local Docker images' runtime JVM from Temurin 17 to 25. This is
runtime-only — MockServer's library is still compiled to the Java 17
floor, so consumers on Java 17 are unaffected; only the JVM inside the
self-contained image changes. Switch the jlink flag from the removed
numeric --compress=2 to the JDK-21+ --compress=zip-6 form (equivalent
ZIP compression), rename the temurin17-trimmed runtime path to
temurin25-trimmed throughout, and update the JDK-version comments. The
AppCDS base and dynamic archives are trained and run on the same JDK 25
so they stay version-consistent. Verified by building docker/local on
25 (java -version = 25.0.3, AppCDS archives load cleanly, status 200);
the ~0.57s startup figure was measured on JDK 17 and is flagged in the
docs for re-measurement on 25 rather than overwritten.

feat(mock): force a response-sequence variant per request with x-mockserver-response-index

A request matching an expectation that carries multiple responses can

but never advance the sequential/switch rotation, which lives on its own
match-time-snapshotted counter so concurrent normal callers keep their
collision-free positions. The header stays on recorded traffic for
verification fidelity and is filtered from every outbound forward — the
HTTP request mapper and the WebSocket passthrough relay. Out-of-bounds
or malformed values are ignored and normal selection applies.

tool can attribute.

fix(mock): only attach a timing block when latency was actually injected

Attaching a timing block to every mock response changed the serialised
response inside recorded log messages, breaking the recorded-log golden
assertions in the netty and servlet integration suites (mockserver-java
build 1451). A plain mock response with no injected chaos latency,
configured delay, or breakpoint hold now carries no timing block, so its
recorded and retrieved form is byte-identical to the pre-waterfall
behaviour; the waterfall still renders whenever MockServer actually
injected latency, which is the only case it has anything to attribute.

fix(demo): fail fast with actionable errors when the MQTT broker cannot start

The --with-broker flow masked environmental failures: an implicit image
pull inside an unchecked docker run surfaced only as a generic 30-second
port timeout, and a port already held by another listener let the TCP
probe pass against the foreign process so the script falsely reported
the broker ready and failed later, deep in the populate step. The demo
container from a previous run is still self-cleaned first; the port is
pre-flighted with a clear port-in-use message; the image is pulled
explicitly with a distinct error naming likely causes; docker run's exit
code is checked; and the wait loop surfaces the container's logs
immediately if it stops running.

fix(ui): remove the recent-view tabs from the app bar

The recent-view quick tabs crowded the navigation so the bar no longer
fit on typical widths, and they were not judged an improvement. The

nav-group icon correction is kept.

The Audit view showed a generic empty state on servers where the audit

fix(release): stop pipefail misreading SIGPIPE from short-circuiting grep as failure

prepare.sh gated the release on 'printf ... | grep -q' under set -o
pipefail: grep -q exits on the first match and closes the pipe, and once
the Unreleased changelog section outgrew the 64 KB pipe buffer (70 KB
for 7.4.0) printf died with SIGPIPE, pipefail surfaced 141, and the
inverted check aborted the release with 'changelog.md has no bullets
under Unreleased' despite 67 bullets. All var-into-grep -q pipes in the
release scripts are converted to here-strings, and the npm packument and
Packagist verification loops capture the curl body before grepping so a

  `accordion inner` (the Java-only OpenAI Realtime and Gemini Live
  blocks are left as-is).
- creating_expectations.html: convert the eight intro per-language
  tabs to `accordion inner`.
- retrieve_code_example.html: add a Java client tab (Format.GO/CSHARP/
  RUBY/RUST/PHP) to the go/csharp/ruby/rust/php retrieve-format groups
  that previously showed only the REST API tab.

Legitimate exceptions preserved: the template-engine tabs in the
capture "Three-Step Order Flow", the REST-only "Force a Variant"
request, WireMock/Mountebank/Mockoon imports (no client helper exists),
and Node-vs-browser / multiple-Java-client tabs.

docs(website): give the capture example full typed client tabs

The "Three-Step Order Flow" example under "Capturing & Reusing Request
Values" previously had only template-engine-split tabs (JSON + Velocity/
JavaScript/Mustache + curl) and no per-client examples, unlike every
other feature on the page.

Rebuild it as the canonical nine client tabs (Java, JavaScript, Python,
Ruby, Go, .NET, Rust, PHP, REST API). Each tab registers both steps —
the step-1 `capture` rule and the step-3 JavaScript response template —
using each client's TYPED model objects and methods (CaptureRule /
HttpTemplate), matching the rest of the page rather than raw JSON:
Java withCapture + template(); Node typed capture/httpResponseTemplate
literals; Python CaptureRule/HttpTemplate; Ruby CaptureRule/HttpTemplate;
Go NewCaptureRule + ResponseTemplate; .NET CaptureRule.Of +
RespondWithTemplate; Rust capture_rule + respond_template. PHP has no
typed capture or response-template model, so it keeps the documented
Expectation::fromArray(...) raw-JSON fallback with a note.

The Velocity/JavaScript/Mustache read-back syntax remains documented in
the section intro, so no template-engine information is lost.

build(analytics): commit PostHog feature-usefulness dashboard provisioner

Keep the "MockServer - UI Feature Usefulness" PostHog dashboard definition
in version control instead of hand-clicking it. scripts/analytics/
create_posthog_dashboard.py (stdlib-only, --dry-run capable) creates the
dashboard and nine HogQL insights via the PostHog REST API, answering which
dashboard UI features and tabs users actually use.

The analytics ingest key baked into released images is write-only and cannot
create dashboards, so the script authenticates with a personal API key read
from POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY (never committed). Tiles are usage-, adoption-,
and trend-based because the analytics is cookieless (distinct_id = session,
not person; no cross-session retention). README documents the run steps, the
event schema, and the data caveats.

fix(release): idempotent MCP republish and self-healing mirror pushes

Rerunning a release against an already-published MCP version failed with
a duplicate-version rejection even though the registry was in the
desired state — that case now logs and succeeds. The PHP mirror pushes
failed permanently when the mirror had been seeded with a scaffold
commit the subtree split can never fast-forward onto; since the mirrors
are derived state written only by this pipeline, a rejected fast-forward
now force-converges the mirror with a logged fallback instead of
failing the release.

fix(build): align netty-tcnative-boringssl-static to 2.0.78.Final

The Netty 4.2.16.Final upgrade pulls the netty-tcnative native classifier
artifacts in transitively at 2.0.78.Final, but the boringssl-static version
was still pinned at 2.0.77.Final, failing the maven-enforcer
DependencyConvergence rule and breaking every build (buildkite + CodeQL java).

Align the pinned version and the matching NETTY_TCNATIVE Docker build args to
2.0.78.Final.

docs(plans): record Jackson 3 upgrade as blocked on swagger-parser

Jackson 3 support is requested regularly (#1970, #2426) and the answer
has so far lived only in issue threads. Capture it as a backlog item
under docs/plans/later/ alongside security-defaults.md.

The sole remaining blocker is io.swagger.parser.v3:swagger-parser, which
has no Jackson 3 release and transitively pins swagger-core. Records the
four upstream trackers to watch (swagger-parser#2261 is the one that
actually gates us), the versions checked on 2026-07-19, why the
io.github.vpelikh swagger-core fork does not unblock us, and a cheap
re-check procedure.

Also records what is no longer blocking: the Java 11 floor went away
with 7.0.0, and Jackson 2/3 coexistence is already proven in-tree by
json-schema-validator 3.x running on tools.jackson.

fix(worktree): resolve rebase lock via git-common-dir, not .git

Inside a linked worktree `.git` is a FILE (a gitdir pointer), not the shared
object-store directory, so a lock path built from a relative `.git/…` or from
`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to a different location per worktree —
the rebase mutex then fails to actually serialise, allowing two sessions to
rebase/push concurrently and clobber each other.

Resolve the lock (and, in agent-status.sh, the worktree base and .tmp samples
path) from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, matching check-halt.sh. Verified
that the main checkout and a linked worktree now compute the identical absolute
lock path.

docs(clustered-state): document length-prefixed composite-key encoding

Add the lossless length-prefixed key encoding used by
ScenarioManager.ScenarioKey#toString() and CrossProtocolEventBus.backendKey()
(<trigger>|<len>:<name>:<len>:<state>:<len>:<pattern>) that prevents component
delimiters from colliding at key boundaries before keys reach the backend
store. Verified against CrossProtocolEventBus.backendKey and its collision
regression tests.

fix(grpc): reply on the request's own HTTP/2 stream

Two pre-existing defects, both unrelated to what issue #2419 reported, and
both invisible to the existing tests because they only manifest against a
real gRPC client over HTTP/2.

Responses written directly by GrpcToHttpRequestHandler (health check, server
reflection, chaos faults, request-decode errors) and the whole of the
server-streaming path bypass the paths that normally stamp the HTTP/2 stream
id: the streaming handler writes raw Netty objects rather than going through
MockServerHttpResponseToFullHttpResponse, and direct writes never reach
ResponseWriter.writeResponse. Netty's HttpToHttp2ConnectionHandler.getStreamId
then falls back to connection().local().incrementAndGetNextStreamId(), so the
reply goes out on a fresh server-initiated stream that the client is not
reading and the call hangs until its deadline.

For server streaming this meant a real gRPC client received NOTHING at all:
measured with grpc-java against an expectation with two messages and no
delays, 0 of 2 messages arrived before this change and 2 of 2 after. HTTP/1.1
was unaffected, as it has no stream ids.

Every direct write now funnels through one place that stamps the stream id
alongside the gRPC-Web marker, so a new direct-response path cannot forget
one. The streaming handler sets the id on its initial response; Netty latches
it from the initial HttpMessage and reuses it for the subsequent content
frames, so setting it once covers the whole stream.

fix(grpc): make gRPC responses spec-compliant for real clients (#2419)

A documented unary gRPC expectation was rejected by every real gRPC client.
Two defects caused it: the JSON-to-protobuf conversion only ran when the
RESPONSE carried x-grpc-service/x-grpc-method, but those are set on the
request and never propagated to the matched response, so a normal mock
returned raw JSON on a stream the client expected to be framed protobuf; and
grpc-status was sent as a response header rather than the terminal trailer the
wire format requires. MockServer now remembers the service and method
resolved from each request, keyed by HTTP/2 stream id so concurrent calls on
one connection are each converted against their own method's output type, and
emits grpc-status as a trailer on every path.

Fixing that exposed the rest of the wire contract, all of it verified against
a real grpc-java client:

- An unmatched request no longer fabricates a plausible success. Any non-2xx
  response without an explicit gRPC status is mapped per the specification's
  HTTP-status table (404 becomes UNIMPLEMENTED) with its body dropped, so a
  typo'd path surfaces as a client-side error instead of a synthesized reply.
- grpc-message is percent-encoded, exactly once, wherever it is written. It
  was previously emitted raw, which corrupts ordinary input because clients
  percent-decode on receipt, mangles non-ASCII, and let a message containing
  CRLF inject a second grpc-status line into the gRPC-Web trailer frame and
  turn an error into a success.
- grpc-timeout is honoured, including mid-stream cancellation of server-,
  client- and bidirectional streaming. An expectation whose delay outlasts the
  client's deadline now returns DEADLINE_EXCEEDED from the server and drops
  the late response, rather than writing to a stream the client abandoned.
- Message-size limits report RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED rather than INTERNAL and are
  configurable via maxGrpcMessageSize; an unsupported grpc-encoding reports
  UNIMPLEMENTED with grpc-accept-encoding telling the client what to retry
  with, instead of failing opaquely inside gzip.
- HTTP/3 behaves identically to HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2: status resolution is
  shared rather than reimplemented per transport, which is how it had drifted
  into reading status from headers only and fabricating success for unmatched
  requests.
- Body-less responses use the Trailers-Only form on HTTP/2, chaos custom
  trailers reach gRPC-Web clients through the in-body trailer frame, and
  MockServer advertises SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS explicitly rather than
  inheriting a Netty default that changed within a minor version.

grpc-java is added at test scope only, so the wire contract is verified
against an actual client rather than asserted at handler level - the gap that
let the original defect ship past a green suite.

fix(client-node): reject failed verifications instead of silently passing

Every verify* method returns a thenable whose rejection handler notified
the caller's error callback when one had been supplied, but simply
returned when one had not -- which fulfilled the promise it returned. A
failure consumed with a single-argument .then(onSuccess) was therefore
swallowed: the success handler never ran, nothing threw, and the promise
resolved as though the verification had passed. Code of the shape

    return client.verify(...).then(() => { ... })

passed unconditionally, so a suite could be green while proving nothing.

Route all seven verify* methods through a single verificationRequest
helper that re-throws when no error callback was supplied. Under Node
that surfaces as a rejection; in the browser build, whose transport is a
hand-rolled thenable running synchronously from the XHR load listener, it
surfaces as an uncaught error instead. Loud in both cases.

await was never affected -- it supplies its own reject handler, which is
why the existing tests never caught this -- and the two-argument
.then(success, error) style is unchanged.

Fix the same swallow in verifySLO, which additionally returned early
before parsing the response, so a PASS/INCONCLUSIVE verdict arriving via
the error path never reached the success callback. It now parses first
and returns its promise so the verdict can be chained.

Drop the inverted guard `if (error) { sucess(result) }` from the same
handlers. It was unreachable: both transports reject with a plain string,
never an object carrying a status code.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: suites consuming a verification with a single-argument
.then(...) may see tests that pass today start to fail. Those failures
are real and were previously hidden. A fire-and-forget call whose promise
is discarded now produces an unhandled rejection, which terminates the
process on Node 15+.

Tests land in mock_server_node_client_test.js, one of the files CI runs.
The three added single-argument .then() tests fail against the previous
code and pass against this one; the await and callback-style tests pass
either way, documenting the paths that were always safe.

Collapses seven copies of the handler into one (-142 lines).

fix(openapi): serve the full control-plane spec and guard the two copies against drift

The OpenAPI specification lives in the repository twice - the copy published on
the website and the copy bundled into the jar and served at
GET /mockserver/openapi.yaml - and nothing compared them. They drifted apart in
both directions: the served copy was missing 54 of 68 paths, while the website
copy was missing model properties the served copy had.

Because every schema is declared additionalProperties: false, the gap rejected
valid payloads rather than merely omitting them. Five realistic expectations
validated against the website copy failed all five; the bundled copy rejected
two of the five.

Reconcile the two into one specification stored in both places. The merge is a
pure union - no path, schema, operation, property, enum value or union branch
was dropped from either side. Every added property was verified against its
serialization DTO first, which turned up HttpChaosProfile.connectionDrop as a
property that does not exist in MockServer at all; it is removed, and the 18
real chaos properties the schema lacked are added.

Also document what the handlers actually read: the correlationId, namespace,
fanInLocalOnly and forwardUnmatchedTo query parameters on /retrieve, the
format=recording mode and its source and redaction parameters on /import, and
the format-by-type applicability constraints that Format.java enforces but the
spec presented as a free cross-product.

Add OpenApiSpecSyncTest asserting the two copies are byte-identical, which is
what stops this recurring. Byte equality is release-safe: prepare.sh already
rewrites the same info.version into both files in one commit. The test reports
the structural difference - which paths and schemas each copy is missing - so a
failure is actionable without diffing 5,500 lines. Its javadoc records the gap
it does not cover: it compares copy to copy and never spec to DTO, so the 11
Expectation fields absent from both copies stay unguarded.

Regenerate the Postman and Bruno collections from the reconciled spec.

docs(changelog): record the OpenAPI spec reconciliation

The entry was dropped by the union merge driver during the rebase of
dd4bcfc80, which reported "Rebasing (1/1)skip" and landed the commit's

fix(log): stop verify(never()) silently passing once the event log evicts

The event log ring buffer discarded entries with no counter, no log line and
no metric, and verification had no way to know. Once the log rolled over,
verify(never()) began passing on its own: the requests proving it wrong had
simply been thrown away. "This endpoint was never called" turned green by
itself, with no signal anywhere.

Eviction is now observable. CircularConcurrentLinkedDeque counts evictions --
it is the only layer that can tell a true eviction from an explicit clear() or
a targeted removeItem(), since all three share one callback. MockServerEventLog
exposes the count, WARNs once on the first eviction naming maxLogEntries, and
mirrors it to a mock_server_evicted_log_entries Prometheus counter.

Verification can no longer claim more than it knows. When the log has evicted,
any verification asserting an upper bound -- never(), atMost(n), exactly(n),
once(), between(a,b) -- now fails rather than passing on an incomplete record.
The strictness is deliberately asymmetric: eviction can only push the observed
count too low, so atLeast(n) and the bare verify(request) (which defaults to
atLeast(1)) are untouched, and a failure is never turned into a pass. Both the
request and response verify paths are guarded. failVerificationOnEvictedLog
(default true) restores the old behaviour for anyone who needs it.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: suites that are green today may correctly go red. If one
does, the log was already incomplete and the previous pass was not
trustworthy. Note this includes once(), which asserts EXACTLY one call.

An explicit reset(), and clear-everything, drop the eviction taint -- otherwise
one rollover would leave a long-running server permanently unable to prove
absence. A filtered clear deliberately does not: removing some entries says
nothing about the evidence eviction already destroyed.

Also fixes a real race on the forward path. The verify/retrieve visibility
guarantee rests on disruptor FIFO ordering, and drainDisruptor can only wait
for entries already published. The mocked path logs before writing, but every
forward path did the reverse, so a client that got its response and
immediately verified could miss the exchange. Plain verify(once()) hid this
because RECEIVED_REQUEST publishes early. The three non-streaming forward
paths now log first; streaming stays as-is and is documented, because its
entry carries the captured body and total duration, neither of which exists
until the stream ends.

Docs: memory-management.md claimed a flat 2-3 log entries per request. Every
expectation evaluated before a match also logs EXPECTATION_NOT_MATCHED at
INFO, so the real figure scales with the expectation count -- users were
sizing maxLogEntries an order of magnitude too low, which is what made this
bug so reachable.

ci: run client conformance suites on server and test-fixtures changes

Client pipelines were gated solely on their own directory, so a change to
mockserver/ triggered only the Java pipeline. Wire-format drift therefore
shipped with zero verification in Node, Python, Ruby, PHP, .NET, Go or Rust.

test-fixtures/ matched no trigger regex at all: editing the shared parity
corpus or known-gaps.json ran no build whatsoever.

Client pipelines now trigger on their own directory OR any server /
test-fixtures change (trigger_client_if_changed). mockserver-maven-plugin/ is
excluded — it has its own pipeline and does not define the wire format — and
test-fixtures/ is added to the Java trigger since the Java model round-trips
the same corpus.

Verified by executing the trigger logic against synthetic change sets: a
mockserver-core change goes from 1 pipeline to 8, a test-fixtures change from
0 to 8, while a client-only change still triggers that client alone and a
maven-plugin change still triggers no client.

ci: actually run the cloud blob-store contract suites

S3BlobStoreContractTest, GcsBlobStoreContractTest and AzureBlobStoreContractTest
are Docker-gated via Assume(isDockerAvailable()). java-build.sh calls
run-in-docker.sh without -s, so the socket was never mounted, Docker was never
available, and all three suites skipped on 100% of CI builds while reporting
green. Any mutation to those three stores passed CI.

They now run in their own socket-enabled step rather than by adding -s to the
main build. run-in-docker.sh exit-0s the ENTIRE script when a socket is
requested on a PR build (host-root breakout risk), so -s on java-build.sh
would have made the whole Java reactor silently pass on every PR — trading a
narrow false positive for a total one. The split keeps the main build
socket-free and confines the PR-build socket skip to the three cloud modules,
where it is announced in the log instead of hidden behind an Assume.

Maven's exit code alone is not a sufficient gate here: the Assume guards mean
an unusable socket reports the suites as SKIPPED and still exits 0. The step
therefore asserts via assert-suite-ran.sh that each suite executed at least
one non-skipped test.

Verified locally with Docker: all three suites run for real against MinIO,
fake-gcs and Azurite (16 tests each, 0 skipped, all passing). Mutating
S3BlobStore.delete to return true on NoSuchKeyException reddens the gate
(shouldReturnFalseForDeletingMissingKey fails, Maven exits 1).

test(container): fail closed when the integration suite records no result

run_all_tests only ever sets EXIT_CODE from a non-empty FAIL_LOG, and every
per-test result is written by the test script itself calling logTestResult. A
script that crashed before reaching that call — missing file, set -e abort in
start-up, docker unavailable, a bad cd — left no record at all, in neither the
pass log nor the fail log. The suite then exited 0 having run nothing.

Two changes:

  - test() records any unaccounted-for non-zero exit, so a crash that never
    reached logTestResult is still tallied. A result the script already
    recorded is not double-counted.
  - the summary fails when nothing at all was recorded. SKIP_ALL_TESTS, and
    SKIP_DOCKER_TESTS together with SKIP_HELM_TESTS, remain explicit opt-outs
    and stay green.

test() takes an optional second argument for deliberately advisory tests.
helm_clustered_convergence is known-flaky and documented as non-blocking, but
a caller-side `|| true` can no longer express that: test() records the result
as a side effect before returning, so the caller never gets the chance. Its
k8s failure modes (kubectl timeout, pod-not-ready, k3d image-import race) abort
under set -e before the script can log anything, which would have reddened the
whole suite. Passing non_blocking routes that case to the warn log instead —
visible and advisory rather than silent. All 23 other call sites stay
fail-closed by default.

Verified: a simulated total crash goes from exit 0 to exit 1 with 15 recorded
failures; a blocking test that crashes without recording reddens the suite; the
non-blocking one does not, but still appears in the warn log; a test that
records its own failure is tallied exactly once.

test(clients): make the silently-skipping client suites actually run

Every non-Java client had an integration suite that reported green while
executing nothing:

  - Go and .NET skipped without MOCKSERVER_URL, which CI never set
  - Rust's suite is entirely #[ignore]d and CI never passed -- --ignored
  - PHP ran --testsuite Unit only, so tests/Integration/ never ran
  - Node CI ran a hand-maintained 7-file list while the suite had 15
  - Go/.NET/Rust testcontainers steps were soft_fail: true, so failures
    reported green

Each client now gets a step that runs its integration suite against a live
MockServer built from HEAD, via a shared with-mockserver.sh helper (the same
build-from-HEAD approach Python and Ruby already use, rather than the stale
published snapshot image). soft_fail is removed from the three testcontainers
steps.

Setting MOCKSERVER_URL alone was not enough. Go additionally skips when the
server is merely unreachable, so a broken helper would have restored the silent
skip. Go, .NET and PHP therefore honour MOCKSERVER_REQUIRE_SERVER=true, which
CI sets: a missing or unreachable server fails the build loudly instead of
quietly testing nothing.

Node test files are now discovered rather than listed. Three divergent
hand-maintained lists existed — the CI step (7 files), run_with_local_server.js
(7) and package.json's test:external/test:coverage (12) — each missing a
different subset, so files added later ran nowhere. sre_slo_chaos_test.js ran
in neither npm test nor CI.

The Node coverage thresholds are raised at the same time, deliberately in this
commit: enlarging the file set while leaving thresholds calibrated for the old
7-file list would ship a weaker gate on a larger suite. Re-measured against all
15 files with a live server — lines 86.91%, branches 84.11%, functions 92.92% —
the gate moves from 68/72/74 to 84/90/80, a 2-3 point margin since CI measures
against a Docker image rather than the HEAD jar.

Verified: the 8 newly-enabled Node files pass (73 tests); the full suite
discovers 15 files and runs 425 tests; the coverage gate passes at 84/90/80 and
demonstrably fails when the bar is raised above actual. Go strict mode goes
from exit 0 with silent skips to a hard failure.

Two pre-existing failures remain in mock_server_node_client_test.js when run
against a HEAD-built server; they are not caused by these changes and are left
for separate diagnosis.

docs(ci): document the client conformance triggering and fail-closed gates

Records why client pipelines now trigger on server and test-fixtures changes,
and adds a table of the gates that previously reported green while executing
nothing, with the mechanism that makes each fail closed.

Also captures why the cloud blob-store suites run in their own socket-enabled
step rather than by adding -s to java-build.sh: run-in-docker.sh exit-0s the
entire step when a socket is requested on a PR build, so -s on the main build
would have made the whole Java reactor pass on every PR.

test(grpc): make the spec-compliance regression guards actually discriminate

Several guards added with the gRPC spec-compliance work were vacuous: the
production code was correct, but the tests stayed green when the fix was
deleted. Each was closed by adding fixtures that change under the transform
being guarded, and every one was proven by applying the exact mutation and
confirming the build turns red.

- gRPC-Web trailer-frame percent-encoding was only ever exercised with
  plain-ASCII messages, so dropping the encode call kept every test in
  mockserver-core green; only a test in mockserver-netty caught it. Added
  core-level coverage with percent, non-ASCII and CRLF payloads.
- The untrusted-upstream grpc-message sanitisation on the forward-proxy path
  had no coverage at all: no test set the header, and stripControlCharacters
  had zero references. Added hostile fixtures, and pinned that the translator
  did not bail to its fail-safe, so a throwing mutation cannot hide in the
  catch either.
- The reflection frame-length header was asserted with a 7-byte payload, so
  the three high-order length bytes were zero and indistinguishable from
  default array initialisation. Sized the fixtures so each byte carries a
  value, and made the harness read the declared length rather than assume
  everything after offset 5 - which makes three existing tests discriminate
  too.
- Reflection error envelopes were asserted only as non-null, valid_host was
  never checked on the response, the health-check service-name varint was
  never tested past one byte, and the streaming decoder's Configuration
  constructor was unused by any test despite four production call sites.

Adds orders.proto/orders.dsc, the first fixture with imports, which reaches
the descriptor store's dependency recursion and the well-known-type example
values - neither reachable from the existing import-free fixtures. Documents
how to regenerate all three descriptor sets; the commands are verified to
reproduce the committed files byte-for-byte.

Registers GrpcHealthRegistryTest in the sequential Surefire phase: it mutates
the process-global registry singleton and was only in the parallel phase.

The one behaviour change: a gRPC forward-proxy response that fails to decode
is now logged at WARN with the service and method. The wide catch is
deliberately left as-is - narrowing it changes proxy failure behaviour and
belongs in its own change - but it no longer swallows failures without trace.

fix(security): make runtime security controls take effect instead of reporting success

Five security controls accepted configuration at runtime, reported success, and
did not act. Each had a positive test (works when set at startup) and no negative
test (actually denies), which is how the whole class survived.

Control-plane authentication never activated when enabled at runtime. The mTLS,
JWT and OIDC handler chain was built once during server bootstrap and pushed into
HttpState, so enabling it afterwards - system property, Configuration setter, or
PUT /mockserver/configuration - returned 200, echoed back true on GET, and left
the handler null. A null handler maps to "authenticated". An operator hardening a
running shared or CI instance was told it was locked while it stayed fully open,
including the recorded request log, which in proxy mode holds real captured
credentials. The handler is now derived from the live configuration and rebuilt
when the auth-relevant configuration changes, so every route takes effect and
disabling works too. If authentication is required but the handler cannot be
built, the control plane now denies rather than falling open.

tlsMutualAuthenticationRequired never reached the SSL context. Neither setter
raised rebuildServerTLSContext - unlike the subject-alternative-name siblings -
so the cached context stayed pinned at ClientAuth.OPTIONAL with a trust-all trust
manager and certificateless clients kept connecting. The setters now raise the
flag, and NettySslContextFactory additionally compares a client-authentication
signature at the point of use. The signature is the substantive fix: the flag is
a manual step that covers only the Configuration route, not the system-property
route, which has no instance to flag. preventCertificateDynamicUpdate no longer
suppresses the rebuild - it governs certificate regeneration, not client-auth
policy.

Forward-proxy credentials were compared case-insensitively and in non-constant
time. Both the CONNECT and plain-HTTP paths checked Proxy-Authorization through
containsHeader, whose comparison is equalsIgnoreCase. Base64 is case-sensitive,
so this accepted credentials differing only in case - roughly one bit of entropy
lost per alphabetic character - and short-circuited, reintroducing the timing
channel ConstantTimeEquals exists to close. Both paths now share one validated
comparison. ConstantTimeEquals' own javadoc claimed the CONNECT path routed
through it; it did not.

GET /mockserver/metrics and GET /mockserver/http3status had no authentication
gate at all, alone among the control-plane endpoints served beside them. Metric
cardinality scales with the number of configured expectations, so an
unauthenticated caller could infer the expectation surface of a running instance.
Both are now gated. Control-plane authentication is opt-in, so default behaviour
is unchanged and no existing scrape configuration breaks.

dashboardAnalyticsKey was never redacted: the predicate matched 13 hard-coded
substrings that omitted bare "key". Redaction is now driven by name shape, with
documented exceptions.

WASM modules ran with no fuel, timeout or interrupt, so a module containing an
unbounded loop pinned the calling thread permanently - and because WASM rules are
evaluated during request matching, that can wedge matcher threads. Adds
wasmExecutionTimeoutMillis (default 5000), enforced on a bounded daemon executor;
a timed-out invocation fails closed. The fail-closed boundary now catches
Throwable so OutOfMemoryError cannot escape it.

Enabling the Velocity sandbox at runtime was inert - velocityDisallowClassLoading
was read once when the engine was built and every call site caches the engine.
The engine is now rebuilt when the setting changes. Adds javascriptAllowedClasses,
an allow-list that takes precedence over the deny-list, because exact-string
denial cannot be a security boundary: denying java.lang.Runtime still leaves
java.lang.ProcessBuilder and Class.forName reach-through. Both template defaults
are deliberately unchanged - flipping them breaks existing templates silently at
request time, which warrants its own decision.

wasmEnabled, wasmMaxMemoryPages and the new wasmExecutionTimeoutMillis are now
read from the live configuration at the point of use rather than the static
property store, so all three take effect through every configuration route.

Tests are parameterised over the configuration ROUTES rather than written once
per control, since the defect was never in a single control but in the assumption
that any route reaches the enforcement point. Verified against the unfixed code:
27 failures for control-plane auth, 4 for mTLS, 3 for the Velocity sandbox, 2 for
redaction, and a hang for the WASM budget.

Kept as one commit: the netty test file spans control-plane auth, the endpoint
gates and the proxy-credential call-site guard, so every seam I tried left a
broken or misleading intermediate.

fix(serialization): stop a leading '!' or '?' inverting a matcher value

A NottableString serialises to a bare string, where a leading '!' means "not"
and a leading '?' means "optional". The reader strips those markers
unconditionally, so string("!foo", false) went on the wire as "!foo" and came
back as NOT "foo" — the exact opposite of what was asked, with no escape.

Serialise such values as the object form {"not":false,"value":"!foo"} instead,
which the deserialiser already read verbatim and which stringOrJsonSchema
already permitted. Ambiguity is detected by re-parsing the string form rather
than by enumerating prefixes, so every value that round-tripped before is
byte-for-byte unchanged and compound markers ("?!", "!?") are covered too.
Generated Java gets the same treatment, emitting string("!foo", false) rather
than a literal the generated code would re-parse as a negation.

Two DTOs collapsed their matcher to a plain String, dropping the negation flag
entirely. buildObject() recovered it by re-parsing a leading '!', but matchJson
is JSON and never starts with '!', so a negated gRPC bidi rule inverted into its
opposite on any control-plane round-trip — and GrpcBidiRuleMatcher depends on
that flag. Both now carry the full NottableString, and the two schemas point at
stringOrJsonSchema so the object form validates.

Separately, BidirectionalWebSocketFrameHandler never consulted isNot() at all,
so a negated WebSocket text matcher was accepted and then silently ignored; it
is now honoured, as the gRPC equivalent already was.

The committed editor schemas are regenerated from the two core schemas, so VS
Code and JetBrains no longer flag the object form as invalid.

fix(client-node): allow gRPC bidi, forward-validate and forward-with-fallback expectations

The Node client's list of expectation action keys was hand-maintained and had
fallen three entries behind the server. For an unlisted action the client
injected an empty httpResponse alongside the real action, the server counted two
actions with no primary, and the expectation was rejected with "exactly one must
be marked as primary" — so those three actions were uncreatable from Node.

Define the list once and check it against the server's own expectation.json
schema, so a newly-added server action fails the test until Node is taught about
it. Also stop materialising an empty httpResponse when there are no default
headers to add, so a future unlisted action degrades to "default headers not
applied" rather than a hard failure.

Both halves are covered observably rather than through a test seam: the Node
test asserts on the bytes the client actually PUTs, captured off the wire by a
throwaway HTTP listener, with its cases derived from the server schema so a
forgotten key cannot simply skip its own case. ExpectationActionCountTest pins
the server-side consequence against the real parser, so neither test assumes the
other's behaviour.

fix(client-go)!: replace phantom ConnectionDrop with DropConnectionProbability

ServiceChaosProfile sent {"connectionDrop": true} on PUT /mockserver/serviceChaos,
but no such property has ever existed server-side — it came from an incorrect
entry in the OpenAPI specification, since removed. The server ignored it, so
every Go user who set ConnectionDrop got no connection drops at all.

The real property is dropConnectionProbability, and the semantics differ: a
0.0-1.0 probability rather than a boolean. Migrate ConnectionDrop: ptr(true) to
DropConnectionProbability: ptr(1.0). This breaks compilation deliberately —
silently reinterpreting the old field would leave users believing chaos was
configured when it never was.

The expectation-level chaos fixtures could not have caught this: they exercise
the chaos block of an Expectation, a different payload from the service-chaos
control-plane body, so no fixture reaches this struct. Guard it instead by
reflecting over every ServiceChaosProfile JSON tag and checking it against the
server's httpChaosProfile.json schema, so a phantom property cannot be
reintroduced.

Also correct the PHP client's docblock, which documented the same non-existent
key. PHP passes the profile through verbatim, so it never sent the property
itself.

fix(ui): stop dropping closeConnection: false from generated code

The dashboard code generator guarded a non-optional boolean on truthiness, so
closeConnection: false was omitted from the generated snippet in all eight
languages. For SSE and WebSocket the server treats an absent closeConnection as
"close", so unticking the box generated code that closed the connection anyway —
the opposite of what was selected. All six generation sites now emit the actual
value.

The two tests that asserted the field was omitted encoded the old behaviour and
are updated, with the reason recorded inline.

The underlying server-side inconsistency is documented rather than changed: SSE
and WebSocket treat an absent closeConnection as "close" while gRPC streaming
treats it as "don't close", and no schema declares a default. Normalising all
three to "absent = don't close" is the recommendation, but it changes behaviour
for existing users and needs its own change; deferring is safe now that the
generator always emits the value explicitly.

fix(clients): carry dropped action fields and deepen the fixture coverage gate

The fidelity coverage gate compared depth-0 keys only, so no fixture ever probed
a nested field. known-gaps.json read clean not because the clients were complete
but because nothing asked them a hard question — graphqlSubscriptionFilter was
expressible by no client at all, including Java.

Derive the action schemas by globbing and filtering on ACTION_FAMILY_KEYS rather
than naming them in a list beside the check — a hand-maintained list next to the
check that reads it is the same blind spot this gate exists to remove, and
widening it immediately surfaced twelve further unprobed properties and four
one-sided booleans. The gate now requires every property of every action schema
to be exercised, and requires action-level booleans to appear as both true and
false: closeConnection's truthiness bug was masked by an SSE fixture that only
ever used true.

Close the gaps the new probes exposed. Rust was missing templateType, primary
and graphqlSubscriptionFilter across the streaming responses, plus streamError,
and none of those types had the serde(flatten) catch-all the others already had,
so a retrieve-then-resubmit destroyed unmodelled fields. Go and .NET dropped the
primary action selector on httpError/httpForward/httpResponse, which can
silently change which action a re-submitted expectation executes. .NET also
dropped httpError.streamError.

Scope the unrepresentable-expectation sentinel per fixture in both harnesses. A
single global token was excused by one ledger entry, so a second fixture
becoming unparseable would have been silently absorbed and the ratchet would
never have re-armed.

Record the remaining gaps with the reasoning that keeps them decisions rather
than oversights: the additive ones and why they are closeable, and the
NottableString object form, which Go drops and Rust and .NET reject outright
because it needs a union field type the additive-only contract forbids — and
which poisons an entire retrieveActiveExpectations() list, not one expectation.

Relax the Python and Ruby exact fixture counts to lower bounds so growing the
shared corpus no longer fails every client at once.

build(ci): guard that every client pins the same MockServer binary version

Each client decides for itself which server binary its launcher downloads,
through seven different mechanisms, and three had no release-time bump at all:
the Python and PHP launchers sat at 7.1.0 and the Rust crate at 7.3.0 while the
project released 7.4.0. Those clients silently downloaded a three-minor-old
server, and the shared binary cache the documentation promises was never shared.

Correct all three, add them to scripts/release/prepare.sh (which hard-fails if a
pattern stops matching, so a renamed constant breaks the release rather than
being skipped), and add a check that asserts agreement between releases. Include
the .NET csproj Version: the launcher prefers the assembly version and only falls
back to the constant, so checking the fallback alone would have missed the value
that actually ships.

Emit the check unconditionally from generate-pipeline.sh rather than behind a
changed-path filter. The pins it guards live in per-client directories, so a
commit that drifts one routes only to that client's own pipeline and would never
reach a path-filtered gate — the drift vector and the guard would never meet.
Pin it to the trigger queue like every other generated step, so it does not cold
start a large instance to run a second of grep.

Read the expected version from the topmost released changelog heading rather than
from git tags: CI checkouts are frequently shallow or tagless, and a tag-derived
expectation would degrade to "skip" on exactly those builds — a guard that
quietly stops guarding. Deriving it by decrementing the Maven patch is also
wrong, since that breaks on every minor or major bump.

fix(dns): make DNS mock responses RFC 1035 conformant on the wire

No test had ever encoded a single DNS byte. DnsRequestHandlerTest built its
EmbeddedChannel without the DatagramDnsResponseEncoder that MockServer#bindDnsPort
installs, and never called readOutbound(), so every assertion was on an internal
cache rather than on what a resolver receives. That concealed six defects:

- A name embedded in RDATA with a label of 192 octets or more wrote a length octet
  of 0xC0 or greater, which RFC 1035 4.1.4 defines as a compression pointer: the
  resolver reinterpreted the next 14 bits as a message offset and misparsed the
  whole packet. Labels are now checked against the 63-octet limit and names against
  the 255-octet limit. Netty validates label length on a record's own owner name but
  never validates total name length, and names in RDATA bypass its checks entirely,
  so both checks are load-bearing.
- TXT values over 255 octets were truncated rather than split across character
  strings (RFC 1035 3.3.14), silently corrupting DKIM keys and long SPF records and
  potentially cutting mid-UTF-8-sequence.
- An A record configured with an IPv6 value emitted TYPE=A with RDLENGTH=16, and
  the converse for AAAA, violating RFC 1035 3.4.1 and RFC 3596 2.2.
- A record with no explicit name encoded as the root zone, so the client received
  NOERROR with ANCOUNT=1 and no answer for the name it asked about.
- Oversized responses went out with TC clear. A response exceeding the client's UDP
  payload limit is now truncated with TC set (RFC 1035 4.2.1), honouring an EDNS(0)
  advertised buffer size (RFC 6891 6.1.2) before truncating.
- RA was never set and RD never echoed, so systemd-resolved and similar stub
  resolvers treated the mock as offering no recursion and skipped to the next server.

A record that cannot be encoded now returns SERVFAIL instead of being dropped while
still reporting NOERROR. Length validation is separated from length measurement:
encodedNameLength runs outside the encode try/catch during response-size accounting,
so it must never throw, otherwise the client receives no response at all.

Non-ASCII labels were silently replaced with '?' under US-ASCII encoding and are now
emitted as UTF-8 octets with a correct length octet.

Covered by wire-level tests that parse the emitted datagrams with dnsjava, an
independent resolver implementation, rather than with MockServer's own model objects.
Added at test scope only.

fix(http): stop forcing chunked framing on body-less responses with trailers

A response carrying trailers was unconditionally forced to
Transfer-Encoding: chunked with a Trailer announcement header. For a
body-less status (1xx, 204, 205, 304) Netty's HttpObjectEncoder reports
isContentAlwaysEmpty and enters ST_CONTENT_ALWAYS_EMPTY, which emits a
bare empty buffer: the trailing-header block is only written from the
ST_CONTENT_CHUNK branch, so trailers could never reach an HTTP/1.1 wire
for those statuses regardless of what the LastHttpContent carried.

Forcing chunked anyway was actively harmful for 304, because
HttpResponseEncoder.sanitizeHeadersBeforeEncode strips Transfer-Encoding
for 1xx, 204 and 205 but not for 304 (verified against Netty 4.2.16). A
304 with trailers therefore went onto the wire as:

    HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
    transfer-encoding: chunked
    trailer: x-checksum

advertising chunked framing with no terminating 0\r\n\r\n chunk, which
can leave a peer waiting and wedge a keep-alive connection.

Body-less responses are no longer forced to chunked and no longer
announce trailers they cannot deliver; the framing is now byte-identical
to the same status without trailers. Trailers stay attached to the
LastHttpContent so HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, which can carry trailers on a
body-less response via a trailing HEADERS frame, still deliver them.

The existing shouldEmitTrailersForBodylessResponse asserted the old
behaviour and was green only because it inspected in-memory objects and
never encoded. It now asserts the corrected contract, and the new
encoding test pushes responses through a real HttpResponseEncoder and
asserts the bytes on the wire.

Also documents, at the LifeCycle shutdown call site, why disconnect()
genuinely closes a server channel: AbstractChannelHandlerContext
.disconnect() opens with

    if (!channel().metadata().hasDisconnect()) return close(promise);

and NioServerSocketChannel's metadata is ChannelMetadata(false, 16), so
the pipeline translates disconnect into close before reaching the
channel. NioServerSocketChannel.doDisconnect() does throw
UnsupportedOperationException, which makes this look broken when that
class is read alone, but it is unreachable through the public API used
here. Epoll reaches close() by a different route (doDisconnect() ->
doClose()), so there is no platform divergence. This was raised twice as
a suspected shutdown bug and disproved both times; the comment and the
accompanying regression tests exist so it is not raised a third time.
No behaviour change - the LifeCycle diff is comments only.

fix(openapi): gate OpenAPI expectations on TTL, Times and a derivable spec

BREAKING BEHAVIOUR - two changes, both of which can correctly turn a
currently-green suite red.

1. OpenAPI expectations now respect Times and TimeToLive.

HttpRequestsPropertiesMatcher never checked isActive(). Every sibling
matcher does, but this one delegates to a list of per-operation
HttpRequestPropertiesMatcher instances built with update(HttpRequest)
rather than update(Expectation), so each delegate's own expectation
field stays null and its isActive() is trivially true. The TTL and
remaining-match count live only on the outer matcher's expectation, and
nothing else on the serving path consulted them - so an OpenAPI
expectation created with Times.exactly(1) or a one-minute TTL kept being
served for the life of the server. Plain expectations were always gated
correctly and are unaffected.

2. A data-plane OpenAPI expectation with a blank or null spec no longer
matches every request.

When no per-operation matchers could be derived, matches() fell through
to result = true, so one expectation with an empty or mistyped spec
silently hijacked all traffic and served its action for every request,
including requests other expectations were meant to handle. It now
matches nothing.

The match-all fallback is retained for CONTROL-plane matchers, where an
unpopulated matcher is an empty filter and matching everything is the
intended "no restriction" semantic for clear / retrieve / verify. Only
update(RequestDefinition) sets controlPlaneMatcher, so an
expectation-backed matcher never takes that branch - that is the seam
the split is made on.

Two existing tests, shouldHandleBlankStrings and shouldHandleNulls,
asserted the old data-plane match-all behaviour, so this is a deliberate
override of tested behaviour rather than an unnoticed oversight. They
are updated rather than deleted, and each now has a control-plane
counterpart asserting match-all is preserved there, so both halves of
the split are documented where the decision was originally recorded.
